criticAssessment: Coverage is strong for the subsystems the 22 hunters owned: 88 of 160 lib/ modules carry at least one confirmed finding, and the cross-cutters produced good density in runner/scheduler/state, preload reload, collectors, renderers, commands with heavy traffic (test/start/stop/status/spawn), and the DB logger/sync path. However, mapping the 109 findings' file lists against the module inventory shows 72 zero-finding files, and four clusters of them are genuine blind spots rather than trivia. (1) Test2::Harness2::Util::Queue plus the File::JSON/JSONL write side is a live cross-process concurrency primitive (used by Runner.pm, Command/run.pm, Command/stop.pm) with zero findings — every JSONL finding so far was read-side only; lock scope, truncate-via-rename vs. readers holding the old inode, and writer-killed-mid-append were never examined. (2) The fd-pass job-launch round trip (JobLauncher → FdPass command_listen/target_connect/send_fds/recv_fds → StageProcess/StageDelegate/Preload::Host) was only grazed by one SIGPIPE finding; nobody injected a peer crash at each handshake state, and recv_fds croaks in contexts where an uncaught croak kills a whole stage host. (3) yath replay (916-line command driving Log.pm → RenderLoop producers, all zero-finding) and yath reload (whose runner-side HUP handler is already confirmed broken, making the command's success reporting suspect) were never traced end-to-end. (4) RunPlan/Finder/TestFile test-selection — 'which tests run at all' — has zero findings outside one chdir check and legacy-directive parsing; silent test-drop bugs are the highest-impact class a harness can have. These four gap tasks are worth a second pass; the remaining zero-finding files (Options/*, Plugin stubs, Constants, UUID, Term, Units, help/init/projects) are low-logic and honestly covered by the options-plugins and commands hunters.

confirmedFindings.title: Slow subscriber/peer is dropped on EAGAIN (write_frame treats would-block as fatal on the runner's non-blocking sockets), making `yath test`/`yath run` see a false EOF and finalize mid-run
files: lib/Test2/Harness2/Role/Service.pm:294 (forward_frame drops the conn on any write_frame failure), 81/164 (all peer fhs set blocking(0))
lib/Test2/Harness2/Role/Service/Connection.pm:329-334 (_write closes the connection on any write failure)
confirmedFindings.evidence: Every service-side socket is set non-blocking: Role::Service::service_io does `$fh->blocking(0)` on accept, and service_connect_peer does the same on dial. All writes go through Test2::Collector::Util::Socket::write_frame (t2clib/Test2/Collector/Util/Socket.pm:68-77), whose syswrite loop handles ONLY EINTR: `next if $! == EINTR; croak "syswrite to $desc: $!";`. On a non-blocking socket a full kernel buffer returns EAGAIN, so write_frame croaks — possibly after a PARTIAL frame was written. forward_frame (Role/Service.pm:294-297) then deletes the subscriber and _drop_conn's it; Connection::_write (Connection.pm:331-333) closes the whole peer connection the same way. The reader side can genuinely fall behind: Connection::drain does exactly ONE sysread of 65536 bytes per call, and the client's RenderLoop calls Subscriber::poll once per ~20ms tick, capping intake at ~3.2MB/s (less while renderers format), while the runner forwards every transition frame of up to -j16 concurrent chatty tests, and the whole pipe stalls completely if the user's terminal is flow-stopped (Ctrl-S) or the renderer blocks on a slow pipe.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: Run `yath test -j16` on a chatty suite (or simply press Ctrl-S on the terminal for a couple of seconds mid-run). The renderer stops draining, the runner's ~208KB unix-socket buffer to the subscriber fills, the next forward_frame gets EAGAIN, croaks, and the runner silently drops the subscription (comment claims this only catches a 'vanished' subscriber). The command's Subscriber sees EOF, subscription_complete() returns true, the LiveProducer finalizes: the user gets a premature, wrong summary/rollup built from a partial mirror (jobs synthesized as failed/aborted or missing), then the command sits silently in wait_for_runner while the runner keeps running the rest of the suite whose results are discarded. Same mechanism drops a -L DB logger mid-import (silently incomplete import despite the drain_gate design), kills a client connection mid-large-response (client croaks 'runner closed the connection before sending a reply'), and can close a stage's only dispatch channel (stage never redials; remaining tasks requeue with no live stage).
confirmedFindings.proposal: In write_frame, handle EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK on non-blocking handles: either loop with a short select-for-writable (bounded by a deadline) or add per-connection outbound buffering in Role::Service::Connection that is flushed from service_io when the fh becomes writable; only drop a peer after a generous timeout, never on the first would-block. At minimum, distinguish EPIPE/ECONNRESET (peer vanished — drop) from EAGAIN (peer slow — retry).
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Two scenario details are wrong and should be corrected. (1) The "~3.2MB/s intake cap from one 64KB sysread per 20ms tick" is false: RenderLoop::start (RenderLoop.pm:199-208) sleeps IDLE_DELAY only on an idle tick; when frames are flowing it iterates with no sleep, so a healthy client is not throughput-capped that way. (2) Test event output does NOT traverse the subscriber socket — the Driver reads per-job events.jsonl.zst files by path; only state-transition frames and runner-output frames are forwarded (Runner/Role/Service/Handlers.pm:1184-1194) — so sheer chattiness alone is unlikely to overrun an actively-draining client. The realistic triggers are a fully stalled reader: Ctrl-S flow-stop (renderer print to the tty blocks the whole render loop, halting all drains), a SIGSTOP'd/suspended client, a blocked downstream pipe, or a -L DB logger whose drain stalls behind slow DB writes — after which ~208KB of transition frames fills the socket buffer and the next forward_frame EAGAIN-drops the subscription. The partial-write/corruption sub-claim is moot (the connection is closed either way). The premature-finalize consequence on the transient `yath test` path and the silently-incomplete `-L` DB import are accurately traced; the fix proposal (buffer outbound / retry EAGAIN with a deadline, drop only on EPIPE/ECONNRESET or timeout) is sound.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Cheap fixes, in increasing robustness: (1) minimal — in the eval'd write sites, retry EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK with a bounded select-for-writable (e.g. up to 1-5s) before dropping, and only fast-drop on EPIPE/ECONNRESET; a one-line errno check in write_frame plus a select loop covers all callers since everything funnels through it. (2) proper — per-connection outbound buffer in Role::Service::Connection flushed from service_io on writability, dropping a peer only after a generous stall timeout. Also worth setting a larger SO_SNDBUF on subscriber sockets as a stopgap. Note write_frame can also leave a PARTIAL frame on the wire before croaking, so any retry must resume at the same offset (loop already does) rather than resending the frame. No existing TODO_TASKS.md ticket covers EAGAIN-on-write; the only adjacent ticket (line 1857) is about deduplicating the nonblocking-sysread ladder and would not fix this. Fixing it there in passing would be natural since that ticket already touches Connection.pm's byte-pump.

sev_verdict.reason: Trigger is real in supported configurations. Verified in the tree: every service-side fh is set non-blocking (Role/Service.pm service_io accept path and service_connect_peer both call $fh->blocking(0)), write_frame (t2clib/Test2/Collector/Util/Socket.pm:68-81) retries only EINTR and croaks on everything else including EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK, and forward_frame (Role/Service.pm:294-297) plus Connection::_write treat any write failure as 'peer vanished' and drop/close the connection. So a subscriber whose ~208KB unix-socket buffer is full for even one write gets silently unsubscribed; the client's Connection::drain then sees EOF, subscription_complete() fires, and the run finalizes from a partial mirror. drain_gate is no mitigation — add_subscriber just stores the flag and it only defers workdir cleanup (Runner.pm:558-571), providing zero write backpressure, so the -L DB logger genuinely loses events silently. Reachability: requires the reader to stall or fall behind by >~200KB of compressed frames. Real ways this happens: Ctrl-S/flow-stopped terminal, output piped to a paused pager or a slow SSH/CI log sink, or a DB logger whose inserts are slower than event production on a chatty -j16 suite. One overstated detail in the evidence: RenderLoop's 20ms IDLE_DELAY sleep only fires when poll yields nothing (RenderLoop.pm:199-206), so steady-state intake is renderer-speed-bound, not capped at 3.2MB/s — a responsive terminal on a typical suite keeps up, which is why this isn't an every-run failure. Also the post-drop 'sits silently' state is bounded for yath test (runner finishes the suite and exits, wait_for_runner returns), so it is wrong results/data loss, not a permanent hang. Net: user-visible wrong behavior (premature/wrong summary, silently truncated DB import, possible dead stage dispatch channel) plausible in normal use but requiring a slow/stalled reader condition => P1, not P0.

confirmedFindings.title: `yath stop` / `yath kill` busy-wait `sleep(0.02) while kill(0, $pid)` with no timeout and no signal escalation -- hangs forever on a wedged runner or a reused pid, and `yath kill` never actually kills anything
confirmedFindings.evidence: Both commands end with `sleep(0.02) while kill(0, <pid>);` -- unbounded, no deadline, no fallback. Neither command ever sends a real signal to the runner pid: stop sends the socket 'stop' request + end_queue; kill sends end_queue then SUPER::run (abort.pm) which only issues the socket 'truncate' request. Discovery.pm documents the workdir PID file as 'the signal-based-termination fallback when the socket is unresponsive', but no command implements that fallback. Additionally abort's `$self->client->truncate` goes through Runner::Client::_request, which croaks 'Timed out waiting for the runner's reply' after 30s -- so against a wedged runner `yath kill` dies before even reaching its wait loop, leaving the runner untouched.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: The persistent runner wedges (stuck in a preload, or a stage host deadlock) -- exactly the case `yath kill` exists for. The user runs `yath kill`: end_queue is written into the socket buffer, truncate times out after 30s and the command dies with a croak (runner still running); or, if the runner replies but refuses to exit, the command loops on kill(0) forever with no output. Same for `yath stop`. Separately, if the runner crashed earlier and its pid (from the pfile/PID file) was recycled to a long-lived same-user process, both commands spin forever on a pid that will never die.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Bound the wait (e.g. 30s), then escalate using the documented PID-file fallback: kill TERM, wait, kill KILL, and only then clean the workdir/pfile. In `yath kill`, send the signals unconditionally after the graceful attempts -- it is the forceful command. Guard the truncate/_request croak with eval so a wedged socket cannot abort the kill path.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Line precision: the busy-wait loops are exactly kill.pm:46 and stop.pm:72; abort's truncate croak originates at Runner/Client.pm:266-268 (CONNECT_TIMEOUT=30s), and a second un-eval'd croak path exists at Client.pm:227 (socket never accepts) reachable from kill.pm:38's end_queue via _send->connection. In the crashed-runner/recycled-pid case, `yath stop` degrades in two stages: each eval-guarded socket step (stop.pm:60,65) burns up to 30s then warns, after which the unbounded loop at stop.pm:72 spins forever. Also note attach_runner's kill(0) liveness (Runner/Client.pm:202-205,339) always reports a wedged/recycled pid as alive, so the client's runner_gone no-op escape never triggers for exactly the cases these commands target. Proposal stands: bound the wait, then implement the Pfile.pm-documented PID-file signal escalation (TERM, wait, KILL), eval-guard truncate/end_queue in the kill path, and only then remove workdir/pfile.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Cheap fix, mostly reusing existing code: (1) wrap abort's truncate in the project-standard `my $ok = eval { ...; 1 }` pattern so a wedged socket cannot abort the kill path; (2) bound the final wait using the deadline+grace pattern already written in stop.pm's drain_shutdown (30s deadline, 5s post-death grace); (3) on deadline, implement the fallback Discovery.pm/Pfile.pm already document: read the workdir PID file, kill TERM, wait, kill KILL, then clean workdir/pfile. For `yath kill` send the signals unconditionally after the graceful attempt. No existing TODO_TASKS.md ticket covers the command-side escalation — #11 (overlapping terminate/reap/timeout layers) is runner-internal only — so this needs its own task or a rider on #11.

acc_verdict.reason: All claims verified by tracing the code. (1) Both commands end in an unbounded `sleep(0.02) while kill(0, $pid);` (stop.pm:72, kill.pm:46) with no deadline or escalation. (2) Neither command ever sends a real signal to the runner pid: stop sends socket 'stop'+'end_queue' (one-way _send, eval-guarded); kill sends end_queue then abort's truncate; grep of lib/App/Yath2/Command/ shows the only real TERM kills are in start.pm:177 and test.pm:304, both unrelated to the persistent-runner teardown path. (3) The signal-based fallback is documented as intended behavior but unimplemented: Pfile.pm:28-29 says the workdir PID file exists 'for signal-based termination of a wedged runner' and Discovery.pm:90 calls it 'the signal-based-termination fallback when the socket is unresponsive' — no command implements it, so this is not intended-as-is behavior. (4) Runner::Client::_request croaks 'Timed out waiting for the runner's reply' after CONNECT_TIMEOUT=30s (Client.pm:266-268), and connection() croaks after 30s if the socket never accepts (Client.pm:227); in kill.pm neither attach_runner/end_queue (lines 37-38) nor SUPER::run's truncate (via abort.pm:47) is eval-guarded, so against a wedged runner `yath kill` dies before its wait loop, leaving the runner running. The pid-recycle infinite spin scenario also holds: pfile pid recycled to a long-lived same-user process keeps kill(0) true forever.

Worse, `yath kill`'s abort path calls `$self->client->truncate` uneval'd (abort.pm:47), and Runner::Client::_request croaks after 30s (Client.pm:267; an earlier connect croak at :227 fires if the socket never accepts) — so against a wedged runner `yath kill` dies before its wait loop with the runner untouched. Outcome is a broken designed-recovery path: orphaned runner processes plus stale workdir/pfile blocking subsequent runs. That is user-visible wrong behavior plausible in normal persistent-runner operation → P1, not P2; not P0 because the trigger state itself is not a common path.

confirmedFindings.title: Fire-once decision ledger key mismatch: watchdog/connect-timeout mark first-try jobs decided with is_try=undef (key 'id+0') while the collector EOF checks job_try=1 (key 'id+1'), so aborted jobs get re-decided
confirmedFindings.evidence: A task's first attempt has no {is_try} key (State.pm only seeds it in retry_task: `{is_try => 1, %$task}; $task->{is_try}++`). The collector's identity handshake sends `job_try => $self->is_try` where Job::is_try is `$task->{is_try} // 1` -> 1. But Watchdog::_abort_job calls `mark_job_decided($job_id, $task->{is_try})` (undef) and _enforce_collector_connect_timeout uses `my $job_try = $task->{is_try}` (undef). _decided_key stringifies `$job_try // 0`, so the watchdog writes key 'jobid+0' while collector_conn_eof later checks 'jobid+1' -> job_already_decided is FALSE and the EOF decides the job a second time (the collector_current_try stale-try guard also passes since current==entry==1, or was deleted). The comments explicitly rely on this ledger being shared: 'an EOF that arrives after the watchdog already decided this try is a no-op'.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: A run is aborted (owner `yath run` process dies with abort_on_disconnect, `yath abort`/truncate, or transient wind-down abort_remaining). The watchdog announces every first-try running job 'aborted' and marks 'id+0' decided. Each terminated collector then EOFs; collector_conn_eof checks 'id+1', is not blocked, and decide_collector_outcome runs AGAIN -> a second announce_job('aborted') per job (duplicate failed-job entries / double-counted failures in the subscriber's rollup). If a collector was not flagged terminated (send_control failed because the conn was already gone), a flushed failing final_state instead takes the RETRY path and re-queues a job on a run the user just aborted.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Use the same normalization everywhere: `mark_job_decided($job_id, $task->{is_try} // 1)` in Watchdog and `my $job_try = $task->{is_try} // 1` in _enforce_collector_connect_timeout (or make _decided_key default `// 1` to match Job::is_try).
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Real defect, wrong consequences: downgrade to a latent fire-once-ledger contract violation. First-try aborts (watchdog _abort_job, _enforce_collector_connect_timeout) record decided key 'id+0' while the collector EOF checks 'id+1', so decide_collector_outcome runs twice per aborted first-try job; today the second decision is fully absorbed (terminated flag forces the no-verdict branch; Driver ABORTED_RENDERED dedupes the duplicate announce; running_tasks removal blocks retry), but any future subscriber without job_id dedupe would double-count, and t/AI/unit/Runner_abort_terminate.t masks the bug by using 0-based tries. Fix as proposed: normalize with `// 1` in Watchdog.pm:185 and Handlers.pm:721 (or make _decided_key default `// 1` to match Job::is_try), and update the 0-based-try unit tests to 1-based so they exercise the real key.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Fix is a one-line normalization at each writer: mark_job_decided($job_id, $task->{is_try} // 1) in Watchdog.pm:185 and my $job_try = $task->{is_try} // 1 in Handlers.pm:721 (or change _decided_key's default from // 0 to // 1 to match Job::is_try; also note _enforce_collector_connect_timeout stores the undef job_try into terminated_jobs, though its same_try check tolerates undef). Existing ticket TODO_TASKS.md #49 ('Producer emits 1-based try ordinals', Step DB-4) already mandates auditing ALL is_try uses and starting is_try at 1 at the source — seeding is_try => 1 at first dispatch per #49 fixes this in passing; add this ledger-key site to #49's audit list.

acc_verdict.reason: The key mismatch is real and traced end-to-end: first-attempt tasks carry no is_try (State.pm:504-509 only seeds it in retry_task; start_task/queue never add it), the collector identity sends job_try=1 (Job.pm:429 `is_try // 1`, Job.pm:360), and Watchdog.pm:185 / Handlers.pm:721 mark the decided ledger with undef -> _decided_key 'id+0' while collector_conn_eof (Handlers.pm:360) checks 'id+1'. The EOF therefore re-runs decide_collector_outcome, violating the fire-once contract the comments document. However, both claimed user-visible failures are blocked downstream: (1) the duplicate 'aborted' announce cannot double-count failures because the ONLY consumer, Renderer::Driver::_render_aborted, dedupes per job_id (ABORTED_RENDERED `return if $entry->{$job_id}++`) and skips jobs with a verdict, and Monitor folding is idempotent; (2) the phantom-retry leg is impossible because _terminate_collector sets $entry->{terminated} //= 1 unconditionally BEFORE the closed-conn check (so every aborting-run entry takes the terminated -> _collector_no_verdict branch), and even without that, _collector_retry_if_tries requires the task still in running_tasks, which the watchdog's stop_task already removed. Net current impact is one redundant aborted mutation frame plus a redundant eval-guarded stop_task — a latent contract violation, not a P2 double-count/re-queue.
acc_verdict.refinement: Real defect, wrong consequences: downgrade to a latent fire-once-ledger contract violation. First-try aborts (watchdog _abort_job, _enforce_collector_connect_timeout) record decided key 'id+0' while the collector EOF checks 'id+1', so decide_collector_outcome runs twice per aborted first-try job; today the second decision is fully absorbed (terminated flag forces the no-verdict branch; Driver ABORTED_RENDERED dedupes the duplicate announce; running_tasks removal blocks retry), but any future subscriber without job_id dedupe would double-count, and t/AI/unit/Runner_abort_terminate.t masks the bug by using 0-based tries. Trigger paths are real and common (Ctrl-C/crash of the owning yath command with abort_on_disconnect, yath abort, wind-down abort_remaining, --collector-connect-timeout). Impact is bounded, though: since _terminate_collector marks entries terminated, the second decision is a duplicate announce_job('aborted') per job — double-counted failures/duplicate failed-job entries in the rollup of a run the user already aborted. The worse leg (a non-terminated collector flushing a failing final_state and taking the RETRY path, re-queuing a job on an aborted run) needs a narrower race. No hang, no data loss, no happy-path corruption → P2, not P1.
sev_verdict.refinement: Fix is a one-line normalization at each writer: mark_job_decided($job_id, $task->{is_try} // 1) in Watchdog.pm:185 and my $job_try = $task->{is_try} // 1 in Handlers.pm:721 (or change _decided_key's default from // 0 to // 1 to match Job::is_try; also note _enforce_collector_connect_timeout stores the undef job_try into terminated_jobs, though its same_try check tolerates undef). Existing ticket TODO_TASKS.md #49 ('Producer emits 1-based try ordinals', Step DB-4) already mandates auditing ALL is_try uses and starting is_try at 1 at the source — seeding is_try => 1 at first dispatch per #49 fixes this in passing; add this ledger-key site to #49's audit list.

confirmedFindings.title: Persistent runner grows without bound: runner-side Monitor never prunes collectors/jobs/runs and its pending change-lists are never drained; decided_jobs/job_passed/announced_runs ledgers also grow forever
confirmedFindings.evidence: The runner's hub Monitor (Handlers::monitor) accumulates a COLLECTORS entry per collector, a JOBS entry per job, and a RUNS entry per run, with no purge API and no caller that removes entries. Worse, _process pushes every new collector onto PENDING_NEW (and finalizations onto PENDING_FINALIZED, aborts onto PENDING_ABORTED), and the drain methods (new_collectors etc.) are only ever called on SUBSCRIBER-side monitors (Renderer::Driver) - the runner's own monitor's pending arrays grow monotonically. announce_run cleans aborting_runs/terminated_jobs/collector_reap but NOT decided_jobs (one key per job_id+try, Handlers:385), job_passed (Handlers:436, only deleted on a reap that observes it), announced_runs (Handlers:1315), or any Monitor state.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: A `yath start` persistent runner used as a long-lived dev daemon runs thousands of tests per day. Each job permanently retains: a Monitor JOBS + COLLECTORS record (with final_state hashes), a PENDING_NEW/PENDING_FINALIZED array slot, and a decided_jobs key; each run a RUNS record. Over days the runner's RSS climbs steadily (and each new global subscriber's snapshot - which serializes the entire COLLECTORS/JOBS maps - gets slower and larger), eventually degrading dispatch latency or OOM-killing the runner mid-run.
confirmedFindings.proposal: On announce_run (run end), purge that run's collectors/jobs/run record from the runner-side Monitor (retain only while an owner/subscriber needs the snapshot), clear the runner-side pending lists (or don't populate them on the hub), and delete decided_jobs/job_passed/announced_runs entries scoped to the ended run.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Two precision fixes: (1) job_passed is bounded in the common case — it is deleted on BOTH reap paths (Runner.pm:1457 _check_post_pass_health, reached from set_proc_exit for watched no-preload children and from _reaped_unwatched_pid for subreaper-reaped detached preload collectors), so it leaks only for pass-reporting collectors that are never reaped (non-subreaper platforms, the documented accepted-loss case). (2) The leak is broader than the three pending lists named: all seven runner-side lists grow (PENDING_NEW/FAILING/DIAGNOSING/COMPLETED/EXITS/FINALIZED/ABORTED), and RUN_HEALTH is an append-only array too. Also note snapshot($run_id) iterates every historical collector/job key (Monitor.pm:370-382), so even run-scoped subscribe cost grows linearly with lifetime history, not just the global-subscriber snapshot size.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Cheap fix mirroring #35: on announce_run (or in State::purge_run) delete the run's Monitor RUNS entry and its run-scoped collectors/jobs, clear that run's decided_jobs/job_passed/announced_runs keys, and skip populating PENDING_* arrays on the hub-side monitor (subscriber-only feature). Also note run-scoped snapshot() includes collectors/jobs with undef run linkage in every snapshot, so purge must handle those. No open TODO_TASKS.md ticket covers Monitor purging; #12/#35 are DONE and scoped to State.pm only — a new ticket is warranted.

confirmedFindings.title: Watchdog-aborted job whose collector already launched is double-counted: second launch event, TESTS_SEEN+2, and a phantom 'Times Run 2' retry row
confirmedFindings.evidence: _render_aborted (line 348) says "If the launch was never rendered ... render it now" but renders the launch UNconditionally: the only dedup is its own ABORTED_RENDERED ledger, keyed by job_id — it never consults the BY_UUID launched flag or $job->{tries} that _render_launch (line ~320: TESTS_SEEN++, $job->{tries}++) already set for the same job when the collector's launch was rendered. So for an already-launched job it dispatches a second harness_job_start/harness_job_launch, increments TESTS_SEEN again and $job->{tries} again (=2). Base::compute_final then pushes a retried row (`if $tries > 1`) => ['job', 2, file, 'NO'].
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: A test's collector starts (launch rendered, TESTS_SEEN=1) and then the runner watchdog aborts the job (dispatch-failure, halt/bail wind-down, or owner-drop while running). Output shows the file 'started' twice, the final 'File Count' is inflated by one per aborted job, and the summary prints 'The following jobs failed at least once: ... Times Run: 2 ... Succeeded Eventually? NO' for a job that ran exactly once. The formatter status counters also skew (running never returns to 0, todo goes negative).
confirmedFindings.proposal: In _render_aborted, skip the synthetic launch (and the TESTS_SEEN++/tries++) when the job's launch was already rendered — e.g. guard on $job && $job->{tries}, or look up the job's collector uuid in BY_UUID and check {launched}.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: All cited lines are accurate. Two clarifications: (1) the only abort path that CANNOT double-render is Watchdog::abort_job from a failed dispatch (collector never started, so launch was never rendered); the double-count occurs on the abort_remaining paths (run wind-down, yath abort, owner-drop) when the job's collector had already appeared. (2) The per-job `launched => {}` field seeded in Base.pm:147 is vestigial (written nowhere else), so the cleanest fix is the proposal's $job->{tries} guard, or mapping job_id back to the collector uuid's BY_UUID{launched} flag; the guard should skip only the synthetic launch block (lines 364-384 counters + dispatch), still emitting the aborted harness_job_exit/harness_job_end.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Cheap fix as proposed: in _render_aborted, skip the synthetic launch block (and TESTS_SEEN++/$job->{tries}++) when the launch was already rendered — guard on ($job && $job->{tries}) or resolve the job's collector uuid and check $self->{+BY_UUID}{$uuid}{launched}; still emit the aborted harness_job_exit/harness_job_end so the job settles. No TODO_TASKS.md ticket covers this renderer-side dedup directly, but the 'Bail + abort teardown (A4/B3/B4)' item (~line 583) and the harness_runner_job failed/aborted event work (~line 580) touch the same abort-rendering path and could absorb this fix in passing. Worth a regression test: abort a run with one job mid-flight and assert TESTS_SEEN==1 and no retried row in compute_final.

acc_verdict.reason: Confirmed end-to-end. _render_aborted (Driver.pm:348-419) is reachable for a job whose launch was already rendered: Watchdog::abort_remaining (Watchdog.pm:119-159) aborts every still-running task on wind-down/yath-abort/owner-drop, explicitly including jobs whose collectors are live (it terminates them), and such a job has no verdict yet so the line-353 guard passes and the ABORTED_RENDERED ledger (line 362) is fresh. The comment's stated intent proves this is a defect, not design; no renderer test in t/ covers the launched-then-aborted path.

confirmedFindings.title: CTRL-C during `yath test` prints misleading 'No tests were seen!' + dies 'Final data never received from collector!' (exit 255)
confirmedFindings.evidence: render() line 438: `return if $self->signal;` — on a caught signal it returns BEFORE harvesting $loop->final_data/tests_seen/asserts_seen. run() then continues to stop() (which prints "No tests were seen!" at line 487 because TESTS_SEEN was never copied from the loop, even though tests ran and rendered) and then dies at line 155: `my $final_data = $self->{+FINAL_DATA} or die "Final data never received from collector!\n"`. VERIFIED LIVE this session: SIGINT to a mid-run `yath test` produced exactly: 'Caught SIGINT... / Waiting for child processes... / No tests were seen! / Final data never received from collector!' with exit 255. Children were cleaned up correctly.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: User hits CTRL-C on a running `yath test`. Instead of an honest 'interrupted by SIGINT' summary (with the partial results the loop already tallied), they get a false 'No tests were seen!' plus an internal-error-looking die about the collector, and exit 255 rather than a conventional signal exit (e.g. 130). Users reasonably file this as a harness crash.
confirmedFindings.proposal: In run(), when $self->signal is set after stop(), print an explicit 'Run interrupted by SIG<x>' message, harvest whatever the loop already saw for honest partial reporting, skip the final-data die, and exit by re-raising the signal (kill $sig, $$ after restoring DEFAULT) or a documented nonzero code.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Citation lib/App/Yath2/Client.pm:81-96 points at POD; the operative code is handle_signal at Client.pm:242-257. Also note this structure is inherited from yath 1.x's identical render()/run() flow, so it is legacy-parity rather than a 2.0 regression; since child cleanup is correct and the exit is nonzero (just 255 with misleading messages instead of a signal-style exit), P3 may be more apt than P2.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Borderline P2/P1 because the trigger (CTRL-C) is normal use; kept P2 since the run still correctly reports failure and cleans up. Cheap fix: in run(), branch on $self->signal after stop() — print "Run interrupted by SIG<x>", harvest the loop's partial tests_seen/final_data in render() even on signal (move the harvest above the `return if $self->signal`), skip the final-data die, and re-raise the signal after restoring DEFAULT (matches the 1.0 parse_exit signal-death convention already cited in TODO_TASKS.md ~line 874). Note the signal path also silently skips plugin finish() hooks. No existing TODO_TASKS.md ticket covers this; ticket #89 (render_final_data/summary hoist into the Command base) touches the same code and would be a natural place to fold the fix in, and `yath run`/watch (which share or override this flow) should be checked for the same pattern.

acc_verdict.reason: Path traced end to end and confirmed. confirmedFindings.title: `yath spawn` exits 0 when the supervisor dies without reporting an exit status (control EOF is treated as status 0)
files: lib/App/Yath2/Command/spawn.pm:291-305 (bridge_io status loop defaults to 0 on EOF)
confirmedFindings.evidence: bridge_io's wait loop: `my $status = 0; while (1) { my $msg = $ctl->read_message; last if $ctl->closed && !$msg; if ($msg && $msg->{exit_status}) { $status = ...; last; } }` then `return parse_exit($status);` and run() does `exit($exit->{err})`. If the control channel EOFs WITHOUT an exit_status frame — the detached supervisor was SIGKILLed, crashed, OOM-killed, or its Control::_send of the status failed (note read_message_nb leaves the supervisor's fh O_NONBLOCK, so a would-block write in send_exit_status dies and closes without sending) — $status stays 0 and the command exits 0 with no diagnostic, while the script child's real fate is unknown (it may have died or may still be running under the supervisor's group-kill path).
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: A user scripts `yath spawn worker.pl && next-step`. The supervisor process is OOM-killed (it holds the whole preloaded image, a prime OOM target) while worker.pl is mid-run. `yath spawn` immediately exits 0; `next-step` proceeds on the false premise that worker.pl completed successfully.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Treat control EOF without an exit_status frame as a failure: print a 'supervisor vanished before reporting the child's exit' diagnostic and exit non-zero (e.g. 255), mirroring the existing die for a pre-hello EOF.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: The primary scenario (supervisor killed abnormally → false exit 0) is exact as written. The secondary evidence point about read_message_nb leaving the supervisor's fh O_NONBLOCK is real in code (_fill(0) sets O_NONBLOCK and never restores it; _send dies on EAGAIN and closes without sending, Control.pm:210-217, 249-261) but is practically remote for a ~50-byte status frame into an otherwise-empty socket buffer — it would require the command-side receive buffer to be full. Treat it as supporting color, not a second concrete trigger. Proposed fix is sound: mirror the pre-hello EOF die (spawn.pm:286-287) — on closed-without-exit_status, emit a 'supervisor vanished before reporting exit' diagnostic and exit non-zero (e.g. 255).
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Cheap fix mirroring existing style: the pre-hello EOF at line 286 already dies with a diagnostic; make the post-hello loop symmetric — track whether an exit_status frame was ever received, and on EOF without one, warn "spawn supervisor closed the control channel before reporting the child's exit" and exit 255 (parse_exit of a sentinel or direct exit). ~3 lines. No existing TODO_TASKS.md ticket covers this; spawn work (#39/chunk 13) is marked complete, so it needs its own small follow-up. The secondary claim (read_message_nb leaving the supervisor fh O_NONBLOCK so send_exit_status could die on a would-block write) is a lower-probability sub-trigger — control frames are tiny and the peer is blocked reading, so buffer-full is unlikely — but restoring blocking mode before the final status write would be a worthwhile companion hardening.

acc_verdict.reason: Confirmed by direct code trace. lib/App/Yath2/Command/spawn.pm:291-300 initializes $status=0 and exits the wait loop on `$ctl->closed && !$msg`, so a control-channel EOF without an exit_status frame falls through to parse_exit(0) and exit(0) with no diagnostic. No test pins the current default-0 behavior.

confirmedFindings.title: Interactive accept-loop parent reports exit 0 when the yath child dies from a signal, and can hang forever if the child is reaped elsewhere
confirmedFindings.evidence: `my $got = waitpid($pid, POSIX::WNOHANG()); $finish->($? >> 8) if $got == $pid;` — (a) `$? >> 8` discards the signal bits: a child killed by a signal has $? = signo, so $?>>8 == 0 and the wrapper exits 0 (success). (b) waitpid returning -1 (ECHILD, e.g. yath spawned with $SIG{CHLD}='IGNORE' inherited from the parent process, which auto-reaps children) is never handled: `$got == $pid` is never true, so the loop polls select(0.2) forever after the run finishes.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: (a) CI runs `yath test -i ...`; the yath child is OOM-killed (SIGKILL). The interactive parent computes 9 >> 8 == 0 and exits 0 — CI reports the run green although it was killed mid-run. (b) A wrapper that sets SIGCHLD to SIG_IGN execs yath -i; the child is auto-reaped, waitpid returns -1 forever, and the parent never exits — terminal hangs after the tests complete.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Handle signals: `if ($got == $pid) { $finish->(($? & 127) ? 128 + ($? & 127) : ($? >> 8)) }` and also `$finish->(1) if $got == -1;`.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Part (a) is the substantive defect (false-green exit in CI/automation when the yath child is signal-killed, e.g. OOM). Part (b) should be downgraded to a hardening note: it needs $SIG{CHLD}=SIG_IGN inherited across exec — unusual — and -i sessions are attended, so the handled SIGINT/SIGTERM rescue it; it is a hang-until-Ctrl-C, not an unrecoverable deadlock, and the loop sleeps 0.2s per iteration (not a busy spin). Fix as proposed, but guard with `$got != 0` (or `$got < 0 || $got == $pid`) rather than only `-1`, and reuse Test2::Harness2::Util::parse_exit for the sig/err split to match codebase convention.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Cheap fix, worth applying in passing: in _interactive_accept_loop replace `$finish->($? >> 8) if $got == $pid;` with signal-aware forwarding `$finish->(($? & 127) ? 128 + ($? & 127) : ($? >> 8)) if $got == $pid;` and add `$finish->(1) if $got == -1;` to break the ECHILD poll loop. No existing TODO_TASKS.md ticket covers it (Tier 5 #40 interactive is marked DONE), so it needs a small follow-up patch; same $?-decoding audit could also be grepped for elsewhere (`>> 8` on raw $? without checking `$? & 127`).

confirmedFindings.title: DB-logger config temp files are never unlinked (UNLINK => 0 and no consumer-side unlink, despite the comment claiming the logger 'reads and unlinks')
confirmedFindings.evidence: start_loggers creates `File::Temp::tempfile("yath-logger-$$-XXXXXX", TMPDIR => 1, SUFFIX => '.json', UNLINK => 0)` per -L target and passes the path to the fork+exec'd logger. The comment says each logger is 'handed a temp-JSON config file ... it reads and unlinks', but App::Yath2::DB::Logger::run_from_config_file only opens, slurps, and closes it -- `grep unlink lib/App/Yath2/DB/Logger.pm` is empty, and no other code path removes it. If run_cmd/exec fails the parent doesn't remove it either.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: Every `yath test -L<target>` run leaves a yath-logger-<pid>-XXXXXX.json file in the system TMPDIR forever; the file contains the -L target string (a DB DSN, potentially with credentials) persisted world-readable-per-umask in /tmp, and on CI machines running many logged suites /tmp steadily fills with these files.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Either unlink($ARGV[0]) in run_from_config_file after decode (matching the comment), or keep the tempfile object with UNLINK=>1 in the command's CLEANUP_SUBS and remove it in wait_for_loggers/stop.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: The credential-exposure detail is overstated: File::Temp::tempfile creates files mode 0600 regardless of umask, so the persisted -L target/DSN is owner-readable only, not world-readable. The real defect is purely accumulation: one small (~200-byte) yath-logger-<pid>-XXXXXX.json per -L target per `yath test -L` invocation left in TMPDIR forever. Fix as proposed: unlink($path) in run_from_config_file after decode (matching the comment), plus parent-side removal in wait_for_loggers to cover exec-failure cases.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Downgrade the exposure claim: File::Temp guarantees 0600 perms, so 'world-readable-per-umask' is incorrect; the leak is disk clutter, not a credential disclosure. Cheap fix matching the existing comment: add `unlink($path)` in App::Yath2::DB::Logger::run_from_config_file after decode_json, and in start_loggers unlink $cfg_file when run_cmd yields no pid (or track paths and remove them in wait_for_loggers). confirmedFindings.title: `yath watch` exits immediately: done_check tests `-f $self->pfile->path`, but the pfile path is a symlink to a unix SOCKET, so -f is always false (verified empirically)
confirmedFindings.evidence: watch.pm:70 `return 1 unless -f $self->pfile->path;` — Pfile::path returns Discovery->link, the discovery symlink whose target is `$workdir/runner.socket` (Discovery::write_link). -f follows the symlink and tests for a PLAIN file; the target is S_IFSOCK. Verified: `-f` on both the socket and a symlink to it returns 0 while a live listener holds it (-e/-S return 1). So for a perfectly healthy runner the check returns 1 the first time `$producer->idle` is true, which happens as soon as the historical runner-events backlog has been rendered and one tick passes with no new frames. The same constant-false test at stop.pm:75 (`unlink($pfile_path) if -f $pfile_path`) means `yath stop` never removes the symlink itself (masked by the runner's own Scope::Guard cleanup on graceful exit).
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: User runs `yath watch` against an idle (or briefly quiet) persistent runner: it prints the backlog and exits on the first idle tick — behaving exactly like the documented `yath watch STOP` mode — instead of staying attached 'until the runner goes away'. Monitoring a runner between runs is impossible.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Use `-e` (or -S) on the link, or better key on Discovery::resolves / the subscriber connection: the socket EOF (`$sub->closed`) is already checked, so the file test could be `return 1 unless -e $self->pfile->path;`. Fix the same test in stop.pm.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Primary defect is watch.pm:70 only; the stop.pm:75/kill.pm unlink instances are real dead code but harmless (symlink is later cleaned by Discovery::find's stale-link cleanup or the runner's graceful-exit cleanup), so fix them for hygiene, not correctness. Proposed fix is right: use -e (or -l, since the link itself is what should vanish) instead of -f, or key on Discovery::resolves; note -e would still be true for a dangling link until discovery cleans it, so -l plus resolves (or just relying on $sub->closed plus -l) is the most precise stop condition.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Fix is trivial: change -f to -e (or -S) at lib/App/Yath2/Command/watch.pm:70, lib/App/Yath2/Command/stop.pm:75, and lib/App/Yath2/Command/kill.pm:47; or in watch.pm key the exit on App::Yath2::Discovery::resolves (the liveness check that already exists) since done_check already tests $sub->closed for the socket-EOF case. No existing TODO_TASKS.md ticket covers this.

confirmedFindings.title: yath() capture wait loop busy-spins: `sleep 0.02` is integer sleep(0)
confirmedFindings.evidence: Tester.pm imports no Time::HiRes (only `use POSIX;` at line 14). In the capture wait loop: `waitpid($pid, WNOHANG) or do { ... sleep 0.02; next; };` (line 216). Both CORE::sleep and POSIX::sleep truncate the argument to an integer, so this is sleep(0). Verified empirically: `perl -MPOSIX -e 'sleep 0.02'` elapses 0.0001s. Every other loop in the codebase that wants sub-second sleep uses Time::HiRes (e.g. Command/stop.pm line 7 imports it explicitly).
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: Any test that calls App::Yath2::Tester::yath() with capture enabled (the default — essentially every integration test in t/) makes the parent process spin at 100% CPU doing seek+readline+waitpid syscalls with zero delay for the entire lifetime of the spawned yath child (seconds to minutes). Under `prove -j16`/`yath -j16` this burns up to 16 cores on pure polling, slowing the very children being waited on and inflating suite wall time.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Add `use Time::HiRes ();` and call `Time::HiRes::sleep(0.02)` (or import sleep from Time::HiRes) in the wait loop.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Scope note: Tester.pm is test infrastructure only (used by t/ self-tests), not shipped runtime code, and the spin is bounded by the child's lifetime or the 120s YATH_TESTER_TIMEOUT. Impact is suite CPU waste and wall-time inflation under -j16 (parent polling competes with the very children it waits on), not incorrect results — P2 defensible, P3 arguable.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Trivial fix: add `use Time::HiRes ();` and call `Time::HiRes::sleep(0.02)` at line 216 (the only fractional sleep in the file). This matches the project's own recorded convention (memory: "Sub-second sleep pattern — use Time::HiRes::sleep, proactively clean up when seen") and the pattern already used in Command/stop.pm. No existing TODO_TASKS.md ticket covers this specific loop; the nearest is the `_drain_transitions` 50x-spin quick-fix item (~line 497), which a fix here could ride along with. Fixing it should measurably cut CPU load and possibly wall time for parallel integration-suite runs.

confirmedFindings.title: Interactive mode: Ctrl-C makes the pre-fork parent exit immediately and File::Temp CLEANUP deletes the workdir out from under the still-running yath child and runner
files: lib/App/Yath2/Options/Debug.pm:298-313 (fork; parent = accept loop), 352-378 (accept loop: local SIG INT/TERM -> $finish -> exit)
lib/App/Yath2/Options/Workspace.pm:64-68 (workdir tempdir CLEANUP registered in the original pid)
confirmedFindings.evidence: option_post_process ordering is ascending (Workspace runs at 0, _post_process_interactive at 99998, show_opts 'runs last' at 99999), so the workdir tempdir(CLEANUP => 1) is created BEFORE the interactive fork, registering its cleanup in the ORIGINAL pid. _post_process_interactive then forks: the original pid becomes the accept loop and the child continues as the yath command (File::Temp will not clean in the child, $$ mismatch). In _interactive_accept_loop, `local $SIG{INT} = sub { $finish->(1) }` calls exit(1) directly from the handler; exit runs END blocks, and File::Temp's END removes the workdir tree. Additionally $finish forwards only `$? >> 8`, so a child killed by a signal yields parent exit code 0 on the normal path.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: User runs `yath test --interactive t/foo.t` and presses Ctrl-C. SIGINT hits the whole foreground pgroup: the yath child begins its graceful shutdown (forward signal to runner, halt_run, wait for children/loggers), but the accept-loop parent exits instantly and its File::Temp END removes the workdir while the runner and collectors are still writing to it -- the runner detects orphaned() and hard-TERMs, events files vanish mid-write, a -L DB logger records 'workdir vanished ... INCOMPLETE and POSSIBLY CORRUPT', and the shell prompt returns (exit 1) while children are still printing shutdown output over it.
confirmedFindings.proposal: In the accept-loop parent, defuse the inherited File::Temp cleanup (File::Temp::cleanup registration removal or $File::Temp::KEEP_ALL scoping) and/or on INT/TERM just forward the signal to the child and keep waitpid-ing, deleting the workdir only after the child is reaped; also propagate signal deaths (exit 128+sig instead of $? >> 8).

confirmedFindings.title: Spawn supervisor's command-death path sends only TERM with no KILL escalation, then blocks in waitpid forever if the script ignores TERM
confirmedFindings.evidence: On control-channel EOF (the `yath spawn` command died): `kill('-TERM', $child); local $?; waitpid($child, 0); POSIX::_exit(0);`. waitpid has no timeout and there is no SIGKILL escalation (contrast the harness's usual TERM-then-KILL pattern, e.g. Preload::Host::stop lines 444-455). The documented contract (module comment lines 110-112 and POD) is that on command death the supervisor "kills the child's process group" so "no orphan survives".
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: `yath spawn daemon.pl` where daemon.pl installs a SIGTERM handler that defers/ignores shutdown (common for graceful-shutdown daemons). The user closes the terminal / kills the yath spawn command. The supervisor sends TERM to the group and then blocks in waitpid(child, 0) indefinitely: the spawned script keeps running forever holding the dead terminal's passed descriptors (keeping the pty open), and the supervisor process lingers alongside it. The user is left with orphaned processes that the advertised cleanup path was supposed to reap.
confirmedFindings.proposal: After kill('-TERM', ...), poll waitpid with WNOHANG for a grace period (e.g. 5s, matching Host::stop) and escalate to kill('-KILL', $child) before the final blocking waitpid.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Line anchor: the EOF-cleanup branch is lines 175-181 (closed check 175, kill('-TERM') 177, blocking waitpid 179, _exit 180). The contrast file is lib/Test2/Harness2/Preload/Host.pm (Test2::Harness2::Preload::Host, not under Runner/), sub stop lines 438-457 with the TERM/5s/KILL sequence at 443-454. Note the escalation must be kill('-KILL', $child) to the group, since the script may have forked TERM-ignoring descendants too.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Cheap, precedented fix: replace the blocking waitpid at JobLauncher.pm:179 with a WNOHANG poll loop for a grace period (~5s), then kill('-KILL', $child) and final blocking waitpid — exactly the TERM→KILL escalation already used in Preload::Host::stop (lines ~444-455) and referenced as the standard pattern in TODO_TASKS.md line 125 ("the existing TERM→KILL escalation"). No existing TODO_TASKS.md ticket covers this specific spawn-supervisor gap (Tier 5 spawn work #38-40 is marked DONE), so it would need a small new item or a drive-by fix; it is ~10 lines with no design questions.

confirmedFindings.title: Corrupt bytes on any service socket crash the whole service: zstd croak from FrameBuffer->drain is uncaught in Connection::drain
confirmedFindings.evidence: Connection::drain (line 287) does `for my $rec ($self->{+FB}->drain)` with no eval. FrameBuffer::next_frame calls zstd_frame_size/decompress_blob (t2clib/Test2/Collector/Util/Zstd.pm), which `croak "not a zstd frame: bad magic"` for any >=6-byte buffer whose first 4 bytes are not \x28\xB5\x2F\xFD, `croak` on reserved block type, and `croak "Compress::Zstd::decompress failed"` on corrupt content. The connection's documented bad-frame policy (3 strikes, close conn) is implemented only for JSON decode failures inside the eval at line 289; transport-level corruption throws straight through Role::Service::service_io (line 351) into the consumer's loop. Runner.pm's main loop (line ~1229 `while (1) { $self->service_io; ... }`) runs inside the single `eval { $self->run_scheduler_only(); 1 }` in Runner::process, so the exception tears down the entire runner.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: Any local process writes non-zstd bytes to runner.socket (e.g. `printf garbage | nc -U $workdir/runner.socket` — 7 bytes >= 6 with wrong magic), or any peer's stream desyncs mid-frame. The next service_io croaks "not a zstd frame: bad magic"; the persistent runner (or a preload stage host) exits its scheduler loop, tears down preload stages and all in-flight tests, and the whole `yath test` run aborts. One garbage frame from one bad peer kills the service for every connected client instead of closing that one connection.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Wrap the FrameBuffer drain per-connection in an eval inside Connection::drain (or make next_frame return an error record); on a framing/decompress croak apply the existing bad-connection policy: close the connection (it can never resync anyway) and return the events gathered so far, instead of letting the exception escape to the service loop.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Two small refinements: (1) on a zstd framing/decompress croak the connection can never resync (unlike bad-JSON frames, which stay frame-aligned), so the fix should close the connection immediately on first occurrence rather than use the 3-strike counter; (2) the same unprotected FB->drain path also runs for outbound client connections (Connection::drain is shared), so a corrupt frame from a service can likewise crash a client — the fix in Connection::drain covers both.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Cheap fix (a few lines): eval-wrap the $self->{+FB}->drain call in Connection::drain; on croak, close the connection (a desynced framing stream can never resync) and return events gathered so far — consistent with the existing bad-frame policy the team decided to keep (TODO_TASKS.md line 504). No existing ticket covers this; it could ride along with the Connection/Control byte-pump extraction refactor at TODO_TASKS.md line 1863 (shared read_available + idempotent-close role), which touches exactly this drain path.

acc_verdict.reason: Traced the full path and every link holds. Zstd.pm croaks on bad magic for any >=6-byte non-zstd buffer (line 52), on reserved block type (line 115), and on failed decompress (line 36). FrameBuffer::next_frame/drain (t2clib/Test2/Collector/Util/Zstd/FrameBuffer.pm:23-40) do not catch these; Connection::drain (lib/Test2/Harness2/Role/Service/Connection.pm:287) calls FB->drain with no eval — its only eval (line 289) guards decode_json of an already-decompressed payload, so the documented 3-strike bad-frame policy is reachable only for JSON corruption, never for transport corruption. confirmedFindings.title: run_cmd fork-child failure paths use plain die instead of _exit, letting the forked child execute the parent's cleanup (unlink runner.socket, write 'complete', kill the sampler)
confirmedFindings.evidence: _run_cmd_fork's child branch runs `$_->() for @{$params{run_in_child}}`, `chdir($dir) or die`, `open(my $OLD_STDERR, '>&', \*STDERR) or die`, and `@$cmd = map { ref($_) eq 'CODE' ? $_->() : $_ }` — all plain `die` in the forked child (only the _swap_in_io/exec failures use the POSIX::_exit(127) $die). A die here unwinds the PARENT'S copied call stack in the child. For a runner-forked job (IPC->spawn), the exception is caught by Runner::process's eval at line 474 IN THE CHILD, which then performs the runner's full wind-down in the child process: stop_sampler kills the real runner's sampler by pid, _drain_transitions services the inherited (still-open) listen socket and steals connections/frames from the real runner, close_service unlinks runner.socket from the filesystem, and Command::runner::generate_run_sub writes the workdir 'complete' marker — all while the real runner is still running.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: The runner hits EMFILE (fd exhaustion under -j high) or ENOSPC when forking a test job: `open(my $OLD_STDERR, '>&', STDERR)` (or the job's collector-setup coderef) dies in the freshly forked child. The child unwinds into the runner's process() eval, kills the shared sampler, unlinks runner.socket (so every subsequent collector's socket_reporter finds no socket and jobs abort on connect-timeout or lose their transitions), and writes the 'complete' marker prematurely. The user sees a cascade of unrelated job failures/hangs after a single transient fd/disk error.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Wrap the entire post-fork child body of _run_cmd_fork in `my $ok = eval { ...; 1 };` and call POSIX::_exit(127) on any failure (route chdir / cmd-coderef / clone-STDERR failures through the existing $die helper), so a child can never unwind into parent cleanup code.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Correct the mechanism: for runner-forked jobs the child never reaches _run_cmd_fork's chdir / open($OLD_STDERR) / @$cmd map — the job's command coderef is invoked at lib/Test2/Harness2/Util/IPC.pm:121 and normally POSIX::_exits. The actual escape hatch is any die inside that coderef before Test2::Collector's own _exit discipline engages: (a) Test2::Collector::collect construction croaks (e.g. "chdir '...' is not a directory", "stdin '...' does not exist" — ../Test2-Collector/lib/Test2/Collector.pm:148-151); (b) run_collector's pipe+fork spawn outside its eval — `fork // die "fork: $!"` and Atomic::Pipe creation under EMFILE/EAGAIN (Collector.pm:201, Collector/Runner.pm:38-45); (c) set_cloexec's die (Util/IPC.pm:47) and the requires in run_under_collector (Runner/Job.pm:219-303). Consequences as claimed, plus two aggravations: stop_sampler in the child actually TERM/KILLs the real sampler and burns ~5-7s of service_io stealing frames from the shared inherited connections (Runner.pm:1063-1096), and generate_run_sub's 'complete' write is not pid-guarded while the adjacent resources cleanup is (App/Yath2/Command/runner.pm:70-79). Fix: in _run_cmd_fork wrap everything after the fork (including the command-coderef invocation at line 121) in `my $ok = eval { ...; 1 };` and POSIX::_exit(127) on failure, and/or pid-guard the 'complete' write and Runner::process wind-down ($$ != rootpid => POSIX::_exit).
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Cheap fix: hoist the existing $die/POSIX::_exit(127) helper (currently defined at Util/IPC.pm:133, AFTER two of the vulnerable dies) above the run_in_child/chdir block, or wrap the entire post-fork child body in `my $ok = eval { ...; 1 }; POSIX::_exit(127) unless $ok;` per the finding's proposal. TODO_TASKS.md line 503 already plans extracting the shared pre-exec IO-swap code from _run_cmd_fork/_run_cmd_spwn — this hardening can be folded into that refactor in passing. Same defect class also affects other in-runner run_cmd callers (Command::test line 271, plugins), but the Runner::process job-launch path is the worst consequence.

confirmedFindings.title: Collectors terminated via the per-job connect-timeout intent are never hard-killed: _enforce_terminate_grace only enforces run-level aborting_runs intents
confirmedFindings.evidence: _enforce_terminate_grace bails immediately with `my $aborting = $self->{'aborting_runs'} or return; return unless keys %$aborting;` (Handlers.pm:655-656) and, per entry, requires a run-level intent: `my $intent = $aborting->{$entry->{run_id} // ''} or next;` (Handlers.pm:666). But service_identified's per-job late-connect path (Handlers.pm:274-280, fed by _enforce_collector_connect_timeout's terminated_jobs intent) calls _terminate_collector directly WITHOUT creating any aborting_runs entry — the run is deliberately not aborted ("Per-job (NOT run-scoped: the run continues...)", Handlers.pm:733). Such an entry has terminate_sent set but no run intent/deadline, so the per-tick hard-kill fallback documented at Handlers.pm:645-651 ("hard-killing any that do not comply within the grace") can never fire for it.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: --collector-connect-timeout (default 30s) expires for a job (stage was overloaded), the runner fails the job and reclaims its slot; the collector then finally connects and is sent the terminate control. The collector is wedged (blocked writing to a full pipe, stuck in the test child's teardown, or simply not reading its control channel), so it never kills its child and never EOFs. Because no aborting_runs intent exists for its run, _enforce_terminate_grace skips it forever: the orphaned test child keeps running for the rest of the run (and beyond, on a persistent runner), consuming its CPU/DB/port resources and potentially corrupting shared fixtures for the retried/other tests, while its stale entry sits in collector_conns. The user sees stray perl test processes that yath claims it already failed and tore down.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Give the per-job termination its own deadline: stamp a deadline into the terminated_jobs/service_identified path (e.g. store `deadline => time + $self->_terminate_grace` on the entry itself in _terminate_collector) and have _enforce_terminate_grace fall back to the entry-level deadline when there is no run-level intent, removing the early `return unless keys %$aborting` guard.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Strengthen the evidence with _terminate_collector's own comment (Handlers.pm:623-628), which states terminate_sent is stamped "so the per-tick fallback can hard-kill it if it does not comply" — showing the fallback was intended to cover every terminate send, including the per-job path. Also note announce_run's terminated_jobs sweep (1324-1326) only drops intents for collectors that never connected; it does not clean up a connected-but-wedged collector, whose stale entry stays in collector_conns until EOF. The proposed fix (entry-level deadline stamped in _terminate_collector, with _enforce_terminate_grace falling back to it when no run-level intent exists) is sound and also unifies the deadline source for both paths.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Cheap fix as proposed: stamp `deadline => time + $self->_terminate_grace` on the entry in _terminate_collector and have _enforce_terminate_grace use an entry-level deadline fallback (dropping the `return unless keys %$aborting` early-out so the scan runs whenever any entry has terminate_sent). This also hardens the run-abort path against a deleted/missing run intent for free. Nearest-neighbor context: this is the connect-timeout/#33-adjacent per-tick enforcement family; no existing TODO_TASKS.md ticket covers the per-job hard-kill gap specifically, so it would need a small new item or a note folded into any future §5.4 watchdog work.

confirmedFindings.title: stop_sampler cannot see a sampler already reaped by the subreaper sweep: 5s+2s shutdown stall and TERM/KILL sent to a possibly-reused pid (PRELOAD_ROOT has a guard, SAMPLER does not)
confirmedFindings.evidence: The runner's per-tick `waitpid(-1, WNOHANG)` sweep (_bring_out_yer_dead) reaps EVERY child. It special-cases PRELOAD_ROOT_PID (deletes it and sets PRELOAD_ROOT_REAPED so stop_preload_root returns early), but has no equivalent for SAMPLER_PID: a sampler collector that dies mid-run is reaped as an 'unwatched pid' and forgotten while `$self->{+SAMPLER_PID}` stays set. stop_sampler then loops 250x `waitpid($pid, WNOHANG)` (which returns -1/ECHILD, never == $pid) sleeping 0.02s = a guaranteed 5s stall, then `if (kill(0, $pid))` -- a classic check-then-act on a pid that is no longer ours: if the OS reused it for another same-user process, the runner sends it TERM, waits 2 more seconds, then SIGKILLs it (`kill('KILL', $pid); waitpid($pid, 0)`).
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: The sampler process crashes during a run (SystemLoad read error, OOM kill, etc.); the tick sweep reaps it. At shutdown every `yath test`/runner exit stalls 5 seconds in stop_sampler for no reason. On a busy machine where the pid has been recycled to an unrelated same-user process (e.g. one of the user's other test children), stop_sampler TERMs and then KILLs that innocent process.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Mirror the preload-root guard: in _bring_out_yer_dead, if the reaped pid == SAMPLER_PID, delete SAMPLER_PID (and skip); stop_sampler already no-ops when the pid field is gone. Same pattern review applies to AUX_PIDS in stop_aux.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Two precision corrections. (1) The AUX_PIDS analogy is only partial: stop_aux (682-703) self-heals the stall because line 690's `kill(0,$_)` grep drops an already-reaped unrecycled pid on the first pass — but the pid-reuse hazard does apply (line 687 TERMs, 695-697 KILL, any recycled pid). (2) The trailing `waitpid($pid, 0)` at 1089 does not hang on a recycled non-child pid (returns -1/ECHILD immediately); the harm from pid reuse is the TERM/KILL signals plus the extra 2s wait, not a blocking reap. Trigger requires the sampler to actually die mid-run (crash/OOM — its ChildMonitor watches the runner, so it never self-exits while the runner lives), after which the 5s stall is deterministic on every shutdown of that runner; the wrong-process kill additionally requires a full pid-space wrap during the run, so it is rare.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Fix is the proposed one-liner: in _bring_out_yer_dead (Runner.pm:1493-1497 area), add a SAMPLER_PID guard mirroring the PRELOAD_ROOT_PID one — delete $self->{+SAMPLER_PID} and next when the swept pid matches; stop_sampler already no-ops via `or return` at line 1066. Apply the same pattern to AUX_PIDS in stop_aux (Runner.pm:682-703). No existing TODO_TASKS.md ticket covers this; the sampler ticket (~lines 983-1027) claims "reap-at-stop handled (Runner::stop_sampler)" and should be annotated. Secondary hardening: replace the unconditional kill('KILL') fallback with an ECHILD check after the first waitpid loop to eliminate the recycled-pid kill even if the guard is missed.

confirmedFindings.title: Every `yath test --hide-runner-output` run stalls a fixed 5 seconds at finalize: runner_output_done can never become true because the reader is gated off
confirmedFindings.evidence: LiveProducer::_drain_runner_output loops `until ($engine->runner_output_done)` with sleep 0.02, bounded only by DRAIN_RUNNER_OUTPUT_TIMEOUT (5s). Renderer::Base::step_runner_output starts with `return unless $self->{+SHOW_RUNNER_OUTPUT};`, so with --hide-runner-output the SERVICE_READERS entry for runner-events.jsonl.zst is never created, and runner_output_done returns 0 forever (`my $reader = $self->{+SERVICE_READERS}{$rfile} or return 0;`). The loop's condition is therefore unsatisfiable and always burns the full 5s budget.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: User runs `yath test --hide-runner-output t/`. The run finishes, the runner closes its socket, the render loop reaches finalize -> _drain_runner_output; the until-loop polls ~250 times over exactly 5 seconds before the timeout fires. Every such invocation (including CI runs) pays a guaranteed 5-second dead wait between the last test output and the summary, looking like a hang on short suites.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Short-circuit _drain_runner_output when the engine is not showing runner output (e.g. expose show_runner_output on the engine and `return unless $engine->show_runner_output`, or have runner_output_done return 1 when SHOW_RUNNER_OUTPUT is false).
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Scope precisely: the stall hits `yath test --hide-runner-output` (transient runner, sub closed at finalize) and also the sub-undef fallback path (runner never bound its socket); the persistent `yath run` path is unaffected because the open socket triggers the early return at LiveProducer.pm:301. It is a bounded fixed 5s delay, not an indefinite hang. Cleanest fix is in Base::runner_output_done: return 1 when !$self->{+SHOW_RUNNER_OUTPUT} (there is nothing to drain when the reader is intentionally gated off), which fixes all callers without teaching the producer about display options.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Cheap one-line fix: add `return 1 unless $self->{+SHOW_RUNNER_OUTPUT};` at the top of runner_output_done in lib/Test2/Harness2/Renderer/Base.pm (when output is hidden there is by design nothing to drain, so "done" is trivially true); this fixes both LiveProducer and any other caller keying on the predicate. Related ticket: TODO_TASKS.md #65 already flags the show_runner_output derivation being copy-pasted across test.pm/watch.pm/stop.pm and general Driver/Base renderer duplication -- this fix could land in passing there, though #65 does not currently mention the drain stall itself (worth adding a line to it).

acc_verdict.reason: Confirmed by full code trace. With --hide-runner-output, test.pm driver() passes show_runner_output=0 and workdir to the Driver engine (Base subclass, no overrides). Base::step_runner_output returns immediately at line 337, and Base.pm:345 is the ONLY place the runner-events RunnerReader is ever created, so SERVICE_READERS never gets the runner-events.jsonl.zst entry. At finalize (RenderLoop.pm:230 -> LiveProducer::finalize -> _drain_runner_output), the transient run's subscriber is closed (that is what ended the loop), so the line-301 early return does not fire; runner_output_done (Base.pm:399-406) has WORKDIR set so it skips the return-1 path and hits `or return 0` on the missing reader forever. The until-loop body (poll on EOF'd socket + gated no-op step + sleep 0.02) cannot create the reader, so every such run burns the full 5s DRAIN_RUNNER_OUTPUT_TIMEOUT. The comment at Base.pm:395-398 shows the reader-missing->0 fallback was designed for a runner that never produced an events file, not for the display option, so this is unintended.

confirmedFindings.title: yath resources loops forever showing a blank screen after the runner goes away (unreachable return)
confirmedFindings.evidence: run() probes once up front and dies if no runner, but inside `while (1)` (lines 58-76) the per-tick result is `$self->runner_resources // []` — runner_resources returns undef when the pfile is gone or kill(0,$pid) fails (lines 37-40), and that undef is silently coerced to an empty list. There is no loop exit condition; `return 0` at line 78 is unreachable.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: User runs `yath resources` while a persistent runner is up, then the runner is stopped (yath stop in another terminal) or crashes. The command clears the screen every 0.2s and prints only '==== Resource state ====' forever, with no indication the runner is gone; the user must Ctrl-C. The pre-loop probe explicitly exists to avoid 'spinning forever on an empty screen', but the in-loop undef case recreates exactly that.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Distinguish undef (runner gone) from an empty list inside the loop: `my $resources = $self->runner_resources; last unless defined $resources;` then print a 'Runner has gone away' message and return 0.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Minor precision: the finding cites runner_resources' undef returns at "lines 37-40", which is exact; note additionally that Pfile->find itself never signals staleness (it deletes the no_fatal/no_warn/no_checks params, Pfile.pm:105), so the pfile_params(no_fatal=>1) override in resources.pm:27 is vestigial — all dead-runner detection collapses into the undef return that the loop discards. Proposed fix (last unless defined, print "runner has gone away", return 0) is correct as written.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Already tracked: TODO_TASKS.md #91 (Persist-family command cleanups, step 3) plans exactly this fix — attach once before the loop, per-tick eval { $self->client->resources } with a runner-gone exit modeled on ping.pm:71-75 plus SIGINT/SIGTERM flag, making return 0 reachable. #91 is in the DO-FIRST safe-to-land list and must be coordinated with #95 (Pfile->Discovery migration touches the same discovery code in resources.pm). Cheapest standalone mitigation matching the finding's proposal: 'my $r = $self->runner_resources; unless (defined $r) { print "Runner has gone away\n"; return 0; }' inside the loop.

acc_verdict.reason: Confirmed by tracing the code. In lib/App/Yath2/Command/resources.pm, run() dies on a failed probe only before the loop (lines 53-56); inside `while (1)` line 59 does `$self->runner_resources // []`, coercing undef to an empty list. runner_resources (lines 34-46) returns undef once the runner is gone: App::Yath2::Pfile->find delegates to Discovery->find which "returns nothing for a dead runner (and cleans the stale symlink)" (Pfile.pm:102-107), and even with a lingering symlink kill(0,$pid) at line 40 fails. The undef path short-circuits before any client/socket call, so no exception can break the loop either. With an empty list the loop clears the screen and prints only the header every 0.2s; there is no exit condition and `return 0` (line 78) is unreachable, so the user sees an eternal blank screen and must Ctrl-C — exactly the state the pre-loop probe comment (lines 50-52) says the code was written to avoid. Not a CPU spin (sleep 0.2 per tick), but the finding claims a UX hang, not a spin.
acc_verdict.refinement: Minor precision: the finding cites runner_resources' undef returns at "lines 37-40", which is exact; note additionally that Pfile->find itself never signals staleness (it deletes the no_fatal/no_warn/no_checks params, Pfile.pm:105), so the pfile_params(no_fatal=>1) override in resources.pm:27 is vestigial — all dead-runner detection collapses into the undef return that the loop discards. confirmedFindings.title: _project_name returns the workdir's PARENT directory ('tmp' for the default workdir), so every run is attributed to project 'tmp'
confirmedFindings.evidence: The comment says 'best-effort from the workdir basename', but the code takes File::Spec->splitpath(...)[1] — the DIRECTORY portion, not [2] the basename. For the default workdir tempdir('yath-$$-XXXXXX', DIR => $tmp) (Options/Workspace.pm line 131-146), rel2abs gives /tmp/yath-<pid>-XXXXXX, splitpath[1] is '/tmp/', and parts[-1] is 'tmp'.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: Every `yath test -L db.sqlite` on any machine/project creates/reuses a single projects row named 'tmp' (or the tmp dir's basename); all runs and test_files from unrelated projects collapse into one project in the DB, and the user's --project setting is ignored entirely.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Use the settings' yath project when available (pass it through the logger config), falling back to the ORIGINAL cwd basename — not the workdir path; at minimum fix [1] -> [2] to match the stated intent.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Two corrections to the finding: (1) with a user-supplied --workdir the parent-dir accident can coincidentally yield a plausible name (e.g. workdir inside the project tree), so the collapse-to-'tmp' is specific to the default tempdir workdir; (2) the proposal's minimal fix ([1] -> [2]) would be WORSE for default workdirs — the basename is the random 'yath-<pid>-XXXXXX', minting a new projects row per run. The correct fix is the finding's primary proposal: pass settings->yath->project (or original-cwd basename) through the logger config file written in Command/test.pm start_loggers.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Two-line fix available now: in _ensure_run_row use the settings project (thread settings->yath->project through the logger config written by Command/test.pm:228-267) and fall back to the ORIGINAL launch cwd's basename — the workdir is a throwaway tempdir and even the intended splitpath()[2] would yield a useless unique 'yath-$$-XXXXXX' per run (a different bug: one project row per run). Note the code's own comment (Logger.pm:268-269) already flags attribution as provisional pending the webapp/DB spec; no existing TODO_TASKS.md ticket covers passing --project to the logger, but the DB-layer rewrite tickets (~lines 1124-1402, projects natural-key work) are the natural place to fold this in — worth adding explicitly so it isn't lost. Persistent-runner docs (PreCommand.pm:85: project 'is necessary for a persistent runner') make --project a normal, already-set knob for daemon users, strengthening the case it should win over any heuristic.

confirmedFindings.title: Jsonl renderer lastlog symlink: dangling symlink never removed (-f follows the link) and symlink() failure is invisible because eval{...;1} ignores its return value
confirmedFindings.evidence: Line 77 `next unless -f $name;` — `-f` follows symlinks, so a DANGLING ./lastlog.jsonl (its old target deleted) is skipped and never unlinked. Line 85 `if (eval { symlink($file, $name); 1 })` — symlink() failing (returning 0, e.g. EEXIST) does not die, so the eval still returns 1, LAST_LOG is set, and finish() later prints " (Symlinked to: ./lastlog.jsonl)". Contrast Options/Logger.pm _maybe_lastlog which correctly checks `-l $link || -e $link`. Also the failure branch warns with $@ (empty) instead of $!.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: A user logs a run to a file, later deletes/rotates that log (lastlog.jsonl now dangles), then runs `yath test -L...jsonl` again in the same directory. The dangling symlink survives the -f check, symlink() fails with EEXIST but is treated as success, and the run ends printing 'Wrote log file: <new file>' plus '(Symlinked to: ./lastlog.jsonl)' — but lastlog.jsonl still points at the deleted old path. Following the advertised symlink gives ENOENT (or, if the old path was recreated, the WRONG run's log).
confirmedFindings.proposal: Test `next unless -l $name || -e $name;` for the stale-link sweep, and check symlink()'s return value (`if (symlink($file, $name)) {...} else { warn "...: $!" }`) instead of eval{...;1}.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Only refinement: the eval around symlink() is presumably there for platforms where symlink() dies as unimplemented, so the fix should keep the eval but check the return value, e.g. `if (eval { symlink($file, $name) }) {...} else { warn "Could not symlink the log file to '$name': " . ($@ || $!) }`, plus `next unless -l $name || -e $name;` (or just `unlink($name) if -l $name || -e $name;`) for the sweep at line 77, matching Options/Logger.pm line 240. Impact is limited to a stale/misleading lastlog symlink and false '(Symlinked to:)' message; the real log file is unaffected.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Trivial fix, exactly as proposed and already precedented in-tree: mirror Options/Logger.pm's _maybe_lastlog, i.e. sweep with `next unless -l $name || -e $name;` and replace the eval with a direct return-value check `if (symlink($file, $name)) {...} else { warn "Could not symlink the log file to '$name': $!" }` (also fixes the wrong error variable — the current warn prints $@, which is empty since symlink() doesn't die). No existing TODO_TASKS.md ticket covers this (the lastlog mentions at lines 1241/1328 are feature-spec references, not bug tickets), but any task touching the Jsonl renderer's lastlog handling could fold this in; consider unifying with the Options/Logger.pm helper so there is one correct implementation.

acc_verdict.reason: Confirmed by code trace and empirical test. Line 77 `next unless -f $name;` skips dangling symlinks (-f follows the link and stats the missing target, returning false), so a stale ./lastlog.jsonl is never removed. Line 85 `eval { symlink($file, $name); 1 }` treats symlink()'s 0-return (EEXIST from the surviving dangling link) as success because the eval block still returns 1; LAST_LOG is set and finish() (line 127) prints '(Symlinked to: ./lastlog.jsonl)' while readlink still shows the old deleted target.
