confirmedFindings.title: Reloader stat-throttle never engages: STAT_LAST_CHECKED assigned to a dead lexical copy
confirmedFindings.evidence: _get_changes: 'my $last_checked = $self->{+STAT_LAST_CHECKED}; return if $last_checked && $gap && ...; $last_checked = $check_time;' — the final assignment updates only the lexical; $self->{+STAT_LAST_CHECKED} is never written anywhere (only deleted in reset()), so it stays undef forever and the 'Do not hammer the disk' guard ('return if $last_checked && ...') can never trigger. Preloader constructs the Reloader with stat_min_gap => 2, which is therefore dead.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: On any system without Linux::Inotify2 (macOS/BSD, or Linux without the module), every Preloader::check tick (once per second per stage process) stat()s every single watched file — for a large preload set that is thousands of stat calls per second per stage instead of the intended once-per-2s, and the stat_min_gap knob silently does nothing.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Write it back: $self->{+STAT_LAST_CHECKED} = $check_time;
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Impact is smaller than the scenario implies: the only caller of reload_changes() is Preloader::check (Preloader.pm:652), which has its own 1-second throttle (Preloader.pm:646-647). Actual effect is one stat() pass over the full watch set every ~1s instead of the intended ~2s — a 2x amplification, not unbounded hammering. Bug and fix are otherwise exactly as stated.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Fix is the proposed one-liner: replace '$last_checked = $check_time;' with '$self->{+STAT_LAST_CHECKED} = $check_time;' at Reloader.pm:158. Note the outer Preloader::check 1s gate makes the inner 2s gap only reduce every-other sweep; if the intent is to honor stat_min_gap fully, the fix is still correct as written. No existing TODO_TASKS.md ticket covers the Reloader stat path (reload tickets there are about preload-root/stage lifecycle), but any future chunk touching Preloader reload (#11/§4.7a preload resource work) could absorb this fix in passing. Also worth noting for that pass: on the stat fallback path, a deleted watched file makes _get_file_times return [undef, undef] and line 168's '==' comparison warns; harmless but noisy.

confirmedFindings.title: Discovery symlink is published before runner.socket exists and cleaned by path without identity check -- concurrent discovery deletes the live link and orphan-kills the new runner
confirmedFindings.evidence: start.pm run(): `start_runner(persist => $link, ...)` forks the runner, then IMMEDIATELY `App::Yath2::Discovery->publish($settings, workdir => $dir)` (line 160) creates the symlink -> $dir/runner.socket. The runner child only binds runner.socket later, inside Runner::process() after perl startup/module loading (start_service, Runner.pm ~line 454). Discovery::find() (lines 149-163) does `return $self if $self->resolves; $self->clean unless $no_clean;` where resolves() returns 0 when `-S $target` is false (socket not yet created), and clean() unconditionally `unlink($link)` with no check that the link is the same one it probed (readlink-then-unlink TOCTOU, and no dead-vs-not-yet-alive distinction). write_link() is also non-atomic (unlink + symlink, lines 386-391) rather than symlink-to-temp + rename. Finally Runner::orphaned() returns true when `!-e $pfile` (PERSIST == the link path), setting SIGNAL=TERM and shutting the runner down.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: User runs `yath start` while any discovery-using command runs concurrently (a `yath status`/`run`/`which` in another terminal, a cron, or a second start). start publishes the link at T0; the runner needs ~0.5-2s to load modules and bind runner.socket. In that window the other command's Discovery->find() readlinks the link, sees the target is not (yet) a socket, declares the runner dead, and unlinks the fresh symlink. When the runner finishes booting, its main loop sees `!-e $pfile` -> orphaned() -> SIGNAL=TERM and the just-started persistent runner silently shuts itself down; the user sees 'Persistent runner started!' followed by every subsequent `yath run` failing with 'no persistent harness found'. The same unlink-by-path race lets find() delete a link a new runner just published over a crashed runner's stale path.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Do not treat 'target is not a socket yet' identically to dead: only clean when the target exists and connect fails with ECONNREFUSED (probe() already distinguishes; find()/resolves() do not), and/or have publish happen in the runner itself after start_service binds the socket. Make write_link atomic (symlink to temp name + rename over). In clean()/clean_if_owned(), re-readlink and only unlink if the target still matches the probed target.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Two corrections. (1) The orphaned()->SIGNAL=TERM self-kill only executes on the NO-PRELOAD path: the loop check is gated `unless ($self->_preload_root_hosts_stages)` (Runner.pm:1267) and orphaned() is called nowhere else. For the typical preloading persistent runner the symptom differs: the runner is NOT killed — it survives as a permanently undiscoverable, leaked daemon (the link is never republished), and every subsequent `yath run` fails with 'no persistent harness found'. Both symptoms share the same trigger; the finding's failure text should cover both. (2) The sequential `yath start && yath run` workflow usually escapes the race: the runner writes its PID file (Runner.pm:439) microseconds before binding the socket (454), so by the time start's wait_for_runner_pid returns and a follow-up command finishes its own perl startup, the socket is bound. The realistic trigger is a genuinely concurrent discovery command (second terminal, cron, CI parallelism) landing inside the runner's boot window — hence P2, not P1.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Cheapest robust fix: move publish into the runner itself right after start_service binds runner.socket (start.pm already waits on the workdir PID file via wait_for_runner_pid and could instead/also wait for `-S $dir/runner.socket` or for the link to resolve). Alternatively, make find()/clean() distinguish 'not yet a socket' from 'dead': only unlink when the link target's workdir is gone or connect fails ECONNREFUSED on an existing socket (probe() already classifies states that resolves() collapses); and re-readlink-and-compare before unlink to close the TOCTOU. write_link should be symlink-to-temp + rename for atomicity. No existing TODO_TASKS.md ticket covers this race, but #95 (Pfile removal) and #62 (REF-PORT Discovery->list/ping rework) both churn exactly these files (Discovery.pm, Pfile.pm, ping/which call sites) and are sequenced soon -- folding the liveness-vs-not-yet-alive distinction and atomic write_link into #62/#95 would fix it in passing.

confirmedFindings.title: Detached spawn supervisor never closes inherited stage-host fds (listen socket, runner channel, collector stdout/stderr pipes)
confirmedFindings.evidence: Preload::Host::request_handler_spawn double-forks a detached, setsid'd supervisor from the preload stage while every service fd is open; the comment at Host.pm:356 says 'The detached supervisor: drop the host's inherited service sockets so it holds no dup of any peer connection (ARCHITECTURE.md 5.4), then run the supervisor body' -- but neither that call site nor JobLauncher::launch_spawn ever calls $runner->stop()/close_all_connections in the supervisor. launch_spawn only closes the SCM_RIGHTS-received terminal fds ($class->_close_fds(@fds), line 159). Only the script CHILD cleans up (_run_spawn_child, lines 217-218). FD_CLOEXEC set in Role::Service::start_service cannot help: there is no exec on this path. The supervisor therefore holds, for the entire lifetime of the spawned script (which by design 'survives runner/stage teardown'): the stage's preload-<stage>.socket listen fd, the stage's registered connection to runner.socket, the yath-spawn command's service connection, and -- because the stage runs under a collector (Preloader::launch_stage) -- the stage collector's captured STDOUT/STDERR pipe write ends on fds 1/2.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: User runs `yath start -PFoo`, then `yath spawn long_running_script.pl` (e.g. a REPL or dev server), then `yath stop` (or the stage reloads on a file change). The stage process exits, but the runner never sees EOF on that stage's runner.socket channel (the supervisor holds a dup of the client end), so the stage is never dropped from service_peers/service_conns; the stage's collector never sees EOF on its capture pipes (supervisor holds fds 1/2) and stalls at its orphan timeout instead of finalizing -- `yath stop`/reload wedges for the orphan-timeout window or until the spawned script exits. Exactly the EOF-defeat failure ARCHITECTURE.md 5.4 calls a hard prerequisite to prevent, and the code's own comment claims it is prevented here.
confirmedFindings.proposal: In JobLauncher::launch_spawn, before dialing back to the command (or immediately after the fork that created the supervisor in Host.pm), run the same sweep _run_spawn_child does: $runner->stop(); $runner->close_all_connections; and reopen STDIN/STDOUT/STDERR onto /dev/null (the supervisor's diagnostics can go to its own detached stderr) so the stage collector's pipes are released.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Real defect, wrong consequences and severity. The detached spawn supervisor (Host.pm:359 -> JobLauncher::launch_spawn) does leak every inherited stage-host fd (preload-<stage>.socket listen fd, the stage's registered runner.socket connection, the yath-spawn client connection, and the stage collector's capture pipes on fds 1/2) for the entire lifetime of the spawned script, directly contradicting the comment at Host.pm:356-358 and the §5.4 sweep every other no-exec fork path performs (_run_collected_child:338, _run_spawn_child:217-218, cleanup_process:395-397). But no wedge results: the stage collector is is_test=>0 and finalizes on reap without waiting for pipe EOF/orphan timeout (t2clib/Test2/Collector.pm:498-519), and runner teardown/reload is message+waitpid driven with stale-peer-safe re-registration (Role/Service.pm:371, 409-410). Actual impact is soft: the runner keeps a dead stage connection in its select set until the spawned script exits (writes to it during the reload window are silently discarded into an unread buffer instead of failing), plus stray held fds. The proposed fix is still correct and cheap: in the supervisor (before or at the top of launch_spawn) call $runner->stop() + $runner->close_all_connections and reopen 0/1/2 onto /dev/null, making the code match its own comment. Severity P3 (hygiene/latent hazard), not P1.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Cheap fix, exactly as proposed: at the top of launch_spawn (before target_connect at line 128), run the same sweep as _run_spawn_child — $runner->stop(); $runner->close_all_connections if $runner->can('close_all_connections'); — and reopen fds 0/1/2 onto /dev/null so the stage collector's capture pipes are released (the supervisor's warn diagnostics are already detached and expendable). This also makes the Host.pm:356 comment true instead of misleading. No existing TODO_TASKS.md ticket covers it (TIER 5 spawn group is marked DONE; the orphan-timeout item near TODO_TASKS.md:1029 is a different, already-fixed collector stall), so a new ticket or direct patch is warranted. A regression test can assert via /proc/<supervisor-pid>/fd that no stage socket/pipe fds survive in the supervisor after spawn handshake.

confirmedFindings.title: HUP reload is always silently dropped: _preload_root_stage_identity compares stage peer_pid to the wrong pid
confirmedFindings.evidence: spawn_preload_root stores PRELOAD_ROOT_PID = Test2::Collector::spawn_collector(...) return value. spawn_collector (t2clib/Test2/Collector.pm:93) does `my $pid = fork; return $pid if $pid` and the forked COLLECTOR PARENT then fork+execs the actual preload-root perl (Collector/Runner.pm:45,138) — so PRELOAD_ROOT_PID is the collector parent, and the preload-root perl process is its child with a DIFFERENT pid. Every service connection announces `pid => $$` of the dialing process (Role/Service/Connection.pm:220), so the base/default stage peer (hosted in the preload-root perl) announces the child pid. _preload_root_stage_identity (Runner.pm:771) requires `$pid == $root_pid`, which can never be true, so it always returns undef and the HUP handler (Runner.pm:204) does `or return`. No other code writes preload_root_pid (grep confirms). The unit test t/AI/unit/Runner_reload_routing.t passes only because it fabricates FakeConn peers whose pid is set equal to preload_root_pid, baking in the same false assumption.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: User runs a persistent preloaded runner (`yath start` with -P preloads), edits a preloaded module, and sends SIGHUP (`yath reload` / kill -HUP <runner-pid>). The handler looks up the base-stage peer by pid, never matches, and returns without sending 'reload_root'. Nothing is reloaded, no warning or event is emitted; the user keeps running stale code and has no indication why.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Match the base stage against the pid the 'preload-root' handshake peer announced (service_peers->{'preload-root'}->peer_pid) instead of PRELOAD_ROOT_PID, or record the exec'd child's pid during the handshake and compare against that. Fix the unit test to model the real two-process (collector parent vs exec'd child) pid split.

confirmedFindings.title: task_stage re-resolution divergence between queue-time bucket and start-time lookup crashes the runner ("Task ... was not pending")
confirmedFindings.evidence: _queue_task buckets a task in PENDING_TASKS using task_fields->task_stage evaluated at queue time. task_stage for a multi-entry preload_list returns 'the FIRST listed stage that is currently up' (State.pm:866-868), so the result changes as stage lifecycles change. _next traverses the task at its physical bucket location and returns that bucket's stage, but _start_task re-calls task_fields($task) (State.pm:408) and uses the FRESH resolution to locate the pending bucket (line 410). If a higher-preference stage came 'up' between queueing and dispatch, the fresh resolution names a different bucket: $set is undef ("Can't use an undefined value as an ARRAY reference") or lacks the job (`die "Task $job_id was not pending"`, line 413). scheduler_tick deliberately has no eval (Role/Scheduler.pm 'fail fast'), so the die unwinds run_scheduler_only into process()'s eval and the entire runner winds down. Multi-entry preload_list is a first-class test-header feature (App/Yath2/TestFile.pm preload_list handling), and the flush window (run_scheduler_only flushes submissions as soon as ONE stage is live while others are still 'starting') makes queue-time/dispatch-time lifecycle skew the normal startup sequence.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: Preload config with stages A and B; A is slow to ready. Tasks are flushed/queued while B is 'up' and A still 'starting'; a test whose preload_list is [A, B] buckets under B. Seconds later A registers stage_ready. On the next tick _next picks the task from the B bucket, _start_task re-resolves task_stage to A, the lookup in bucket A fails, and the runner dies mid-run: every running job is killed and yath aborts with 'Task <job_id> was not pending' (or an undef-array-deref). Same crash on a persistent runner whenever a restarting stage comes back up while tasks listing it first sit bucketed under a later-preference stage.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Make _start_task locate the pending bucket by the stage _next actually found it under (pass the bucket stage through the spec, or record the bucketed stage on the task at queue time) instead of re-resolving task_stage; alternatively re-bucket tasks whenever a stage lifecycle transitions to 'up'.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: One addition to the proposal: _start_task already receives the bucket stage as $spec->{stage} (advance_tasks line 1068 passes _next's run_by_stage, which _stage_order guarantees equals the bucket key), so the minimal fix is to use $spec->{stage} for the PENDING_TASKS lookup at State.pm:408-410 instead of re-resolving via task_fields — only $cat/$dur/$run_id/$smoke need task-derived values, and none of those are time-dependent. Also note the undef-deref variant fires at line 411 (my $count = @$set), not 410.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Cheap fix already in hand: _start_task receives the bucket stage in $spec->{stage} ($run_stage from _next, which per _stage_order (1126-1139) is identical to the bucket key lstage). Use that for the PENDING_TASKS lookup (run_id/smoke/cat/dur from task_fields are stable; only the stage dimension is volatile) instead of the re-resolved value — a one-line change at State.pm:410 plus the prune_hash path at 415. Optionally also add a symmetric _rebucket_stage_tasks call on the starting/restarting->up transition (mirroring the existing down-demotion rebucket from the DONE ticket at TODO_TASKS.md:726-736) so tasks migrate to their preferred stage rather than merely not crashing. No existing TODO_TASKS.md ticket covers the up-transition divergence.

acc_verdict.reason: Traced end to end and confirmed. _queue_task buckets by task_stage's time-dependent resolution (State.pm:866-868 returns the first preload_list stage currently 'up') and nothing records the chosen bucket on the task. The skew window is the normal startup sequence: run_scheduler_only flushes buffered submissions once _ready_to_schedule is true, which needs only the stage map + ONE live stage peer (Runner.pm:806-814, 738-751); later stage_ready reports (Handlers.pm:1035) call only state->stage_ready — _rebucket_stage_tasks runs solely on starting->down expiry (State.pm:697), never on an up-transition. At dispatch, _next returns the task from its physical bucket (B) with run_by_stage=B, Resource::Preload::available returns 1 (a listed stage is up, no gate), but _start_task line 408 re-calls task_fields, which now resolves stage A (first-listed, freshly 'up'); the line 410 lookup hits bucket A: $set is undef (undef-array-deref at line 411) or lacks the job (die "Task ... was not pending", line 413). scheduler_tick (Role/Scheduler.pm:89-101) is deliberately eval-free ("fail fast ... left to propagate"), so the die unwinds run_scheduler_only into process()'s eval (Runner.pm:474) and the whole runner winds down, killing running jobs. confirmedFindings.title: Run/task submissions buffered after readiness regresses mid-run are never flushed (flush_submit_buffer is called exactly once)
confirmedFindings.evidence: submit_action buffers any queue_run/queue_task/stop_run/end_queue submission whenever `_preload_root_hosts_stages && !_ready_to_schedule` (Runner.pm:887-890). _ready_to_schedule requires _has_live_stage_peer (line 811), which regresses to false whenever every 'preload-<stage>' connection is closed — e.g. during a reload_root re-exec of the whole preload tree, or while a lone 'default' stage restarts under --monitor-preloads. flush_submit_buffer is called at exactly one place, Runner.pm:1203, after the startup until-loop and before the main while(1) loop; nothing in the main loop or in any request handler (grep confirms) ever flushes again. So a submission that lands in the buffer mid-run stays there forever even after the stages re-register.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: Persistent runner with preloads; a source change (or `yath reload`) triggers a stage/tree reload. During the few seconds the stage connections are down, a user runs `yath test`: its queue_run/queue_task frames are buffered by submit_action. The stages come back up, but the buffer is never flushed — the run is never queued, the runner idles, and the `yath test` client hangs forever waiting for its run to start, with no error anywhere.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Call flush_submit_buffer from the main run loop (or from the stage_ready / set_stage_data handlers) whenever _ready_to_schedule is true and the buffer is non-empty, preserving order by flushing the buffer before applying the triggering action.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Scenario is realistic and not a rare race: with --monitor-preloads the common sequence "save a source file (triggers tree reload) then immediately run `yath test`" places the submission inside the stage-downtime window. Two additional precise details: (1) reported_stage_data stays defined (stale) across the reload, so the regression is driven purely by _has_live_stage_peer; (2) even on a transient run, a buffered end_queue alone hangs the runner because State::done requires QUEUE_ENDED (State.pm:175-187). Also note a partial-buffer hazard the finding missed: if the window closes mid-stream, queue_run may be buffered while later queue_task frames apply directly, breaking submission ordering — so the proposed fix must flush the buffer before applying any newly-arriving action, as the proposal already states.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Cheap fix matching the finding's proposal: flush at the top of the main while(1) loop (after service_io at Runner.pm:1229) guarded by `_ready_to_schedule && $self->{submit_buffer}`, or flush from the stage-registration handler that re-establishes a live peer; either preserves order if the buffer is drained before applying the triggering action (submit_action already appends, so calling flush_submit_buffer at the top of submit_action's ready branch is the smallest change). Related work in TODO_TASKS.md: ticket #3 (stage lifecycle moves to the preload-root, runner stops managing stage lifecycle, generation stamping deleted) will rework exactly this peer-liveness area — the flush fix should be folded in or re-checked there, since #3 changes what 'live stage peer' means during a reload. No existing ticket names the unflushed buffer itself.

The comments (Runner.pm:800-805, 1171-1177) show buffering was designed for the startup handshake window only; the mid-run regression is an unhandled gap, not intended behavior.

confirmedFindings.title: Demoting a stage to 'down' via set_stage_map or stage_down strands its pending tasks — run hangs
confirmedFindings.evidence: _next only traverses buckets of stages whose lifecycle is 'up' (_stage_order, State.pm:1136), so tasks physically bucketed under a stage that becomes permanently 'down' are never visited. _rebucket_stage_tasks exists exactly to drain such buckets, but it is only invoked from _expire_stale_stages, which is gated on --preload-stage-startup-timeout (default 0 = off) and only handles 'starting'/'restarting'. The other two demotion paths — set_stage_map marking a stage absent from a refreshed map as 'down' (lines 757-761) and stage_down() (request_handler_stage_down) — do NOT rebucket. done() returns 0 while PENDING_TASKS is non-empty (line 179), and resource_timeout defaults to 0 (App/Yath2/Options/Runner.pm:567), so nothing ever times the stranded tasks out.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: Persistent preloaded runner; tasks for stage 'foo' are queued/bucketed. The user removes stage 'foo' from the preload config and HUP-reloads; the preload-root re-reports a stage map without 'foo'; set_stage_map marks 'foo' down but leaves its bucketed tasks in PENDING_TASKS->{run}{smoke}{foo}. _next never walks that bucket, done() never becomes true, the run never completes, and the submitting client hangs indefinitely with jobs 'pending' forever.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Call _rebucket_stage_tasks($stage) whenever a stage transitions to 'down' — in stage_down() and in set_stage_map's removed-stage loop — so task_stage re-resolves the stranded tasks (default stage, or a resource-gated skip).
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Minor imprecision: no in-tree code currently sends a 'stage_down' report (Preload/Host.pm:703 sends 'stage_restarting' on stage exit; StageDelegate::stage_down is a no-op stub), so the request_handler_stage_down path (Handlers.pm:1043-1049) is a latent endpoint with no in-tree sender — the concretely executable trigger is the set_stage_map refresh on preload-tree respawn (mid-run `yath reload`/HUP with a stage removed from the preload's stage set). The proposal (call _rebucket_stage_tasks on both demotion paths) is correct and should cover the latent stage_down endpoint too. Also note: once demoted 'down', even enabling --preload-stage-startup-timeout cannot recover the bucket, since _expire_stale_stages skips 'down' stages.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Cheap fix, exactly as proposed: add `$self->_rebucket_stage_tasks($stage)` after the demotion in set_stage_map's removed-stage loop (State.pm:760) and in stage_down() (State.pm:643) — this mirrors what _expire_stale_stages already does at State.pm:697 and reuses existing, tested machinery (the timeout-path rebucket landed as a DONE TODO item, TODO_TASKS.md line ~726). Note stage_down() is also called by _expire_stale_stages itself, so if the rebucket is moved into stage_down() the duplicate call at line 697 becomes redundant (rebucketing an already-drained bucket is a harmless no-op, but can be cleaned up). No open TODO_TASKS.md ticket currently covers this; TODO #2 (done) defined the 'down'-on-map-refresh semantics but did not add the rebucket to the non-timeout demotion paths. Also worth a line in the fix: keep the stage_down rebucket even though the request has no production sender today — the handler exists on the wire and any future sender would silently reintroduce the hang.

confirmedFindings.title: A run that activates and finishes within a single scheduler tick is never announced (harness_run_end lost, run never purged)
confirmedFindings.evidence: scheduler_tick captures the active run BEFORE the advance loop (`$before = $state->run ? run_id : undef; ACTIVE_RUN //= $before`) and announces only when ACTIVE_RUN (a run observed active across a tick boundary) leaves the slot. State::advance can, in one loop, activate a pending run and immediately clear_finished_run it (a run already marked stopped with zero pending tasks and nothing running — e.g. one halted/aborted while still pending, or an empty run). Such a run is active only INSIDE the loop: $before was undef (or the previous run), $after skips it, so announce_run is never called for it. announce_run is the ONLY emitter of the harness_run_end frame and the only place aborting_runs/terminated_jobs/collector_reap cleanup and ownerless purge_run happen (grep: single call site, Scheduler.pm:115).
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: Persistent runner: run A is active; a client queues run B and then aborts it (halt_run drops B's tasks, stop_run marks it stopped) before A finishes. When A clears, the same advance loop activates B and immediately retires it. announce_run fires for A only; B's harness_run_end frame is never forwarded, so B's subscriber/renderer waits forever for run end, and B is retained (never purged if ownerless) — a leak plus a hung client on the persistent path.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Detect run transitions inside the advance loop (e.g. have clear_finished_run/advance report the retired run_id) and announce every retired run, instead of diffing the active slot across the whole loop.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: The single failure scenario conflates two distinct legs. (1) Owner-drop-abort leg (the finding's "client aborts B"): if the abort came from the owner disconnecting, that client is gone — no hang — but handle_owner_drop deletes the owner record first (Handlers.pm:302), so the ownerless purge in announce_run (1348) never fires and B leaks permanently in RETAINED_RUNS/STOPPED_RUNS/HALTED_RUNS on the persistent runner. (2) Hung-client leg: requires the owner to stay connected — explicit halt_run+stop_run of a pending run, or an empty run stop_run'd before activation — then the subscriber waits forever for harness_run_end; the run is purged only when that owner finally drops. Also note the bug does not need run A at all: an empty/pre-stopped run activated and cleared within one tick's loop (before=undef) is skipped even as the only run. Proposal (announce every run retired by clear_finished_run, e.g. have advance report retired run_ids) is correct.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Cheap fix matching the finding's proposal: make clear_finished_run (State.pm:970) push the retired run_id onto a small "retired since last poll" list (or have advance return it), and have scheduler_tick announce every drained retired run instead of diffing the ACTIVE_RUN slot across the loop; alternatively announce inside the while(1) loop by re-checking the slot after each advance() call. No existing TODO_TASKS.md ticket covers this specific race (nearby owner-drop/retention work — the abort_on_disconnect owner-gating block and #35 TASK_LOOKUP cleanup — is already DONE and does not fix it), so it would need its own small ticket; the fix is localized to Scheduler.pm scheduler_tick plus a one-line return-value change in State.pm and is a natural drive-by for any future scheduler/announce_run work.

A stopped taskless pending run is reachable three ways: (a) request_handler_halt_run (Handlers.pm:799) + request_handler_stop_run (782, submit_action passthrough) on a not-yet-active run — no guard requires the run to be active; (b) handle_owner_drop (Handlers.pm:296-329) — run_status returns 'running' for a pending run (State.pm:168), so abort_on_disconnect calls abort_run → halt_run+_stop_run on it; (c) an empty run whose stop_run lands before first activation. announce_run (Handlers.pm:1309-1352) has exactly one call site (Scheduler.pm:115) and is the sole emitter of harness_run_end and the sole ownerless purge_run site (1348); yath run keys completion on harness_run_end, not EOF (Command/run.pm:68). No timeout, EOF handler, or other peer ever announces or purges the skipped run.

confirmedFindings.title: _start_task mutates env_vars/test_args refs shared with the TASK_LOOKUP original, duplicating resource args across retries/requeues
confirmedFindings.evidence: _start_task's copy `{%$task, stage => $run_stage}` is shallow (and when the stage already matches, no copy is made at all), so `$task->{env_vars}->{$_} = ...` and `push @{$task->{test_args}} => @{$res->{args}}` (State.pm:420-421) write into the env_vars hash / test_args array shared with the ORIGINAL task kept in TASK_LOOKUP. _retry_task ({is_try=>1, %$task}) and requeue_task ({%$task}) also copy shallowly, so a retried or requeued attempt starts from a task whose test_args already contain attempt 1's resource-assigned args, and _start_task appends attempt 2's on top. The Resource API explicitly documents resources pushing args (`push @{$state->{args}} => $id`, Resource.pm:180/441), and JobCount assigns env_vars in-tree (JobCount.pm:76).
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: A resource class that assigns a per-attempt argument (the documented Resource API pattern, e.g. a port or resource id pushed into args): a test fails and is retried, or is requeued after an assign->launch race. The second attempt's command line contains BOTH the stale attempt-1 resource arg and the new one (e.g. two --port values), so the test runs against the wrong/stale resource; each further retry appends another copy.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Deep-copy env_vars and test_args in _start_task (e.g. `{%$task, stage=>..., env_vars=>{%{$task->{env_vars}//{}}}, test_args=>[@{$task->{test_args}//[]}]}`) so per-attempt resource assignments never leak back into the canonical TASK_LOOKUP task.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Impact correction: no bundled resource pushes args (CPU/Memory/Disk/UnixLimits assign no env/args; JobCount only sets env var T2_HARNESS_MY_JOB_CONCURRENCY, whose per-key overwrite makes its retry pollution benign). The arg-duplication symptom requires a third-party resource following the documented Resource API example, so in-tree runs are unaffected. Additional side effect worth noting: queue items are built with the TestFile object's own env_vars/test_args refs (App/Yath2/TestFile.pm:629-635), so the mutation can also leak into the finder's TestFile, not just TASK_LOOKUP. Proposed deep-copy fix in _start_task is correct.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Cheap fix exactly as proposed: in _start_task always build a fresh task hash with deep-copied env_vars/test_args ({%$task, stage=>$run_stage, env_vars=>{%{$task->{env_vars}//{}}}, test_args=>[@{$task->{test_args}//[]}]}) — note the fix must also cover the `unless stage ne` branch at State.pm:418 where no copy is made at all. No existing TODO_TASKS.md ticket covers this, but TODO #24 (Resource base -> Role refactor) touches the same resource machinery and this one-line deep copy could land in passing there; the requeue_task comment block (:517-536) already claims "TASK_LOOKUP holds the ORIGINAL task ... the resolved-stage copy lives only in RUNNING_TASKS", which this finding shows is only true for top-level keys — worth correcting that comment when fixing.

Runner/Job.pm:447 merges task test_args into the command args, so a resource that pushes per-attempt args (the documented API pattern, Resource.pm:180) yields both the stale and new arg on the retried test's command line, growing each retry. This also violates the code's own stated invariant (State.pm:532-534) that the resolved copy lives only in RUNNING_TASKS.

But since it needs an out-of-tree plugin resource on top of a retry, it is an edge case rather than a normal-use path: P2.

confirmedFindings.title: Runner::Client silently drops one-way submissions on any write failure (including EAGAIN on its non-blocking socket) and transparently reconnects, losing queued tasks mid-stream
confirmedFindings.evidence: Client.pm:233 sets `$fh->blocking(0)` on the client socket. All writes go through Connection::_write -> write_frame (t2clib Socket.pm:68-80), which retries ONLY EINTR: on a non-blocking fd whose send buffer is full, syswrite returns undef with EAGAIN and write_frame croaks; Connection::_write catches the croak and silently CLOSES the connection (Connection.pm:330-334), and send_request then returns undef (Connection.pm:233). Client::_send (Client.pm:249-253) never checks send_request's return nor conn->closed after sending, and Client::connection (Client.pm:207-209) sees the closed connection on the NEXT call and transparently dials a fresh one (`return $conn if $conn && !$conn->closed;` falls through to reconnect). So a queue_task whose frame hit EAGAIN/EPIPE is lost with no error, no retry, and no runner_gone flag, and subsequent tasks continue on the new connection.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: A large `yath test` run submits thousands of queue_task frames in a tight loop while the runner is momentarily not draining runner.socket (busy forking a burst of jobs, preload work, a slow subscriber write). The unix-socket send buffer (~208KB) fills, syswrite returns EAGAIN, the connection is silently closed and the in-flight task frame (plus any not-yet-sent tasks in that call) is discarded; the client reconnects and keeps submitting the rest, then sends stop_run/end_queue. The runner never received some tasks, so those test files are simply never run — the run completes, reports green, and the user has no indication tests were skipped. The same silent-hole behavior occurs if a persistent runner is restarted mid-submission.
confirmedFindings.proposal: In Client::_send, check the result: if send_request returns undef or the connection closed during the send, either croak (submission integrity is broken) or re-establish and re-send the frame. Better: since these client sockets are only made non-blocking for drain(), do writes with a blocking/poll-based write_frame variant (wait for POLLOUT on EAGAIN) so a slow runner causes backpressure instead of data loss.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: The lost frame can also be queue_run, stop_run, or end_queue, not just tasks: a lost stop_run means the runner never learns the run's queue ended, so the run never finishes and the client hangs waiting for run_done — a hang rather than the silent-green outcome, which applies when only task frames are lost. Also note write_frame can partially write a frame before the EAGAIN croak; the subsequent close EOFs the old fd so the runner's FrameBuffer discards the truncated frame cleanly (data loss, not protocol corruption). The proposal's poll-for-POLLOUT blocking-write variant is the right fix since the fd must stay non-blocking for _request's drain loop.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Cheap fix: send_request already signals failure (returns undef when _write closed the connection), so Client::_send just needs to check it and croak or reconnect-and-resend (~3 lines); a POLLOUT-waiting write_frame variant would instead give backpressure. No existing TODO_TASKS.md ticket covers this — the nearby "write-fail / explicit stage ack" item (~line 152) is the runner-to-stage dispatch path, not Runner::Client; consider folding this into that reliability work. Also note write_frame partial-write + EAGAIN can tear a large frame (queue_run) mid-send, not just drop whole frames.

Connection::_write (Connection.pm:329-334) evals the croak and silently closes; send_request returns undef with an in-code comment saying callers must treat that as "not delivered". Runner::Client::_send (Client.pm:249-253) ignores the return, and connection() (Client.pm:207-209) transparently redials on the next call — no retry, no error, no runner_gone. The tight-loop caller exists: App::Yath2::Client::submit_queue (Client.pm:500-512) sends queue_run, then every task, then stop_run with no draining or pacing, and nothing cross-checks delivered vs pending task counts. The intended discipline is proven by contrast: Runner.pm:1127-1139 checks service_send's return and requeues on failure, so Runner::Client's silent ignore is an omission, not design; nothing in ARCHITECTURE.md marks task submission best-effort. confirmedFindings.title: Leading whitespace in HARNESS_PERL_SWITCHES injects an empty-string switch; the exec'd perl treats '' as its program and every test silently does not run
confirmedFindings.evidence: switches_from_env does `split /\s+/, $ENV{HARNESS_PERL_SWITCHES}` (line 375). Verified: `split /\s+/, " -w"` returns ('', '-w') -- a leading empty field. switches() pushes it (empty string is not in %seen/%seen2), and collector_target builds exec => [$^X, @cli_includes, @switches, @cli_options, $run_file, @args], so the argv becomes e.g. `perl -Ilib '' -w -MTest2::Plugin::UUID t/foo.t`. Verified empirically on this machine: `perl '' t.pl` exits 0 and never runs t.pl (the empty arg is taken as the program; everything after it becomes @ARGV). Also, the empty switch forces use_fork=0 (line 567: '' fails m/\s*-w\s*/), so ALL tests take this exec path -- none escape via the preload/fork path. Legacy 1.x has the same split, but the failure is real and current.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: User has `export HARNESS_PERL_SWITCHES=" -w"` (leading space is common when composing from an initially-unset var, e.g. HARNESS_PERL_SWITCHES="$HARNESS_PERL_SWITCHES -w"). Every perl test in the run execs as `perl ... '' -w <file>`: perl exits 0 immediately with zero output, the -M injections (UUID/MemUsage/Interactive) never load, and the test body never executes. The user sees every test end with no events/no plan (reported as confusing failures at best, or a silently green no-op depending on empty-output handling) with no hint that an empty switch is the cause.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Use `split ' ', $ENV{HARNESS_PERL_SWITCHES}` (awk-style split, strips leading whitespace) or `grep { length } split /\s+/, ...` in switches_from_env.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Trigger requires *leading* whitespace specifically: trailing whitespace is harmless because split /\s+/ drops trailing empty fields, and a leading-whitespace-only value like " " still yields one '' field. Whether the user sees every test fail (no plan / empty event stream) or a silently green no-op depends on the collector's final-state handling of an empty stream with exit 0, but in either case no test code runs. Fix as proposed: `split ' ', ...` (awk-style) or `grep { length } split /\s+/, ...` in switches_from_env (Job.pm:375).
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Cheap one-line fix in Test2::Harness2::Runner::Job::switches_from_env (lib/Test2/Harness2/Runner/Job.pm:375): use awk-style `split ' ', $ENV{HARNESS_PERL_SWITCHES}` (strips leading whitespace and collapses runs) or `grep { length } split /\s+/, ...`. No existing TODO_TASKS.md entry mentions HARNESS_PERL_SWITCHES; worth fixing in passing, and the same pattern should be patched in legacy 1.x if it is still cut for releases. A slightly better fix is Text::ParseWords::shellwords, which also handles quoted switch arguments (e.g. -MFoo="a b"), matching what ExtUtils/TAP-era harnesses do.

confirmedFindings.title: -w switch detection matches '-w' as a substring anywhere, so any switch merely containing '-w' wrongly enables $^W and is silently dropped on the preload path
confirmedFindings.evidence: use_fork: `return $self->{+USE_FORK} = 0 if grep { !m/\s*-w\s*/ } $self->switches;` and switches(): `$self->{+USE_W_SWITCH} = 1 if $s =~ m/\s*-w\s*/;`. Because \s* matches the empty string, the pattern is effectively /-w/ -- a substring match. A switch like '-I/srv/my-web/lib' or '-Mmod-with-w' contains '-w', so (a) it does NOT disable use_fork (the grep finds no non-matching switch), letting the job take the preload/fork path where command-line switches are never applied at all, and (b) USE_W_SWITCH becomes true, so JobLauncher::final_state (line 445) sets $^W = 1 in the test.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: User sets HARNESS_PERL_SWITCHES=-I/home/bob/my-website/lib (path contains '-w'). The job is treated as if the only switch were -w: it runs on the preload path where the -I is silently ignored (modules under that path fail to load, or the wrong installed version is used), and $^W=1 is force-enabled, spraying warnings from (or changing behavior of) tests that run clean without it. Intended behavior for any non '-w' switch is use_fork=0 with the switch applied via exec.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Anchor the pattern: m/^\s*-w\s*$/ in all four places (use_fork line 567 and the three USE_W_SWITCH assignments).
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Since switches are whitespace-split tokens, m/^-w$/ suffices as the fix (the proposed m/^\s*-w\s*$/ also works). Clustered switches like -wT would then correctly force the exec path, which is the safe/conservative outcome. confirmedFindings.title: Spawned (detached, harness-outliving) scripts get TMPDIR/TEMPDIR pointing inside the harness workdir, which is deleted at yath stop while the script still runs
confirmedFindings.evidence: Spawn subclasses Job and overrides out_file/err_file/in_file/job_dir/run_dir but NOT tmp_dir or env_vars. The spawn script child runs JobLauncher::cleanup_process -> set_env -> Job::env_vars, which sets TMPDIR/TEMPDIR to Job::tmp_dir = a File::Temp dir created under $runner->tmp_dir; for the stage host that is '<workdir>/tmp' (Preload/Host.pm lines 174-179), inside the harness working directory. Spawn processes are explicitly "detached from the harness lifecycle" and "survive runner/stage teardown" (ARCHITECTURE 4.8, launch_spawn comments), but the workdir (including its tmp subtree) is removed when the persistent harness stops. The script also inherits test-only vars (HARNESS_ACTIVE=1, TEST2_HARNESS_ACTIVE=1, TEST2_JOB_DIR='').
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: `yath start` (preload), `yath spawn app.pl` where app.pl is a long-running tool that creates temp files (File::Temp honors TMPDIR). Later the user runs `yath stop`; the workdir and the spawn's TMPDIR are deleted while app.pl -- designed to survive teardown -- keeps running. Its next tempfile/tempdir creation fails with ENOENT ('No such file or directory' on a path under the vanished workdir), an error the user cannot connect to yath.
confirmedFindings.proposal: In Runner::Spawn, override tmp_dir (and the TMPDIR/TEMPDIR env entries, e.g. via an env_vars override) to use the system temp dir / the settings' orig_tmp instead of the harness workdir, and drop the HARNESS_ACTIVE-style test markers for non-test spawn processes.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Also applies to `yath kill` (kill.pm:48 removes the workdir the same way), not just `yath stop`. TEST2_RUN_DIR is likewise set to '' (Spawn::run_dir returns ""). The env already carries SYSTEM_TMPDIR = settings->harness->orig_tmp, which is the natural value for the proposed Spawn tmp_dir/env override. Job.pm tmp_dir is at lines ~522-532 as cited; all other citations are accurate.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Cheap fix: Runner::Spawn already inherits env_vars that computes SYSTEM_TMPDIR from $settings->harness->orig_tmp; add a tmp_dir override returning orig_tmp (2 lines) and an env_vars wrapper deleting HARNESS_ACTIVE/TEST2_HARNESS_ACTIVE/TEST2_JOB_DIR for non-test spawns. Also confirmed TEST2_JOB_DIR='' (Spawn::job_dir returns ""). No existing TODO_TASKS.md ticket covers this; worth adding one alongside the Tier-5 spawn section (~line 787).

confirmedFindings.title: Named preload stages inherit the 'preload-root' jump frame and re-exec duplicate preload-root trees on reload/HUP
confirmedFindings.evidence: Host::init installs a HUP handler that sets PENDING_RELOAD in ANY Preload::Host process ('$self->{+PENDING_RELOAD} = 1 unless $self->{+SIGNAL}', line 170). run_stage's tail runs 'longjump \'preload-root\' => \'respawn\'' guarded ONLY by PENDING_RELOAD (line 725-727), before the named-stage 'exit 0' (line 729). Named stages are forked (Preloader::launch_stage) from the preload-root process deep inside launch()'s setjump 'preload-root' frame (Preload.pm line 130), so every forked stage INHERITS that Long::Jump frame — the comment's claim that 'only the base/default stage owns that jump frame' is false for forked children. When the base stage ends its loop with SIGNAL=HUP (yath reload via request_handler_reload_root, direct SIGHUP, or a monitor-detected change) it does killall($SIGNAL) (line 715), delivering SIGHUP to every named stage's process group. Each named stage's HUP handler sets PENDING_RELOAD, its loop ends via end_test_loop (SIGNAL set), no 'stop' request ever clears PENDING_RELOAD (stop_stages is a no-op, see separate finding), so each named stage reaches the longjump and execs '$^X -MTest2::Harness2::Preload=launch,runner.socket' — a brand-new full preload-root — from inside itself.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: Persistent runner: 'yath start -PMy::Preload' where My::Preload defines named stages, then 'yath reload' (or edit a monitored file). Base stage killall(HUP)s its children; every named stage execs its own duplicate preload-root. Each duplicate dials runner.socket, re-registers as 'preload-root' (clobbering the peer registry), re-preloads everything, forks its own copy of every named stage and re-binds preload-<stage>.socket over the legitimate tree's sockets. Meanwhile the real base sits in an untimed wait(all=>1) (line 717) for those pids, which never exit because they exec'd into long-lived preload-roots — process count multiplies on every reload and the base hangs.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Guard the respawn by process identity, not just the flag: only longjump 'preload-root' when this process IS the preload-root (e.g. record the preload-root pid at launch() and check $$ == that pid, or check $stage eq 'base'||'default' before the longjump); in named stages a HUP should just exit 0 so the parent relaunches them. Also make the HUP handler ignore/exit for stage children.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Two precision notes: (a) the process-group killall path requires USE_P_GROUPS (true on all non-Windows platforms); without pgroups only the stage's collector PARENT receives the HUP, giving a different failure (stage never reloads) rather than duplication. (b) The monitored-file-change reload path (Host.pm end_test_loop → preloader->check → SIGNAL='HUP', lines 816-818) triggers the same named-stage duplication via killall(HUP) even though it never sets PENDING_RELOAD in the base process itself — so the bug is not limited to request_handler_reload_root/direct SIGHUP. Severity P1 rather than P0: it hard-hangs the persistent runner and multiplies preload trees on every reload, but only in the yath start + named-preload-stages + reload configuration, with no data-corruption or security dimension. The proposed fix (guard the respawn longjump by preload-root process identity, e.g. record launch()'s pid and require $$ to match, or restrict to stage eq 'base'/'default') is correct; note the run_test longjump path must remain fork-reachable, so the guard belongs on the respawn branch only.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Cheap fix: the process-identity guard already exists one line below — line 729's `exit 0 unless $stage eq 'base' || $stage eq 'default'`; wrap the longjump at Host.pm:725 in the same stage (or recorded launch-pid == $$) check so named stages exit 0 on HUP and get relaunched by the respawned tree. Fixing stop_stages delivery (the separate no-op-stop finding) mitigates the common case but leaves a signal-vs-socket race, so the identity guard is still needed. Only transient `yath test` runs without reload/monitor are unaffected; no covering entry found in TODO_TASKS.md.

acc_verdict.reason: Confirmed end to end. (1) Named stages DO inherit the 'preload-root' Long::Jump frame: the fork in Preloader::launch_stage happens inside run_tests, which sits inside launch()'s setjump 'preload-root' (Preload.pm:130); the 'Stage-Collector' longjump unwinds only to the launch_stage frame, leaving the preload-root frame intact. Proof the code itself relies on this inheritance: named-stage test launches call JobLauncher::launch_via_double_fork(..., 'preload-root') (Host.pm:272, JobLauncher.pm:274/344), which longjumps 'preload-root' from a fork of the named stage — so the Host.pm:719-724 comment ('only the base/default stage owns that jump frame') is provably false. (2) PENDING_RELOAD gets set in named stages: yath reload → Runner.pm:190-205 → reload_root → Host.pm:381-391 sets PENDING_RELOAD+SIGNAL=HUP in the base; base loop ends and killall('HUP') (Host.pm:715) signals each StageProcess process group (USE_P_GROUPS=1 on Unix, stage did setpgrp, IPC.pm:108-113), and the stage's inherited HUP handler (Host.pm:160-171) sets PENDING_RELOAD=1. The stop-wins branch (Host.pm:684-687) requires a stop request the reload path never sends. (4) The named stage therefore reaches longjump 'preload-root'=>'respawn' (725-727) before exit 0 (729) and execs a full duplicate preload-root (Preload.pm:141-145), which re-dials runner.socket and rebuilds the whole stage tree. The base's untimed wait(all=>1) (717) waits on the stage collector parent, which cannot exit while the exec'd persistent duplicate holds the stage's stdout/stderr pipes open — the base hangs and processes multiply per reload, as claimed.

(b) The monitored-file-change reload path (Host.pm end_test_loop → preloader->check → SIGNAL='HUP', lines 816-818) triggers the same named-stage duplication via killall(HUP) even though it never sets PENDING_RELOAD in the base process itself — so the bug is not limited to request_handler_reload_root/direct SIGHUP. Severity P1 rather than P0: it hard-hangs the persistent runner and multiplies preload trees on every reload, but only in the yath start + named-preload-stages + reload configuration, with no data-corruption or security dimension. The proposed fix (guard the respawn longjump by preload-root process identity, e.g. record launch()'s pid and require $$ to match, or restrict to stage eq 'base'/'default') is correct; note the run_test longjump path must remain fork-reachable, so the guard belongs on the respawn branch only.

sev_verdict.reason: Confirmed reachable on a core supported path. Named stages are pure forks (Preloader.pm:185) from inside the preload-root's setjump 'preload-root' frame (Preload.pm:130), so they inherit the jump frame; the inherited HUP handler (Host.pm:170) sets PENDING_RELOAD in every stage when the base does killall(HUP) (Host.pm:715); the only clearing path is the 'stop' message (Host.pm:684-687), which per the companion finding never arrives (and is a socket-vs-signal race even if it did). Fixing stop_stages delivery (the separate no-op-stop finding) mitigates the common case but leaves a signal-vs-socket race, so the identity guard is still needed. confirmedFindings.title: Monitor-detected change in the base stage never sets PENDING_RELOAD, so the stage host exits instead of respawning — persistent runner terminates itself
confirmedFindings.evidence: end_test_loop sets '$self->{+SIGNAL} //= \'HUP\'' when preloader->check() detects a change (line 816-819) but never sets PENDING_RELOAD — that flag is only set by the actual SIGHUP handler or request_handler_reload_root. So when the base/default stage (which runs in the preload-root process and owns the respawn jump) detects a changed file, run_stage's 'if (delete $self->{+PENDING_RELOAD}) { longjump respawn }' does not fire; base falls to 'exit 0 unless base' (no-op), run_stage returns, run_tests' setjump gets no jump and returns, process() returns, and Preload::run_driver announces stage_host_exited. Runner side (_handle_dead_preload_root, Runner.pm 842-860) treats a dead preload-root as fatal — 'the runner does NOT respawn it' — sets SIGNAL=TERM and winds the whole runner down. This directly contradicts the in-file comments claiming a monitored file change uses 'the same flow' as the respawn (Host.pm 719-724, Preload.pm 380). On the persistent path monitor is always on and reload-in-place is off by default, so ANY change to a base-stage-loaded module takes this path (reloaded=0 'reloading disabled' -> @todo -> CHANGED -> SIGNAL=HUP).
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: 'yath start -PMy::Preload' (persistent; monitor on, --reload off); edit any module the base stage preloaded. Base's check() blacklists it and sets SIGNAL=HUP; the stage host exits without respawning; the runner prints the preload failure output, sets SIGNAL=TERM and the entire persistent runner shuts down. User expected a stage reload, gets a dead daemon.
confirmedFindings.proposal: In end_test_loop (or where check() returns true) on the base/default stage, set PENDING_RELOAD (not just SIGNAL=HUP) so run_stage takes the longjump 'respawn' path and re-execs the preload tree.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Monitor-detected change in the base/default stage sets SIGNAL=HUP but never PENDING_RELOAD (Host.pm:805-826), so run_stage (Host.pm:725-729) skips the 'preload-root' respawn longjump; the stage host winds down its stages and returns, and run_driver (Preload.pm:201-223) announces stage_host_exited and then idles until stopped. The preload-root stays ALIVE, so Runner._handle_dead_preload_root never fires; with empty stage_host_errors Runner.pm:1249 also does not fire. Net effect on 'yath start -P...': editing any base-preloaded file kills all stages, marks them 'restarting' forever, and leaves the persistent runner wedged (new runs hang at the dispatch gate waiting for a live stage peer); only if stray warnings were captured does the runner instead TERM itself. Fix as proposed: set PENDING_RELOAD alongside SIGNAL=HUP when preloader->check() returns true in end_test_loop (or immediately after the check), matching request_handler_reload_root (Host.pm:381-391).
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Cheap fix: where check() returns true in end_test_loop (Host.pm:816-818), also set PENDING_RELOAD — but ONLY for the base/default stage (guard by stage name): a named child stage does not own the 'preload-root' Long::Jump frame and an unguarded longjump would die; named stages already relaunch correctly via their exit-0 path. No existing TODO_TASKS.md ticket covers this; ticket #4 (stage lifecycle/generation stamping) is adjacent and could absorb the fix in passing. A regression test should cover: persistent runner + monitor on + reload off + touch a preloaded module → expect respawn (stage_restarting then fresh stage_ready), not runner TERM.

acc_verdict.reason: Core bug confirmed by trace: end_test_loop (Host.pm:816-818) sets only SIGNAL=HUP on a monitor-detected change; PENDING_RELOAD is set only by the SIGHUP handler (Host.pm:170) and request_handler_reload_root (Host.pm:387), so the base/default stage never takes the longjump 'preload-root'=>'respawn' at Host.pm:725-727 and the preload tree is never respawned — directly contradicting the intent stated at Host.pm:376-378 ("the same flow a monitored file change uses") and Preload.pm:137-140. confirmedFindings.title: Host::stop_stages is a silent no-op: child stages never register as peers of the parent host, only of the real runner
confirmedFindings.evidence: stop_stages does service_send("preload-$stage", 'stop') on $self (the parent host). But child stages dial the REAL runner's runner.socket (_connect_runner, line 597-609) and bind their own preload-<stage>.socket; nothing ever connects them to the parent host's service, so the parent's service_peers only ever contains 'runner' (and, in the root, nothing at all after close_service). service_send returns 0 (service_peer_conn undef) and the eval swallows it, so no stage ever receives this 'stop'. The comment's premise ('stopped via service_send to their peer identity ... the SAME registered channel each stage opened to the runner') is wrong — that channel terminates at the real runner, not at this host.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: Whenever run_stage ends for a reason the real runner did not initiate (monitor-detected change, direct SIGHUP, orphaned workdir), stop_stages delivers nothing; the only thing that ends child stages is the subsequent killall(SIGNAL) — i.e. the raw-signal paths that trigger the duplicate-respawn (HUP) and rogue-idler (TERM) bugs above. Graceful stage shutdown from the host side never happens.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Either delete stop_stages (and rely on the runner's stop_preload_stages) or make it signal children with a dedicated benign mechanism (e.g. have stages also dial their parent's socket, or send TERM only after fixing the TERM exit path).
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Standalone impact is smaller than the P2 guess implies: no hang can result from the no-op because StageDelegate::done is a constant 0 (StageDelegate.pm:142), so a stage-service run loop can only end with {+SIGNAL} set, meaning the killall($SIGNAL) fallback at Host.pm:715 always fires and children are always terminated. On the runner-initiated shutdown path each stage also receives a direct 'stop' from the real runner (Runner::stop_preload_stages), so stop_stages is redundant there too. The standalone defect is dead code plus a wrong comment that silently forces all host-initiated child teardown onto the raw-signal paths; the direct user-visible harm belongs to the companion HUP duplicate-respawn / TERM exit-path findings. P3 standalone; P2 only as an enabler of those.

confirmedFindings.title: Runner::Preload::default_stage returns a StageConfig object when no default() was declared, so no stage is ever flagged default and the runner falls back to the alphabetically-first stage
confirmedFindings.evidence: default_stage: 'return $self->{+DEFAULT_STAGE} if ...; return $self->{+STAGE_LIST}->[0];' — STAGE_LIST holds StageConfig OBJECTS (add_stage pushes $stage), and merge() caches that object into DEFAULT_STAGE ('$self->{+DEFAULT_STAGE} //= $merge->default_stage'). Host::stage_data then computes 'default => (defined($default) && $name eq $default) ? 1 : 0' (line 257); StageConfig has no string overload, so $name eq 'Test2::Harness2::Runner::StageConfig=HASH(0x...)' is never true and the reported stage map flags NO default. Runner::State::_default_stage_from_map (State.pm 886-896) then defensively picks the first stage BY SORTED NAME, not the first-declared stage. Preloader::task_stage (line 108) likewise returns the object where callers expect a name. Same latent quirk exists in 1.x, but in 2.0 stage_data/eq is the live consumer.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: Preload library declares 'stage ZMain => ...; stage Aux => ...' without calling default(). Intended default (first declared) is ZMain; the map flags nothing and the runner buckets every test lacking an explicit HARNESS-STAGE directive into 'Aux' (alphabetically first) — tests silently run in the wrong preload environment (missing modules, wrong fixtures), or wait on a stage that was never meant to take default traffic.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Make default_stage return $self->{+STAGE_LIST}->[0]->name (and have merge() store the name), or stringify via ->name in Host::stage_data before comparing.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: One correction of scope (bug is broader than stated): because merge() uses `DEFAULT_STAGE //= $merge->default_stage` and the cached object is truthy, a preload lib merged FIRST without default() also permanently masks an EXPLICIT default() from any lib merged later — violating the POD's documented 'first default set (based on load order) wins' contract (Preload.pm:415-417). So the failure hits even suites where some lib does call default(). Minor extra symptom: set_default_stage's croak message would interpolate the raw object. Proposal is correct; storing/returning `$self->{+STAGE_LIST}->[0]->name` fixes both the eq compare and the //= masking (name strings still mask correctly per the documented first-wins rule).
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Already ticketed: TODO_TASKS.md #78 ("Preload DEFAULT_STAGE type fix + closure/resolve duplication", line 1816) covers exactly this, including the merge()-cache poisoning (Preload.pm:177 can permanently cache the object) and the proposed one-line fix `return $self->{+STAGE_LIST}[0] ? $self->{+STAGE_LIST}[0]->name : undef;` plus normalizing the merge cache with `blessed($v) ? $v->name : $v`. Cheap to fix in passing; #78 also notes the fix intentionally changes observed behavior for no-default() preloads (first-declared stage becomes the flagged default instead of alphabetical fallback). Bug audit should dedupe against #78 rather than file new.

confirmedFindings.title: Transitive blacklist propagation is dead: check() looks up dep_map with absolute watched paths but DepTracer keys dep_map by relative require paths
confirmedFindings.evidence: DepTracer records 'push @{$dep_map->{$file}} => $loaded_by' where $file is the require argument ('Foo/Bar.pm', relative; absolute paths are even filtered out by the /^[_a-z]/i check). In Preloader::check, for HASH items $abs = $item->{file}, which comes from Reloader's watched path (absolute — monitor() stores $INC{$file} / catfile($dir,$file)); 'my $next = $dep_map->{$abs} or next;' therefore always misses, so no dependent is ever pushed onto @todo. For ARRAY items (would-be dependents) $abs is loaded_by's caller[1] (a source file path), again never a dep_map key. Net effect: only the changed module itself is blacklisted; the modules that loaded it (which the dep tracing infrastructure exists to catch) never are. Additionally dep_map values are [package, file] pairs where package can be '' (loaded_by fallback), which would die on ''->can(...) if the lookup ever matched.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: Persistent runner, monitor mode: lib/Config.pm (loaded by lib/App.pm inside the restarted stage's parent) changes. Only Config is blacklisted; App remains preloaded in the parent stage, so the relaunched child stage forks with the STALE Config already bound inside App's compiled code — tests keep seeing old behavior after the 'blacklisting changed files and reloading stage...' notification claimed a fix.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Look up dep_map by the relative path ('$dep_map->{$rel}'), and normalize ARRAY items' caller files through %CNI to relative keys before recursing (map $mod/$rel consistently); guard against the '' package before calling ->can.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Bug confirmed at lib/Test2/Harness2/Runner/Preloader.pm:705: dep_map must be keyed by the relative require path, so the lookup should be $dep_map->{$rel} (the $rel already computed at lines 691/695 but currently unused, along with the dead %CNI map at 682); also lc/normalize ARRAY items via %CNI as the code already attempts, dedupe %seen on $rel, and guard $mod ne '' before $mod->can('TEST2_HARNESS_PRELOAD') (loaded_by can return ['','']). Corrected failure scenario: persistent runner in monitor mode, Config.pm (loaded by preloaded App.pm) changes and cannot be reloaded in place — only Config is blacklisted; the stage restarts and correctly picks up the new Config (no stale code, contrary to the original scenario), but because App is not transitively blacklisted the relaunched stage preloads App which re-loads Config into the preheated image, so every subsequent edit to Config triggers another full stage restart (blacklist churn-prevention is dead) and Config's own blacklist entry is bypassed via the dependent. Inherited verbatim from legacy 1.x (reference/legacy/lib/Test2/Harness/Runner/Preloader.pm:588-614).
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Fix is nearly free: $rel is already extracted at Preloader.pm:691 — use $dep_map->{$rel} (and for ARRAY items map the caller file through the already-built %CNI at line 682 to a relative key before recursing), and skip entries with '' package before the ->can('TEST2_HARNESS_PRELOAD') call at line 702 (loaded_by can return ['',''], which would die once the lookup starts matching). confirmedFindings.title: Sampler's 5%-bucket change gating starves Resource::Memory of fresh mem_available exactly in the danger zone, so fine-grained thresholds (e.g. -R Memory=512mb) never defer
confirmedFindings.evidence: Sampler::service_tick only sends a system_load message when the rounded-up-to-5% cpu_pct or mem_pct bucket changes (`return unless $cpu_trig || $mem_trig`, line 208); the raw mem_total/mem_available bytes ride along only on those sends, and the runner just stores the last snapshot (Handlers.pm request_handler_system_load -> State::set_system_load). _round_up_5 saturates: every used_pct in (95,100] rounds to 100, so once memory use crosses 95% no further reports are sent no matter how far free memory falls. Resource::Memory::is_temporarily_unavailable compares the *stale* $load->{mem_available} bytes from that last report against its threshold (_effective_min_free_bytes).
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: 64GB host, `yath test -R Memory=512mb -j32`. Memory use climbs; when it crosses 95% used the sampler sends its last report with mem_available ~= 3.2GB (just under 5% of total). Tests keep leaking; free memory falls 3GB -> 400MB -> 50MB, but rounded mem_pct stays 100 so no new system_load message is ever sent. Memory::available keeps seeing the frozen 3.2GB, 3.2GB >= 512MB, so it never defers and the runner keeps launching new tests until the OOM killer fires or forks fail - the exact condition the option was configured to prevent. Same defeat for any pct threshold < 5% and, on the recovery side, memory freed within the top bucket (99%->96%) keeps a bytes-threshold deferral latched until use drops below 95%.
confirmedFindings.proposal: When a metric's rounded bucket is pinned at 100 (or more generally when the configured threshold is finer than the 5% bucket), keep reporting: e.g. always send when the raw value moved past any resource-relevant boundary, add a max-staleness heartbeat (send unconditionally every N seconds), or make the sampler bucket size configurable and/or compare unrounded values near saturation. Alternatively have Resource::Memory treat a snapshot older than a few seconds in the top bucket as saturated.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: The scenario needs one explicit precondition: raw mem_total/mem_available bytes ride along on ANY send, including CPU-triggered ones ($snap carries raw bytes; only the pct fields are replaced with rounded values at Sampler.pm:215-216). So total starvation also requires the CPU bucket to stay flat — plausible under -j32 saturated load since round-up maps every cpu_pct > 95 to bucket 100 and a dip must hold below the bucket for decrease_delay (1s) to send. Intermittent CPU bucket changes would refresh the memory bytes and soften the failure to "stale between CPU-triggered sends". Also note the default 5%-pct threshold is NOT affected: the 95->100 bucket-transition send itself carries mem_available just under 5% of total, which crosses that threshold; only thresholds finer than the 5% bucket (small byte values or pct < 5, and --utilize > 95) are starved. Cited lines are accurate.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Cheap mitigations: (a) add a max-staleness heartbeat in service_tick — send unconditionally if the last send is older than N seconds (a few lines, preserves the change-gating design's chatter goal); (b) or bypass gating whenever the rounded mem bucket is 100 (always-send in the danger band); (c) or have Resource::Memory carry a snapshot timestamp and treat a top-bucket snapshot older than a few seconds as unavailable. No existing TODO_TASKS.md ticket covers this — #23 (~line 983-1027) documents the 5%-bucket change-gating as intentional design and #52 only adds the durable event emission; a fix would need a new ticket or could ride on any future Sampler touch (e.g. the fd/rlimit sampler extension noted near TODO_TASKS.md:1495). Note the secondary recovery-side latch (deferral stuck while memory frees within the 96-100% band, until usage holds below 95% for decrease_delay=1s) is bounded and self-heals; the primary starvation direction is the meaningful one.

So a bytes threshold finer than the 5% bucket (512mb on 64GB = ~0.78%) sees a frozen ~3.2GB free forever and never defers while real free memory collapses — the claimed failure is concrete and reachable.

confirmedFindings.title: JobCount::status_data uses key 'headers' but the base role reads 'header', so the `yath resources` slot table renders with no column header row
confirmedFindings.evidence: JobCount::status_data returns `headers => [qw/Runtime Slots Name/]` (line 119), but Resource::status_lines builds the table with `header => $table->{header}` (Resource.pm line 82), so Term::Table gets header => undef. Verified with the installed Term::Table 0.028: it renders the rows headerless (no croak). Every other resource in this set uses the singular 'header' key.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: User runs `yath resources` (runner renders each resource's status_lines, Runner/Role/Service/Handlers.pm line 926). The JobCount table - the one every run has, since -j is a job limiter - prints rows like `| 42s | 1 | t/foo.t |` and `| -- | 3 | ** FREE ** |` with no Runtime/Slots/Name header row, leaving the columns unlabeled and the output misleading.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Rename the key to `header => [qw/Runtime Slots Name/]` in JobCount::status_data.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Already tracked as TODO_TASKS.md ticket #80 ("Resource JobCount header fix + v5.38/signature normalization", line 1841), whose step 1 is exactly the proposed one-word rename `headers` -> `header` at lib/Test2/Harness2/Runner/Resource/JobCount.pm:119. confirmedFindings.title: UnixLimits nproc gate compares the runner's own /proc/self/status Threads (constant 1 for unthreaded perl) against RLIMIT_NPROC (a per-user process count), so the advertised nproc throttle can never trigger
confirmedFindings.evidence: _dimension_states uses `$status->{Threads} // 0` as the 'current' usage for the nproc dimension (line 468) against the soft cap parsed from '/proc/self/limits' Max processes. RLIMIT_NPROC is enforced at fork() against the real user's total process/thread count, but Threads in /proc/self/status is only this process's thread count - and the runner is a single-threaded Perl process, so it is always 1. free = soft_cap - 1 is effectively the whole cap, so with the default 10% headroom (or any pct) the state is永 'ok'. Conversely an absolute threshold near the cap (e.g. nproc=128 with `ulimit -u 100`) makes it permanently 'low'. Either way the value never tracks actual process pressure from the forked test jobs.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: User with `ulimit -u 4096` runs `yath test -R UnixLimits -j64` on a suite whose tests each fork many children, expecting the documented nproc headroom gate to defer new starts as the user's process count approaches 4096. The gate reads Threads=1 every check, free=4095, never 'low', so yath keeps launching tests until fork() starts failing with EAGAIN across the run (tests error out, possibly the harness's own forks too). The -R UnixLimits nproc protection silently did nothing.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Measure the per-user process/thread count for the nproc dimension (e.g. count `/proc/*/status` entries whose Uid matches, or sum Threads across the user's pids; getrlimit semantics), or drop the nproc dimension until a correct usage source exists rather than shipping a gate that cannot fire.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Scope to the nproc dimension only: line 468 is the defect; nofile (self fd count vs RLIMIT_NOFILE) and as (VmSize vs RLIMIT_AS) are semantically correct per-process comparisons. Two concrete failure modes: (a) default pct threshold -> gate is a permanent no-op (free = soft_cap - 1 always), matching the finding's EAGAIN scenario; (b) count threshold >= soft_cap - 1 -> permanently 'low', throttling the whole run to min_concurrent (default 1) with no indication. Fix options: count the user's tasks (sum Threads across /proc/*/status entries with matching real Uid, matching kernel RLIMIT_NPROC accounting), or drop/deactivate the nproc dimension. Note the defect is inherited verbatim from reference/old3/lib/Test2/Harness2/Resource/UnixLimits.pm line 223 (introduced to this tree in commit 0e93506b0, PR #59), and t/AI/unit/Resource_OSLimits.t only exercises fake_status mocks so no test covers real semantics.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Two failure modes, not one: (a) pct-threshold nproc gate can never trigger (Threads=1 => free ~= cap always), and (b) absolute count threshold near/above cap-1 makes the dimension permanently 'low', throttling every run to min_concurrent=1 — a silent serialization worth calling out since it looks like a harness hang-adjacent slowdown. Module POD (lines 39-48) documents the thread-count sampling, so this is a design defect ported from old3 (#59), not a transcription bug. Cheap mitigations: drop the nproc dimension until a correct per-user metric exists, or sample the user's task count by summing Threads across /proc/[pid]/status entries with matching Uid (one pass per availability check; comparable cost to existing /proc reads). confirmedFindings.title: SubReaper uses syscall 548 for FreeBSD procctl, but SYS_procctl is 544 — subreaper acquisition always fails on FreeBSD
confirmedFindings.evidence: `use constant SYS_procctl_FREEBSD => 548;` but FreeBSD's sys/sys/syscall.h defines `#define SYS_procctl 544` (verified: https://cgit.freebsd.org/src/tree/sys/sys/syscall.h and https://alfonsosiciliano.gitlab.io/posts/2021-01-02-freebsd-system-calls-table.html — 544 procctl; 548 was the removed freebsd11 numa_getaffinity slot, now nosys). The same wrong number is also used for DragonFly, whose syscall numbering differs from FreeBSD entirely. So on FreeBSD/DragonFly, subreaper_supported() returns true but acquire_subreaper() invokes the wrong syscall and returns false (ENOSYS/EINVAL).
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: On FreeBSD, every runner start prints the warning 'could not acquire child-subreaper status: Function not implemented' (Runner::become_subreaper), and detached double-forked preload collectors reparent to init instead of the runner, so the runner's zombie-reaping/health post-pass for reparented collectors (ticket #28 C1) never sees them. A supported platform is silently degraded, contradicting the subreaper_supported()==true report.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Change SYS_procctl_FREEBSD to 544, and give DragonFly its own syscall number (or drop DragonFly from the supported list until its number is tabled) instead of sharing the FreeBSD constant.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: The DragonFly half is worse than the finding states: DragonFly's SYS_procctl is 536 (not just 'different'), syscall 548 there is SYS_wait6 — so on DragonFly the module actually issues wait6(0, $$, (int*)2, 0), failing with EFAULT rather than ENOSYS — and DragonFly's PROC_REAP_ACQUIRE/PROC_REAP_RELEASE are 0x0001/0x0002 versus FreeBSD's 2/3, so the shared cmd constants at SubReaper.pm:19-20 are also wrong for DragonFly. Fixing only the syscall number to 544 fixes FreeBSD but leaves DragonFly broken twice over; the proposal's fallback (drop dragonfly from the line-80 match until given its own number AND cmd constants) is the correct minimal fix.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Cheap fix under existing ticket #28 (TODO_TASKS.md Tier 4, ~lines 601-623): change SYS_procctl_FREEBSD to 544 (one-line edit in lib/Test2/Harness2/Util/SubReaper.pm:21), and either table DragonFly's own SYS_procctl number or remove 'dragonfly' from the OS match at line 80 so it reports unsupported instead of a false-positive subreaper_supported(). #28 already calls for porting 40-subreaper-behavior.t; running it on a FreeBSD CPAN-testers box would have caught this and will verify the fix. DragonFly's misnumbered syscall is eval-guarded and args would EINVAL, so no additional risk there.

acc_verdict.reason: Confirmed end to end. lib/Test2/Harness2/Util/SubReaper.pm:21 hardcodes SYS_procctl_FREEBSD => 548, but FreeBSD's sys/sys/syscall.h (verified against freebsd-src main) defines SYS_procctl as 544; slot 548 is the obsolete numa_getaffinity slot (nosys), so the syscall returns -1/ENOSYS. Since _resolve_platform (lines 80-90) unconditionally reports freebsd/dragonfly as supported, subreaper_supported() is true, Runner.pm:404-415 (become_subreaper, called from process at line 428) passes the guard, acquire_subreaper() always fails, the 'could not acquire child-subreaper status' warning fires on every runner start, and detached double-forked collectors reparent to init instead of the runner — exactly the claimed scenario. The behavior is not intended: the POD explicitly advertises FreeBSD/DragonFly procctl support and the constant is named for FreeBSD's procctl. Non-fatal by design (Runner comments + ARCHITECTURE §5.4 EOF-based completion), so P2 stands.
