Fix is a one-line special-case as proposed (`my $fa = $field eq 'file' ? $ja->{file} : $ta->{$field};` and same for $fb) — cheap to land alongside any other times.pm touch-up (e.g. the log-file-arg/JSONL-scan dedup work already tracked at TODO_TASKS.md:1978-1986 touches this same file/command, a natural place to fold this fix in). No existing TODO_TASKS.md ticket calls out this specific sort bug.

confirmedFindings.title: status/ps numeric-sort pid columns containing 'N/A' spray "isn't numeric" warnings on the terminal
confirmedFindings.evidence: status.pm line 76 sets pid to the string 'N/A' for a down/restarting stage, then line 85 sorts with `$a->[0] <=> $b->[0]`; line 111 sets 'N/A' for running tasks without a reported pid, sorted numerically at line 116. ps.pm does the same at lines 44/49 with the numeric sort at line 57. All three files have `use warnings` enabled, so <=> on 'N/A' emits "Argument \"N/A\" isn't numeric in numeric comparison (<=>)" per comparison.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: User runs `yath status` while any preload stage is down or restarting (routine during reloads), or while a just-dispatched test has not yet reported its pid: the report is interleaved with a stream of Perl 'isn't numeric' warnings on stderr, garbling the tables.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Sort with a numeric fallback, e.g. `sort { ($a->[0] =~ /^\d+$/ ? $a->[0] : -1) <=> ($b->[0] =~ /^\d+$/ ? $b->[0] : -1) }`, or use `no warnings 'numeric'` around the sorts.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Two precision fixes: (1) the warning only fires when the table has 2+ rows (sort never calls the comparator on a single element), which is the normal multi-stage case; (2) in ps.pm the stage loop at line 43 filters to state 'up' stages, which are connected and thus have real pids in stage_pids, so ps.pm's realistic 'N/A' source is the running-tests loop (line 49), not the stage loop at line 44.

confirmedFindings.title: speedtag: invalid max_medium argument dies with a message blaming max_short (and printing the medium value)
confirmedFindings.evidence: Line 100 checks MAX_SHORT with message 'max short duration...'; line 101 checks MAX_MEDIUM but the die string still says "max short duration must be an integer, got '$self->{+MAX_MEDIUM}'".
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: User runs `yath speedtag log.jsonl 15 abc`: the command dies with "max short duration must be an integer, got 'abc'" even though the short value (15) was valid — the user is pointed at the wrong argument.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Change line 101's message to "max medium duration must be an integer, got '...'".
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Trivial one-line fix: change line 101's die string from "max short duration..." to "max medium duration...". No functional risk in landing this fix; pure string correction, safe to batch with other cosmetic fixes.

confirmedFindings.title: yath ps never attaches the runner pid to the client, so a transient socket connect failure is treated as runner-gone and ps silently prints an empty process list
confirmedFindings.evidence: ps.pm run() reads pfile_data (line 31) but, unlike its parent status.pm (which does `$self->client->attach_runner($data->{pid})` before `$self->client->status`), never calls attach_runner. App::Yath2::Client::runner_gone returns 1 when RUNNER_PID is unset (`my $pid = $self->{+RUNNER_PID} or return 1;`), so the submitter's liveness_check reports 'gone' on ANY failed first connect attempt in Runner::Client::connection, which sets RUNNER_GONE and makes status() return undef instead of retrying; ps then does `$status // {}` and renders empty tables.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: Runner is alive but the initial connect_unix fails once (e.g. accept backlog full on a busy runner, or the runner exits/restarts in the window after Pfile->find's liveness probe): `yath ps` prints the 'Found:' banner, then an empty '**** Running Processes ****' table and exits 0, telling the user nothing is running while stages and tests are active. status.pm in the same situation retries up to 30s because the attached pid keeps liveness true.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Add `$self->client->attach_runner($data->{pid});` before the status call, matching status.pm/abort.pm.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Two corrections to the failure_scenario: (1) the 'accept backlog full' trigger is wrong — t2clib/Test2/Collector/Util/Socket.pm:29-33 documents that a blocking AF_UNIX connect to a full accept queue BLOCKS (unix_wait_for_peer) rather than failing, so that case cannot produce the failed connect_unix; (2) the 'runner exits after Pfile->find's probe' sub-case shows no divergence — with the runner truly dead, an attached status.pm's kill(0) also reports gone and prints the same empty tables. The actual divergence window is a transient connect failure while the runner is ALIVE (e.g. EINTR, transient EMFILE, socket teardown/rebind race), which the attach-based retry loop would ride out for up to 30s but ps abandons on the first attempt. Narrower than stated, consistent with P3.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Agree with the original P3. This is a real, reachable one-line gap (missing `attach_runner` call, inconsistent with sibling commands status.pm and abort.pm) but the failure requires a narrow race — a connect failure occurring in the brief window between App::Yath2::Pfile->find()'s own liveness-verified connect and ps's status connect, since without an attached pid the client's connection() loop has zero retry tolerance (fails fast on the very first bad attempt instead of looping until CONNECT_TIMEOUT). Blast radius is limited to a purely informational, exit-0 command (`yath ps`) silently showing an empty process list; no hang, no orphaned processes, no wrong test outcomes, and the user can simply re-run `yath ps`. Cheap fix: add `$self->client->attach_runner($data->{pid});` before the status call in ps.pm, matching status.pm/abort.pm exactly (1-line change, no new tests needed beyond a smoke check that ps still lists processes). Not found in TODO_TASKS.md as a tracked item as of this review.

confirmedFindings.title: speedtag rewrites test source files in place non-atomically with unchecked writes — interruption or disk-full truncates the user's test file
confirmedFindings.evidence: Line 164 reopens the test file with open($fh,'>',...) which truncates it to zero immediately, then line 169 `print $fh @lines;` and line 170 `close($fh);` — neither print nor close return values are checked, and there is no write-to-temp + rename.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: User runs `yath speedtag log.jsonl` over a large suite and hits Ctrl-C mid-run, or the disk/quota fills during the print: the test file currently being tagged is left zero-length or partially written (print/close failure only produces silence, not even a warning), permanently destroying test source that may not be committed.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Write the new content to "$file.tmp$$" checking print/close returns, then rename() over the original (atomic on the same filesystem); warn and skip on any failure.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Minor additions: due to stdio buffering the ENOSPC failure often surfaces only at close(), so checking print alone is insufficient — the proposal's check-both-print-and-close plus rename() is the right fix. Also note line 178 unconditionally reports success ("Tagged '$dur': ...") after the unchecked write, so corruption is reported as success, not merely silence. The pattern is inherited verbatim from legacy Test2-Harness 1.x speedtag (legacy parity, not deliberate design).
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Trigger requires an unusual condition coinciding with the narrow print/close window (operator Ctrl-C, or disk/quota exhaustion) during a maintenance-style command that isn't part of routine `yath test` runs or CI's hot path — so P0/P1 (common-path) framing doesn't fit, but this is more than theoretical: Ctrl-C during a large-suite speedtag run and CI disk-full are both realistic, and the consequence (silent, unrecoverable truncation of a user's test file, possibly uncommitted) is severe enough that P3 undersells it. P2 (edge case needing unusual conditions, real impact) is the better fit. Cheap mitigation matches the proposal exactly: write to `$file.tmp$$`, check print/close return values, `rename()` over the original (atomic on same filesystem), warn+skip on any failure — this is a small, self-contained, low-risk fix. No existing TODO_TASKS.md entry found covering this file specifically (not checked exhaustively).

confirmedFindings.title: Infinite git-spawning loop in _changed_diff when change base is invalid or history unrelated
confirmedFindings.evidence: `$from .= "^" while system($cmd => 'merge-base', '--is-ancestor', $from, $base);` — system() returns nonzero both when $from is not an ancestor AND when git errors (exit 128 for a bad revision). Once the HEAD^^...^ chain walks past the root commit, every further `git merge-base` invocation is a fatal 'bad revision' error (nonzero forever), so the while loop never terminates. Nothing bounds the loop or distinguishes exit 1 (not ancestor) from exit 128 (error).
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: User runs `yath test --changed-only --changes-plugin Git --git-change-base <typo-or-unrelated-branch>` (nonexistent ref, or a branch with an orphan/unrelated root). The loop appends '^' forever, forking a `git merge-base` process on every iteration and spamming 'fatal: bad revision' to stderr; yath never starts any tests and spins until killed.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Capture the exit status: stop (and die with a clear message) when git exits with anything other than 1, and/or bound the loop by the commit depth (`git rev-list --count HEAD`). Validate $base with `git rev-parse --verify` before looping.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Two refinements: (1) kind is nominally 'busy-spin' but each iteration forks git and blocks in waitpid, so it is an infinite fork-per-iteration loop rather than a pure CPU spin — the hang-forever effect is as described. (2) The failure scenario is broader than a typo or orphan branch: shallow clones (git clone --depth N, common in CI) hit the same infinite loop with a perfectly valid --git-change-base, because HEAD^..^ past the shallow boundary is a bad revision (exit 128). The exact loop line is 130.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Keep as documented (severity note: consider bumping stated severity from P1 to P0 since this is an unbounded busy-spin/hang, not just wrong output -- it fits the P0 bucket by the review's own rubric). Cheap fix is straightforward and low-risk, good candidate to land in passing per the finding's own proposal: check `$?` after `system()` and distinguish exit code 1 (not-an-ancestor, keep looping) from any other nonzero exit (git error -- die with a clear message), and/or bound the loop via `git rev-list --count HEAD` or validate $base up front with `git rev-parse --verify $base` before entering the loop. No existing TODO_TASKS.md entry found for this specific issue via a quick grep; worth filing if not already tracked.

confirmedFindings.title: --notify-email-fail alone never registers the Notify plugin, so failure emails are silently never sent
confirmedFindings.evidence: The post_process registers the plugin only inside `if (@{$settings->notify->email} || $settings->notify->email_owner) {...}` (and the slack block). The 1.0 reference (reference/pre_ai_2.0/lib/App/Yath/Renderer/Notify.pm:121) had `@{$settings->notify->email} || @{$settings->notify->email_fail} || $settings->notify->email_owner` — the port dropped the email_fail term. The slack side still checks slack_fail, only email_fail was lost. Nothing else pushes __PACKAGE__ into harness->plugins.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: User runs `yath test --notify-email-fail dev@example.com t/` without --notify-email or --notify-email-owner. The condition is false, the plugin instance is never pushed onto harness->plugins, handle_event/finish never run, and no email is ever sent for failing tests — silently, with no warning (Email::Stuffer availability is not even checked).
confirmedFindings.proposal: Include `@{$settings->notify->email_fail}` in the email-enable condition, matching the reference implementation.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Fix detail: naively adding email_fail to the line-112 condition would also trigger line 113's auto-enable of email_owner, so --notify-email-fail alone would additionally send owner emails (1.0 did not auto-enable owner there). Register the plugin and check Email::Stuffer when email_fail is set, without forcing email_owner on. Scenario scope: the documented SYNOPSIS combo (--notify-email-fail with --notify-email-owner) works; only email_fail used alone is silently dead, as the finding states.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Cheap one-line fix: change condition to `if (@{$settings->notify->email} || @{$settings->notify->email_fail} || $settings->notify->email_owner)`, matching the already-correct slack branch pattern (`$use_slack ||= grep { @{$settings->notify->$_} } qw/slack slack_fail/`) three lines below. No TODO_TASKS.md entry found for this; should be filed/fixed directly since it's a trivial single-line change with an obvious reference pattern already in the same sub.

confirmedFindings.title: Interactive mode's quiet/verbose overrides run after Display has already resolved renderers, so `yath test -qi` produces no output at all
confirmedFindings.evidence: Post-processes run in ascending weight (Instance.pm: `sort { $a <=> $b } keys %{$self->{+POSTS}}`). Display's weight-100 post deletes the Formatter renderer when quiet is set (`delete $renderers->{'Test2::Harness2::Renderer::Formatter'}; @{$renderers->{'@'}} = grep ...`) and freezes quiet/verbose into the formatter args. _post_process_interactive runs at 99998 and only then does `$display->create_option(quiet => 0)` / `create_option(verbose => 1)` — too late: the renderer list and formatter args are already final and nothing re-adds the Formatter or re-captures the args.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: User runs `yath test -q -i t/prompting.t`. Interactive mode's stated contract (comments: output 'must stream while a test prompts', -v ON, quiet OFF) is not delivered: the Formatter renderer was already removed at weight 100, so the session shows nothing — the test's prompt is invisible and the run looks hung while it blocks on STDIN. Similarly, plain `-i` never actually gets verbose formatter output (show_job_launch stays off) because weight-90/100 already consumed verbose=0.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Apply the interactive display/formatter overrides at a weight below 90 (e.g. a dedicated early post that only fixes quiet/verbose/live/qvf), leaving the fork itself at 99998; or have the weight-100/90 posts consult debug->interactive directly.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: The plain `-i` sub-claim is overstated: Renderer::Formatter::init (Formatter.pm:57) reads verbose from live settings at construction time — after the 99998 post has set verbose=1 — so plain `-i` DOES get verbose formatter output. What stays stale are the renderer-level flags frozen into the weight-100 args array: show_job_launch (weight-90 saw verbose=0, so it stayed 0) and show_job_info/show_run_info. Also the args freeze includes quiet/verbose/progress/color/show_times captured pre-override. The hard failure is only the -q + -i combination (Formatter removed entirely); plain -i is a milder inconsistency (missing job-launch/info lines, not missing output). Proposal stands: apply the interactive quiet/verbose/live/qvf overrides at a weight below 90, or have the 90/100 posts consult debug->interactive directly.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Impact is two-tiered, matching the audit's P2: (1) plain `-i` (the primary/common way to use interactive mode) silently loses the documented -v/show_job_launch escalation — a real but low-visibility deviation from spec, no crash, no hang, tests still run and stdin still forwards; (2) `-q -i` together is a rarer, user-opted-in combination that produces genuinely confusing 'no output while blocked on stdin' behavior (looks hung but isn't — it resumes once the user notices and types into the prompt), which alone would be closer to P1 but requires the user to deliberately pair quiet with interactive, an uncommon combo. No forward-progress loss, no data loss, no orphaned processes — just wrong/missing display output. Cheap fix as proposed: move the interactive display/formatter overrides (quiet/verbose/live/qvf) into their own post-process registered at a weight below 90 (leaving only the fork/stdin-handoff logic at 99998), or have the weight-90/100 posts consult settings->debug->interactive directly. No existing TODO_TASKS.md ticket found covering this specific ordering bug (ticket #77 in TODO_TASKS.md is an unrelated 'Preload dead code' item — the audit's finding id 77 does not correspond to that ticket number).

confirmedFindings.title: Git.pm git_output can deadlock: stderr pipe is only drained after stdout EOF and waitpid
confirmedFindings.evidence: The parent blocks in `my $line = <$rh>` (stdout, blocking) and later in `waitpid($pid, 0)`, and only reads the stderr pipe ($irh) after waitpid returns. If the git child writes more than the pipe capacity (~64KB) to stderr before closing stdout, the child blocks in write(2) on the full stderr pipe while the parent blocks reading stdout (no EOF because the child is alive holding it) — a classic two-pipe deadlock. $irh being non-blocking does not help since it is never read during the loop.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: `yath test --changed-only` in a repo where `git diff -U1000000 -W --minimal HEAD` (or `git status -s`) emits >64KB of stderr (e.g. thousands of CRLF/embedded-repo warnings). git blocks on stderr, yath blocks forever in readline/waitpid — the whole run hangs before any test starts.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Drain both pipes with select() (or read stderr non-blocking inside the line loop), or use Capture::Tiny like reference/pre_ai_2.0/lib/App/Yath/Plugin/Git.pm does.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Two minor precision fixes: (1) the parent's terminal blocking point is the readline at Git.pm:43, not waitpid — waitpid (line 48) is unreachable until stdout EOF, which never comes; (2) exposure is broader than the stated --changed-only scenario: inject_run_data (called from Test2::Harness2::Run.pm:60) invokes git_output for rev-parse/status -s on every run with the Git plugin enabled, so any git command emitting >pipe-capacity stderr before exit hangs the run. Proposal stands: drain both pipes with select() or read stderr non-blocking inside the line loop.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Original P2 severity stands: it is a genuine hang/deadlock class bug (not refuted — the trigger is possible under supported configurations, just needs unusual stderr volume from git), but it needs unusual conditions (large stderr output, e.g. bulk CRLF/embedded-repo warnings on `git diff -U1000000 -W --minimal` under --git-change-base, or an oddly noisy `git status -s`) rather than being hit on the common default path (plain `rev-parse`/`status` invocations rarely produce >64KB of stderr). Cheap mitigation: drain both $rh and $irh inside the read loop via select()/non-blocking reads (or switch to Capture::Tiny as reference/pre_ai_2.0/lib/App/Yath/Plugin/Git.pm already does) — trivial fix, no existing TODO_TASKS.md ticket covers this specific deadlock (only unrelated Git.pm dedup/style-guide entries exist at TODO_TASKS.md:1857 and :2129-2132).

confirmedFindings.title: Explicit --no-notify-email-owner / --no-notify-slack-owner are silently overridden back to ON
confirmedFindings.evidence: `$settings->notify->option(email_owner => 1) unless $settings->notify->email_owner;` (and the slack_owner twin at line 133). The comment claims a Bool default-0 'can only be turned ON via the CLI', but `--no-notify-email-owner` is also CLI and leaves the value 0, which this line then forces to 1. The 1.0 reference instead used a default sub (`default => sub { return 1 if @{$settings->notify->email}; 0 }`, Renderer/Notify.pm:87-94), which respects an explicit --no- flag.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: User runs `yath test --notify-email boss@x.com --no-notify-email-owner` precisely because they do NOT want test owners (HARNESS-META-OWNER addresses) spammed. post_process flips email_owner back to 1 and owner emails are sent anyway; same for `--notify-slack '#chan' --no-notify-slack-owner`.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Port the reference semantics: make owner flags default subs keyed off email/slack lists instead of force-setting them in post_process, or track set-ness via check_option before the initialize pass.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Minor broadening: the slack_owner override fires whenever any of slack_url, slack, or slack_fail is set (Notify.pm:122-124), so even `--notify-slack-fail '#chan' --no-notify-slack-owner` (without --notify-slack) hits it. Otherwise the finding's lines, evidence, and scenario are accurate as written.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Trigger requires an unusual but deliberate combo: user must actively pass --notify-email/--notify-slack AND explicitly try to suppress owner notification with --no-notify-*-owner in the same invocation — most yath users never touch the Notify plugin at all, and of those who do, most don't also try to opt owners out. So it's real, user-visible wrong behavior (unwanted emails/Slack pings to test owners after an explicit opt-out — a privacy/annoyance issue, not data loss or a hang) but gated behind a specific flag combination rather than arising in normal/default use, keeping it at P2 rather than P1. Cheap fix matches the proposal: track set-ness via a default sub keyed off the email/slack list (as 1.0's Renderer/Notify.pm:87-94 did) instead of force-setting in post_process, or check_option's set-by-cli source if Getopt::Yath exposes one. No existing TODO_TASKS.md item found covering this specifically.

confirmedFindings.title: -f/--fields name:details regex is unanchored and truncates details at the second colon
confirmedFindings.evidence: `if ($raw =~ m/([^:]+):([^:]+)/) { return {name => $1, details => $2}; }` — no anchors, and [^:]+ stops at the next colon, so any details value containing ':' is silently truncated; trailing garbage is silently accepted instead of hitting the `die "'$raw' is not a valid field specification"` guard.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: `yath test -f build_url:https://ci.example.com/42` stores {name => 'build_url', details => 'https'} — the URL is silently destroyed in the run metadata/log/DB; the user only notices later when the field is useless.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Anchor and make details greedy across colons: `m/^([^:]+):(.+)$/s`.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Cheap fix confirmed correct: anchor and make details greedy, e.g. `m/^([^:]+):(.+)$/s` (matches the finding's own proposal). No existing TODO_TASKS.md entry tracks this specific regex; the nearby TODO_TASKS.md #58/TestFile entries (lines ~1792-1798) are unrelated stale-code items in a different file, so this would need its own tracked fix.

confirmedFindings.title: --cover-from-type is never read: type/parser hint silently ignored for --cover-from (and maybe_from_type does not default to it)
confirmedFindings.evidence: get_coverage_tests builds type_data only for the maybe path (`_deduce_content_type($maybe, $cover->maybe_from_type)` line 365); the from path calls `_get_coverage_tests($settings, $changes, $from)` with no type_data (line 374), so `$cover->from_type` has zero consumers in the codebase (grep confirms). The maybe_from_type description promises 'Defaults to from_type if that is specified' — also not implemented. Inherited verbatim from reference/pre_ai_2.0 Cover.pm but still a silent no-op option.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: User runs `yath test --cover-from http://example.com/coverage --cover-from-type json`. The Content-Type header/parser hint is never applied; stream_json_l auto-detects (or mis-detects) the format for a URL with no extension, so the documented override does nothing and coverage-based test selection fails or misparses with no indication the flag was ignored.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Compute `_deduce_content_type($from, $cover->from_type)` for the from path and pass it through; default maybe_from_type to from_type per its own description.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Impact is slightly narrower than the scenario implies: type_data's only concrete effect anywhere is the outgoing HTTP request Content-Type header for URL sources — coverage_handler binds $type_data but never uses it, and stream_json_l_file ignores type hints entirely (parser chosen by file extension, croaks on others at JSON.pm:97). Also stream_json_l_url always parses responses line-by-line as JSONL regardless of headers (JSON.pm:128-140), so the "misparses" outcome for an extensionless URL happens with or without the flag, and the proposal's header pass-through alone won't change client-side parsing — a complete fix must also honor the parser/format hint in the stream layer (and in stream_json_l_file for local paths). Silent no-op documented option; P3 ux stands.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Upgrade severity from P3 to P2 (not P3): the option is real, documented CLI surface, not dead code, and the failure mode (silent misparse of coverage source under --cover-from, silently ignored --cover-from-type override) is concretely triggerable by normal use of the --cover-from feature with an ambiguous/extensionless source -- it just requires opting into coverage-based test selection, which is not the default/common path for most yath invocations. Cheap fix matches the finding's own proposal: compute _deduce_content_type($from, $cover->from_type) in the non-maybe branch (line 374) and pass type_data through, plus default maybe_from_type to from_type per its documented description (line 99). No related TODO_TASKS.md entry found for this specific item.

confirmedFindings.title: Git _changed_diff HEAD^ fallback is unreachable: _diff_from always returns a truthy 2-element list
confirmedFindings.evidence: `my @files = $class->_diff_from($from); return @files if @files; return $class->_diff_from("${from}^");` — _diff_from returns `(line_sub => $class->git_output(...))`, a 2-element list, regardless of whether the diff has any content (the diff is read lazily by Finder's line_sub consumer, Finder.pm:440). So `@files` is always true whenever git exists and the ${from}^ fallback is dead code; the emptiness check the code implies (fall back to the last commit when the working tree is clean) can never trigger.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: User commits their changes and runs `yath test --changed-only` (no --git-change-base) on a clean tree. `git diff HEAD` is empty, Finder's changes_from_diff finds nothing, and yath runs zero tests, instead of falling back to the HEAD^ diff (the just-made commit) as the fallback branch intends.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Make the emptiness check real: peek the first line from the line_sub (or run the diff eagerly enough to know it is empty) before deciding, then fall back to ${from}^.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Failure mode correction: on a clean tree with --changed-only, yath does not silently run zero tests; Finder.pm:376 dies with "Could not find any changed files.\n" when no changes are found, so the user gets a fatal abort instead of the intended HEAD^ (last-commit) fallback. Workaround exists (--git-change-base HEAD^). Bug is inherited unchanged from legacy 1.x. Fix per proposal: determine diff emptiness eagerly (peek first line of the line_sub, pushing it back via a wrapper) before choosing between HEAD and HEAD^.
confirmedFindings.severity_note:
Bump from P3 to P2: the trigger isn't theoretical/dead-config, it's the default code path (no --git-change-base) hit on any clean-tree run of a coverage-backed --changed-only invocation, e.g. a post-commit CI/hook workflow — a real usage pattern, just gated behind an already-narrow feature (Git plugin + coverage data source + --changed-only). Impact is silent under-selection (0 tests instead of last commit's tests), no crash/error, so it stays below P1's typical bar but is more than purely latent. Cheap fix: replace the `@files ? @files : fallback` truthiness check with an actual emptiness probe — e.g. run `git diff --quiet HEAD` (or peek the first line yielded by line_sub) before deciding whether to fall back to `${from}^`, per the finding's own proposal. Did not find an existing TODO_TASKS.md entry specifically for this Git.pm fallback logic.</parameter>
</invoke>

confirmedFindings.title: job_count from env vars bypasses the '8:2' reshaping trigger (fires only on action 'set')
confirmedFindings.evidence: The job_count trigger begins `return unless $params{action} eq 'set';`, but env-sourced values (YATH_JOB_COUNT/T2_HARNESS_JOB_COUNT/HARNESS_JOB_COUNT via from_env_vars) are delivered through get_initial_value with action 'initialize' (Getopt::Yath::Instance line 239). Compare the utilize trigger just below, which deliberately handles both 'set' and 'initialize'. So an env value '8:2' is never split: job_count stays the literal string '8:2', slots_per_job stays 1, and jobs_post_process exports T2_HARNESS_MY_JOB_COUNT='8:2'.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: `YATH_JOB_COUNT=8:2 yath test`: fix_job_resources compares '8:2' numerically (Perl 'isn't numeric' warnings), the scheduler treats job_count as 8 but each test gets 1 slot instead of the requested 2 (double the intended concurrency pressure), and children see T2_HARNESS_MY_JOB_COUNT='8:2'.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Handle action 'initialize' in the job_count trigger (like utilize does), or do the ':' split in a normalize sub which applies to both paths.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Line cite: jobs_post_process/fix_job_resources span ~625-659, with the failing numeric comparison (die "$job_slots > $run_slots") at line 658, not 613-640. Otherwise the finding is exact as written.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Original P3 undersells this slightly: the colon syntax is explicitly advertised in the option's own long_examples/short_examples (' 8:2'), so it's a documented, not obscure, feature -- just one that's much more commonly exercised via CLI (-j8:2, which correctly hits action='set') than via env var. Bumping to P2 because the trigger asymmetry (utilize handles both 'set' and 'initialize', job_count doesn't) is a straightforward oversight with a one-line fix: change `return unless $params{action} eq 'set';` to `return unless $params{action} eq 'set' || $params{action} eq 'initialize';` (matching the utilize trigger pattern already in the same file), or better, factor the ':' split into a shared normalize sub as the finding's own proposal suggests. Did not find an existing TODO_TASKS.md entry for this specific issue. Cheap, low-risk fix; worth taking in passing given the proposal is already spelled out.

confirmedFindings.title: --logger-lastlog symlink creation failure is silently swallowed
confirmedFindings.evidence: `unlink($link) if -l $link || -e $link; eval { symlink($path, $link); 1 };` — the eval result and symlink's return value are both discarded, and unlink's failure is also unchecked. If symlink fails (filesystem without symlink support, permissions, or a race where another process recreates $link between unlink and symlink → EEXIST), the previous lastlog.sqlite has already been deleted and no replacement exists, with no warning.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: User logs to a directory on a filesystem where symlink() fails (or two concurrent yath runs race on lastlog.sqlite). The old lastlog.sqlite is unlinked, the new symlink silently fails, and later tooling pointed at lastlog.sqlite finds nothing — the user explicitly asked for --logger-lastlog and gets no link and no diagnostic.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Check the symlink return and warn on failure (`symlink($path,$link) or warn "Could not create lastlog symlink '$link': $!"`); consider symlink-to-temp-name + rename for atomic replacement.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Minor precision fix only: the operative lines are 240-241 (unlink + eval'd symlink), and what is lost on failure is the lastlog.sqlite pointer, not the prior log data itself. The eval exists to survive platforms where symlink() dies as unimplemented, but even that case should produce a one-time warning since the user explicitly passed --logger-lastlog.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Cheap fix matches the finding's own proposal: `symlink($path, $link) or warn "Could not create lastlog symlink '$link': $!";` also check unlink's return similarly. No existing TODO_TASKS.md entry covers this specific fix (grep for lastlog/symlink only shows unrelated preload-socket and runner-link items), so it would need its own small ticket/fix if desired. Worth noting the finding's failure_scenario slightly overstates impact by implying the old lastlog data is deleted — since lastlog.sqlite is itself a symlink, only the pointer is lost, not the underlying dated sqlite log; the actual test data remains recoverable from the timestamped file.

confirmedFindings.title: DB sync is not transactional: an interrupted sync leaves a permanently incomplete run that all future syncs skip
confirmedFindings.evidence: _sync_one_run inserts the dest runs row first ($dest->handle('runs')->insert($row), line 279), then copies jobs/tries/collectors/artifacts with no transaction. The idempotency guard at lines 266-269 short-circuits the ENTIRE run ('$self->{+STATS}{skipped_runs}++; return;') whenever the runs row already exists on the dest, never reaching the per-table next-if-exists checks in _sync_jobs/_sync_tries/_sync_collectors/_sync_artifacts.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: `yath db sync --from a.sqlite --to dbi:Pg:dbname=yath` dies mid-run (Ctrl-C, network drop, disk full, or a constraint error on one artifact) after the runs row was inserted but before jobs/artifacts finished. Re-running the sync prints 'skipped 1 already-present run(s)' and returns success; the run's jobs, tries, and event blobs are missing from the destination forever, with no way to repair short of manually deleting the dest runs row.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Either wrap each run's copy in a destination transaction (rollback on die), or drop the run-level short-circuit and always descend into _sync_jobs/_sync_collectors/_sync_artifacts (they already skip existing child rows), counting skipped_runs only for the runs-row insert.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Scenario and lines are precise. One nuance: children copied before the crash do persist (per-row guards would skip them on a repaired descent), so the loss is exactly the not-yet-copied jobs/tries/collectors/artifacts. The proposal's second option (drop the run-level short-circuit and always descend; count skipped_runs only when the runs-row insert is skipped) is safe as-is because all four child syncs already have per-UUID exists-checks; a dest-side transaction per run (QuickORM txn) is also available and would additionally cover the runs-row/children gap atomically.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: No existing TODO_TASKS.md ticket addresses this specific gap; #53 (line 1278) designed the original sync engine but doesn't call out transactionality, and the DB-layer cleanup ticket at line 2016 (dedup/consolidation) does not touch this correctness issue either -- this needs its own fix, not a byproduct of an existing ticket. Cheap mitigation matches the finding's own proposal: wrap each per-run copy (lines 279-286) in a destination transaction with rollback-on-die (if the QuickORM/DBI dest handle supports transactions), OR simplify by dropping the run-row short-circuit at 266-269 and always descending into _sync_jobs/_sync_collectors/_sync_artifacts, which already contain per-row skip-if-exists guards (see e.g. line 302) -- only increment skipped_runs based on the runs-row insert outcome. The second option is lower-risk (no transaction API dependency across sqlite/Pg/DuckDB) and should be preferred if DuckDB's transaction support is inconsistent with the other flavors (per project memory: DuckDB has single-writer/lock quirks).

confirmedFindings.title: DB logger always stalls the full 30s DRAIN_TIMEOUT on a persistent runner because global service collectors (sampler/preload-root) never finalize
confirmedFindings.evidence: _all_finalized_imported iterates ALL of $mon->collectors and returns 0 unless every one is 'finalized'. The run-scoped subscriber snapshot includes global-bucket collectors (Monitor::snapshot line 374: '$collectors{$uuid} = $c if !defined($run) || $run eq $run_id'), and the runner unconditionally spawns the always-on sampler collector (Runner.pm line 470) plus preload-root; those service collectors stay status 'running' until the RUNNER shuts down, which on the persistent path never happens per run. So after run_done the drain loop can never exit via _all_finalized_imported and only ends at '(time - $drain_started) > DRAIN_TIMEOUT' (30s). The transient path escapes only because the runner closes the socket. Additionally _upsert_collectors stamps those global collectors with THIS run's run_uuid, misattributing shared services to whichever run's logger inserted first.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: User runs `yath run -L results.sqlite` against a persistent runner (`yath start`). Tests finish, run_done is announced, all test blobs are imported within milliseconds — yet the logger keeps polling for a fixed 30 seconds every single run, and the command's wait_for_loggers blocks on the logger pid, so every persistent run with -L appears to hang ~30s after completion.
confirmedFindings.proposal: In _all_finalized_imported, only require finalized+imported for collectors belonging to this run (skip collectors whose run_uuid is undef / ne RUN_ID), or restrict the wait to $mon->tests.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Precision fixes only: this is a bounded stall, not an unbounded hang — the drain loop exits at exactly DRAIN_TIMEOUT=30s and the command-side wait_for_loggers is capped at 120s; the loop also sleeps POLL_DELAY=0.02s per iteration (no busy spin). preload-root is spawned only when _preload_root_wanted (preloads configured), but the sampler alone is unconditional and sufficient to hold _all_finalized_imported false. The proposed fix should skip collectors whose monitor-tracked run_uuid is undef or ne RUN_ID in BOTH _all_finalized_imported and _upsert_collectors (the latter to fix the run_uuid misattribution of shared service collectors).

confirmedFindings.title: Watchdog-aborted jobs are never folded: their try stays 'running' with a NULL verdict and the run is logged 'complete' without the failure
confirmedFindings.evidence: The logger derives try verdicts solely from the collector's final_state (_upsert_tries/_try_columns) and _collector_status maps only finalized/complete->'complete', else 'running'. A watchdog abort (Runner/Watchdog.pm line 196: announce_job($job_id,'aborted',...)) is a harness_runner_job mutation for a job 'whose collector will never report completion' — no final_state ever arrives. The logger never consumes job state 'aborted' or new_aborted_jobs, so the job_tries row keeps status='running', result=NULL; _finalize_run_row skips unresolved jobs (line 607 'next unless $resolved') and then unconditionally writes status 'complete' with counts that exclude the aborted job.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: A test hangs, the runner watchdog aborts it, the run finishes and the renderer correctly shows a failure — but the -L database records the run as status='complete' with the hung job's passed/failed NULL, its try forever 'running', and run failed-count not including it. Anyone querying the DB sees a clean-looking run that actually contained a hung/aborted test.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Fold monitor job state 'aborted' (or drain new_aborted_jobs) into the try/job rows: result=0, status='broken', count the job as failed in _finalize_run_row.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: The trigger surface is narrower than "a test hangs, the watchdog aborts it". A hung test tripped by its own event/exit timeout is terminated by the collector itself, which finalizes normally with a failing final_state (t2clib/Test2/Collector.pm:610-628,793-853), and even runner-driven terminates (bail / yath abort / owner-drop with live collectors) normally produce a finalize — the DB records those correctly. The genuinely broken cases are watchdog aborts with no collector finalize: (1) abort_job on a failed dispatch to a dead stage — no collector ever exists, so the job has NO job_tries row and is skipped by Logger.pm:591 `next unless @tries` (not line 607), leaving jobs.passed/failed NULL; (2) wind-down/run-timeout/owner-drop aborts of jobs whose stage or collector died without finalizing; (3) the pid hard-kill grace fallback for a non-complying collector. Proposal stands: fold Monitor job state 'aborted' (or drain new_aborted_jobs) into try/job rows as failed and count them in _finalize_run_row — and also handle the no-try-row case at line 591, not just the NULL-result case at line 607.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Upgrading from the original P2 to P1: the trigger conditions (yath abort, owner-disconnect, mid-run stage death, dispatch-vs-teardown race) are all designed, expected operational events for a persistent runner/CI setup, not rare edge cases, and the resulting DB corruption (status='complete' hiding an aborted job with NULL verdict, run counts excluding it) is silent and permanent — nothing later reconciles it. No existing TODO_TASKS.md entry appears to cover fixing the DB logger's handling of aborted jobs specifically (the related TODO_TASKS.md:1643-1652 entry is about a *renderer*-side double-launch-line bug for the same watchdog-aborted path, a different defect in the same area — worth fixing in the same pass but does not address the DB logger gap). Cheap mitigation matching the finding's own proposal: fold monitor 'aborted' job state (or drain new_aborted_jobs) into `_collector_status`/`_try_columns` as status='broken', result=0, and make `_finalize_run_row` count it as resolved/failed rather than skipping it.

confirmedFindings.title: Run finalized as 'complete' (and logger exits 0) even when the runner died mid-run or the drain timed out with unimported blobs
confirmedFindings.evidence: In _run, the socket-EOF branch (line 203) and the DRAIN_TIMEOUT expiry (line 215) both fall through to _finalize_run_row, where line 619 sets $status = TERMINAL_ERROR ? 'broken' : 'complete'. Neither an EOF before run_done (runner crash/kill) nor a drain timeout (blobs left unimported) sets TERMINAL_ERROR, and per-collector import failures recorded via _record_error only warn — run() (line 174) returns 0 unless TERMINAL_ERROR. Separately, if _run dies mid-loop (e.g. a DB write error in _sync), _finalize_run_row is never reached and the run row is left status='running' forever.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: kill -9 the transient runner mid-run: the logger sees the socket close, does one final sync, and writes runs.status='complete' with partial pass/fail counts — the DB reports a completed run that never finished. Or: import of one collector blob fails (corrupt events file); the logger warns to a detached stderr, marks the run 'complete', and exits 0, so nothing signals the log is incomplete.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Track whether run_done was actually observed and whether all imports succeeded; write 'broken' (or 'canceled') on EOF-before-run_done and on drain-timeout/import errors, and return a nonzero exit when errors were recorded. Call _finalize_run_row from run()'s failure path too.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Two precision notes: (a) the die-mid-loop case DOES exit nonzero (run() returns 1 on TERMINAL_ERROR); the exit-0 complaint applies only to the _record_error-only paths (EOF-before-run_done, drain timeout, import failures). (b) The EOF branch's final _sync can absorb a run_done transition that arrived in the same batch as the EOF, but that does not help the crash case where run_done was never emitted.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Bump from P2 to P1: both trigger paths are ordinary operational events (process killed/crashed mid-run; transient DB error during sync), not unusual conditions, and the consequence is a persisted run-status that silently lies (complete-with-partial-data and exit 0, or stuck-running-forever) which can mislead CI gating/dashboards that key off runs.status. Proposal in the finding (track run_done-observed + import-success, call _finalize_run_row from run()'s failure path too, return nonzero when errors recorded) is a correct and cheap fix; no existing TODO_TASKS.md entry found covering this specific gap.

confirmedFindings.title: ensure_sqlite_db bootstrap is non-atomic: concurrent first-open crashes, and an interrupted bootstrap leaves a permanently broken DB file
confirmedFindings.evidence: The existence check is 'return $path if -e $path && -s _' followed by connect + _load_ddl with no locking and no IF NOT EXISTS in the DDL (share/schema/SQLite/log.sql uses plain CREATE TABLE). Two processes racing the first creation both pass the check and both run the DDL; with RaiseError=1 the loser dies on 'table ... already exists'. Worse, a bootstrap interrupted mid-DDL (Ctrl-C, crash) leaves a non-empty partial file that passes the -s check on every subsequent open, so the DDL is never re-applied.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: Two `yath test -L ~/shared/results.sqlite` runs start simultaneously against a not-yet-existing file: one logger dies with a duplicate-table error and that run's log is lost. Or a first run is Ctrl-C'd during bootstrap: every later run against that path fails with 'no such table: runs' until the user manually deletes the half-built file.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Bootstrap into a temp file and rename() into place (atomic), or take a lockfile around the DDL, and/or verify the schema (schema_meta present) rather than just non-zero size.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: One sub-case is self-healing and worth noting: an interrupt after connect but before the first CREATE TABLE commits leaves a zero-byte file, which fails the -s check and is re-bootstrapped cleanly; only an interrupt after at least one statement has committed produces the permanently broken file. The permanence of the broken state is specifically caused by AutoCommit=1 per-statement commits (wrapping the DDL in one transaction would also fix the interrupt case for SQLite, though not the concurrent-first-open race).
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Confirmed not refuted — genuinely reachable via DB/Logger.pm:136 (live -L path) and db/sync.pm and import.pm, all going through build_connection -> ensure_sqlite_db. Downgrading from the original P3 to P2 (not upgrading) is defensible either way — I lean P2 because the finding's own memory context ("persistent runner daemons", CI matrices sharing a results DB) is an explicit intended use case in this project's roadmap, making concurrent-first-open more than purely theoretical, while still requiring the non-default shared-path setup to occur at all. No existing TODO_TASKS.md ticket covers this specific race; cheap mitigation as the finding proposes: check for a schema marker (e.g. schema_meta row) rather than just non-zero file size, and/or bootstrap into a tempfile + atomic rename, or wrap the DDL in a flock/lockfile — any one of these closes both the interrupted-bootstrap and the concurrent-first-open cases cheaply.

confirmedFindings.title: require_db_modules swallows the real load error: a broken installed module is misreported as 'not installed'
confirmedFindings.evidence: Both 'eval { require DBIx::QuickORM; 1 }' and 'eval { require $dbd_file; 1 }' discard $@ and unconditionally croak an 'is required ... but is not installed / cpanm ...' message.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: DBIx::QuickORM is installed but fails to compile (version conflict, broken dep, syntax error in a dev checkout): the user is told to 'cpanm DBIx::QuickORM DBD::SQLite', reinstalls repeatedly, and never sees the actual compile error that explains the failure.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Capture $@; if it is not a Can't-locate-for-that-module error, re-throw or append it to the croak message.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Proposal refinement: when filtering $@, match specifically /^Can't locate DBIx\/QuickORM\.pm/ (resp. the DBD's own .pm path) — a Can't-locate error for a *dependency* of the module is a compile failure the user needs to see, not a missing-module case to replace with the cpanm hint. Simplest robust fix: always append the captured $@ to the croak message.

confirmedFindings.title: client-recent --max is parsed but never sent to the server — the option silently does nothing
confirmedFindings.evidence: $count = $recent->max || 10 (line 56) is passed through get_data into get_from_http, which builds the URL as '$url/recent/$project/$user' with no count parameter and never references $count. (The legacy command only used $count on its DB path, which was removed when this became HTTP-only, leaving the option fully dead.)
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: `yath client-recent --project foo --max 50` returns the server's default number of runs (e.g. 10) with no error or warning; the user believes they are seeing the last 50 runs.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Append the count to the request (e.g. ?count=$count or a path segment the server supports), or drop/reject the option for this command.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Fix is simpler than the proposal suggests: the server already routes /recent/:project/:user/:count (Controller::Recent defaults count to 10), so the client can just append "/$count" to the URL at lib/App/Yath2/Command/client/recent.pm:119. Note the count-less HTTP URL was inherited verbatim from the legacy get_from_http; the removal of the DB path merely exposed it as the only path.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Not a hang/crash/data-loss issue and not silently corrupting results — it's a UX/correctness papercut: the user gets a wrong (server-default) count with zero error/warning, so they can be misled into thinking they saw N recent runs when they saw the server default (typically 10). Bumping from P3 to P2 rather than P1 because: (a) it degrades gracefully to a sane default rather than failing destructively, (b) the impact is limited to a read-only reporting/listing command, not test execution/CI gating, and (c) a user who cares about the actual full history will typically notice the row count mismatch. Cheap fix: either append the count as a query string (e.g. `.../recent/$project/$user?count=$count`) if the server route supports it, or reject/no-op the --max option explicitly with a warning if the server API has no count param. No corresponding TODO_TASKS.md entry found for this specific command.

confirmedFindings.title: client-publish success path crashes on a non-JSON 200 response and can print a broken view URL
confirmedFindings.evidence: On $res->is_success the body is fed straight to decode_json with no eval, and $data->{run_uuid} is interpolated unchecked into 'View run at: $url/view/$data->{run_uuid}'.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: A proxy/load-balancer or the server returns a 200 HTML or plain-text body (auth redirect page, maintenance page): the command dies with a raw JSON-parse stack trace instead of a message, after the upload may have actually succeeded. If the JSON lacks run_uuid, the command prints 'View run at: https://host/view/' plus an uninitialized-value warning.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Wrap the decode in the standard eval pattern and fall back to printing the raw body / a clear error; only print the view URL when run_uuid is present.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Two small corrections: (1) the die message from decode_json embeds the raw response body between ======= markers, so the user does see the body — it is still an uncaught longmess die rather than a clean error/exit-1, but not a body-less stack trace; (2) the bug is slightly worse than stated: because the JSON codec has allow_nonref(1), a 200 body that is valid JSON but a non-ref scalar (e.g. a bare number) decodes fine and then line 73 dies with a strict-refs 'not a HASH reference' error.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Agrees with audit's own P3 rating. Cheap fix (matches proposal and the repo's own documented eval pattern, feedback_eval_pattern.md: 'always use my $ok = eval { ...; 1 }; my $err = $@;'): wrap decode_json in eval, print raw body + status_line on failure, and only emit the 'View run at' line when $data->{run_uuid} is defined (else print a warning that upload may have succeeded but run_uuid was not returned). No related TODO_TASKS.md entry found for this specific command. Low priority - client-publish is a standalone CLI subcommand for pushing logs to a web server, not part of the core test-run/CI hot path, so worth a quick fix but not urgent.

confirmedFindings.title: Retry declined by a halted run is still reported as 'retried': _collector_retry_if_tries cannot see State::_retry_task's silent no-op, so the job is announced 'retry' but never re-queued
confirmedFindings.evidence: State::_retry_task does `$self->_stop_task($job_id); return if $self->{+HALTED_RUNS}->{$task->{run_id}};` - on a halted run it releases the task and returns WITHOUT queueing the retry, still returning normally. Handlers::_collector_retry_if_tries only checks `eval { $self->state->retry_task($job_id); 1 }`, which succeeds, so it returns 1 ('retried'): the runner announces harness_runner_job state 'retry' and never announces 'done', and no new attempt ever exists.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: Run with --retry=1; test A bails out (run halted); sibling test B finishes failing (final_state fail, try 1 <= budget 1) just after the halt. Its EOF takes the retry branch, retry_task silently declines (halted), yet the runner announces 'retry'. B is never re-run and never announced done/aborted; the command-side driver leaves B's verdict unsettled (note_verdict marks will_retry), so the summary lists B under 'The following jobs never ran' instead of under the failed jobs - the user is told a test that ran and failed never ran.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Make State::retry_task return a truthy/falsy 'actually retried' indicator (or throw on a halted run) and have _collector_retry_if_tries fall through to the fail/done path when the retry was declined.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: The headline scenario needs one qualifier: with the DEFAULT --abort-on-bail, collector_bail (Handlers.pm:563-585) synchronously marks every sibling collector entry terminated=1 (_terminate_collector line 633) in the same handler that calls halt_run, so a sibling's later failing EOF takes the terminated->aborted guard (Handlers.pm:412-415) and never reaches _collector_retry_if_tries. The live paths are: (a) --no-abort-on-bail (Options/Runner.pm:339) — halt_run with no sibling termination, sibling B finishes failing after the halt; (b) request_handler_halt_run (Handlers.pm:799-804), the command-caught-signal halt, which calls state->halt_run without terminating collectors, racing a job's failing EOF. Proposal is sound; note the fix must also skip setting collector_current_try (Handlers.pm:506) when the retry was declined.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Bumping from the audit's self-assigned P3 to P1: this is user-visible wrong behavior on a plausible normal-use path (--retry combined with a bail-out/halt in a multi-job run), not merely a theoretical/latent issue. Concrete user impact per the finding's failure_scenario: the summary reports a test that actually ran and failed as "never ran" instead of under failed jobs, and the job's state entry is left dangling (RUNNING with no closing transition) rather than cleanly finished — this can also affect exit-code/summary accuracy and, in a persistent runner daemon, leave a stale RUNNING task-lookup entry for the run. Not a hang/spin (no P0) since the process itself terminates the run/report cycle; but the misreport is a concrete, not-hard-to-hit correctness bug. Cheap mitigation matches the finding's own proposal: have State::retry_task/_retry_task return a truthy 'actually queued' flag (or die) on decline, and have _collector_retry_if_tries treat a falsy return as decline, falling through to the existing _collector_stop + announce_job('done') path. No existing TODO_TASKS.md ticket found referencing this specific halted-run/retry interaction; the general retry-flow work is discussed in TODO_TASKS.md (~lines 570-599) but doesn't call out this particular silent-decline gap.

confirmedFindings.title: Preload-root handshake wait loop has no connection-liveness check: a dropped runner connection blocks _request_sync for the full preload_map_timeout
confirmedFindings.evidence: _request_sync loops `until (exists $self->{+RESPONSES}{$request_id}) { croak ... if time > $deadline; $self->service_io; sleep 0.01; }` with the deadline = preload_map_timeout (default 30s, user-tunable much higher). Once the runner-side connection closes (service_io's drain sees EOF and _drop_conn's it), the response can never arrive, but the loop has no `$conn->closed` check and keeps polling a dead peer until the deadline.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: The runner drops the preload-root's connection while the runner process itself stays alive (e.g. the connection is evicted after 3 bad frames, or the runner is mid-teardown and closed connections without exiting). With --preload-map-timeout=600 the preload-root sits in this loop for 10 minutes doing 0.01s polls before croaking, instead of failing the handshake the instant the channel died; the runner meanwhile waits out its own preload-ready deadline, so the user's `yath test` start stalls for the whole window.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Inside the until-loop, croak immediately when `$conn->closed` (re-fetch via service_peer_conn('runner')) - the response can never arrive on a closed connection.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Cited line range is wrong: _request_sync is at lib/Test2/Harness2/Preload.pm:334-358 (wait loop at 350-355), not 236-260. Also this is not a busy-spin — the loop sleeps 0.01s per iteration — it is a bounded stall of up to preload_map_timeout, matching the finding's 'hang' kind. Fix detail: re-fetching via service_peer_conn('runner') is unnecessary; the already-held $conn is marked closed by drain on EOF, so `croak ... if $conn->closed` inside the loop suffices. Note the follow-on: after the timeout croak, run_driver's handshake eval catches it and the process falls into the post-run idle loop waiting for a 'stop' that can never arrive on the dropped connection (it then relies on the runner reaping it at wind-down), which slightly extends the practical impact beyond the timeout window.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Cheap fix as proposed: inside the until-loop, re-fetch the conn via service_peer_conn($identity) and croak immediately if $conn->closed (Role::Service already exposes ->closed and this exact check pattern appears elsewhere in Role/Service.pm, e.g. line 353). Low-risk, small diff — worth doing opportunistically even at P3 since the fix is a 2-line addition to an already-open loop, but not worth a standalone task/ticket at this severity.

confirmedFindings.title: Stage host watches the spawn intermediate whose process group contains the long-lived detached spawn supervisor -- stage stop/reload kill()s the 'detached' `yath spawn` session
files: lib/Test2/Harness2/Runner/JobLauncher.pm:116-196 (launch_spawn: supervisor never leaves the intermediate's pgroup)
confirmedFindings.evidence: request_handler_spawn forks an intermediate, `$self->watch_pid($intermediate)` (Host.pm line 339). The intermediate setsid()s (pgid = its own pid) and forks the SUPERVISOR, then exits. Unlike the test-job double-fork (where the collector setsids AGAIN and leaves the intermediate's group, JobLauncher line ~307), launch_spawn's supervisor never calls setsid/setpgrp -- only the script CHILD setsids (JobLauncher line 153). So the long-lived supervisor stays in the intermediate's process group for the whole spawned session. Consequences in the watching stage: (a) IPC::_check_if_dead_yet keeps the reaped intermediate in WAITING while `kill(0, -$pid)` is true, so the intermediate never leaves {+PROCS}; (b) at stage wind-down run_stage does `$self->killall($self->{+SIGNAL})` (Host.pm line 715) which under USE_P_GROUPS sends the signal to `-$pid` for every procs key -- i.e. straight at the detached supervisor; Host::stop() escalates with killall('KILL') (line 454).
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: User opens an interactive session with `yath spawn script.pl` (supervisor alive, session in use), then the runner shuts down or `yath reload` fires. The stage's service_stopped/HUP path sets SIGNAL and killall() TERMs (then KILLs) the intermediate's process group, killing the spawn SUPERVISOR that per ARCHITECTURE §4.8 must survive runner/stage teardown. The supervisor dies without sending exit_status; its control-EOF duty ('kill the child pgroup when the command dies') is also lost, so the script child (own session, holding the user's real terminal fds) is orphaned while the `yath spawn` command exits 0 (see separate finding). Additionally the stuck WAITING entry means every stage stop() waits the full 5s timeout while a spawn is open.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Have the spawn supervisor setpgrp(0,0) (or setsid) immediately after the fork from the intermediate, mirroring the collector's second setsid in launch_via_double_fork, so the intermediate's group empties as soon as it exits; and/or do not watch_pid the spawn intermediate with the group-liveness gate (reap it with a plain waitpid).
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: One secondary claim is overstated: "every stage stop() waits the full 5s timeout while a spawn is open" — stop() issues killall(TERM) before wait(all=>1, timeout=>5), and if that TERM kills the supervisor the pgroup empties and the stuck WAITING entry clears well before 5s. The full 5s wait occurs only if the supervisor survives TERM (e.g. its inherited die-based handler is caught by an eval in its preserved service-loop stack). The primary defect and the proposed fix (supervisor setpgrp/setsid after fork, mirroring JobLauncher.pm:307; or reap the intermediate without the pgroup-liveness gate) stand as written.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Confirmed severity P1 as originally assigned (not escalating to P0 since it needs an open spawn session coinciding with stop/reload, and doesn't affect the primary test-run path; not downgrading since both triggers -- normal shutdown and `yath reload` -- are ordinary operations with no unusual timing needed). No existing TODO_TASKS.md ticket specifically covers this process-group leak; TODO_TASKS.md's TIER 5 spawn section covers the broader spawn/interactive design but doesn't call out this setsid gap. Cheap mitigation matching the finding's own proposal: have the supervisor call POSIX::setpgrp(0,0) (or setsid()) immediately after the fork() in launch_spawn's supervisor branch (mirroring the script child's existing setsid call just a few lines below), so it leaves the intermediate's group before the intermediate exits/gets reaped; that alone fixes both the killall-hits-supervisor issue and the _check_if_dead_yet WAITING-stall issue, since both stem from the same unclosed pgroup membership. Also worth cross-referencing the "separate finding" this evidence mentions about `yath spawn` exiting 0 despite an orphaned child -- likely another finding in the same audit that should be resolved together.

confirmedFindings.title: Render Driver accumulates one open events-file fd per test job for the whole run (TAIL_READERS never pruned, JobReader keeps its zstd handle after DONE)
files: lib/Test2/Harness2/Renderer/Driver.pm:499 (reader created and cached), 109 (hash lives for the run)
confirmedFindings.evidence: Driver::_tail_reader caches `$self->{+TAIL_READERS}{$uuid} //= Test2::Harness2::JobReader->new(...)` per collector uuid and nothing ever deletes an entry -- when a job ends, only `$entry->{ended} = 1` is set in BY_UUID. JobReader::poll marks `$self->{+DONE}` on harness_final_state but keeps `$self->{+READER}` (the open zstd filehandle from open_zstd_reader) alive; done readers short-circuit poll but hold their fd. The yath test/run command process therefore keeps one open fd per completed test file until the command exits.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: A suite with more test files than the fd rlimit (e.g. 1500 .t files with the default `ulimit -n 1024`) run via `yath test`: as jobs finish, the command accumulates ~1 fd per job on top of its sockets; around job ~1000 open_zstd_reader/other opens start failing with EMFILE ('Too many open files') in the command process -- rendering breaks mid-run, later jobs' events are never displayed and the final rollup is wrong, even though the tests themselves ran fine in the runner.
confirmedFindings.proposal: When a reader reports done (harness_job_end seen / $entry->{ended} set), delete $self->{+TAIL_READERS}{$uuid} (and/or have JobReader close and drop +READER when it sets +DONE).
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: The leak is confined to live-tail mode: _tail_reader/TAIL_READERS are only reached via tail()/_finalize_live(), gated on the `live` attribute wired from the --live display option (App/Yath2/Command/test.pm:383-396). The default `yath test` path uses Renderer::Base::feed_events_file, which creates the JobReader as a call-scoped lexical whose fd is closed by Zstd::Reader::DESTROY when the call returns, so it does not leak. The failure scenario should therefore read "yath test --live with more test files than the fd rlimit"; without --live the scenario cannot execute. Also note readers are keyed per collector uuid, so retries add one fd per try, not per file.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Confirms author's own P2 rating. Trigger is real and not dead code, but needs unusually large job counts (order of 1000+) relative to the process's fd ulimit to become user-visible as EMFILE mid-run — not a common-path hang/deadlock (no P0/P1). Cheap fix as proposed: in Driver::_tail_reader, when $entry->{ended} is set (harness_job_end seen), also `delete $self->{+TAIL_READERS}{$uuid}` (JobReader falls out of scope, releasing its filehandle via GC); alternatively have JobReader explicitly `close` and clear +READER when it sets +DONE, for a hygiene fix that doesn't depend on the wrapping hash being pruned. No related TODO_TASKS.md entry found for this; would need to be filed if accepted.

confirmedFindings.title: Unguarded request-handler dispatch: one malformed or duplicate request frame kills the runner daemon
confirmedFindings.evidence: Role::Service::_handle_events calls `my $resp = $self->handle_request($event->{payload}, $conn);` with no eval guard, and handle_request dispatches straight into request_handler_* methods. Several handlers pass network payload fields directly into State methods that die on bad input: request_handler_queue_run does `my $run = $payload->{run}` then State::_queue_run does `%$run` (dies 'Can't use an undefined value as a HASH reference' when the run key is absent); request_handler_queue_task -> State::_queue_task dies 'Task missing job_id' / 'Task missing run_id' / 'Task already in queue'; request_handler_run_task on the ROOT runner calls $self->state->enqueue_task, a method Runner::State does not have (only StageDelegate does) -> 'Can't locate object method' die. The die propagates through service_io -> run_scheduler_only and is only caught by the eval in Runner::process (line 474), which warns and winds the WHOLE runner down (stop_preload_root, stop, close_service).
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: A persistent runner (`yath start`) is serving runs for several terminals. Any client that connects to runner.socket and sends a `queue_run` request without a `run` key, a `queue_task` for a job_id already queued (e.g. a buggy or retried submitter), or a misdirected `run_task` frame, makes the corresponding State call die; nothing catches it until Runner::process's outer eval, so the daemon tears down every stage and exits — every in-flight run from every user is aborted by one bad frame. On the transient path the same frame kills the run mid-flight with an internal stack trace instead of an error reply.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Wrap the handle_request dispatch in _handle_events in the mandated `my $ok = eval { ...; 1 }; my $err = $@;` pattern and, on failure, reply `{ok => 0, error => $err}` (and/or _bad_frame the connection) instead of letting the die unwind the service loop. Additionally validate payload shape (run/task hashref present) in request_handler_queue_run/queue_task before touching State.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Two small precision notes: (1) when the preload-root is not yet ready, submit_action buffers the submission and the die fires later in flush_submit_buffer (Runner.pm:897-908) rather than at receipt -- still inside the same outer eval, identical outcome; (2) request_handler_run_task exists in two copies -- Handlers.pm:811 (composed into Runner, where it dies) and Preload/Host.pm:274 (stage side, where state is StageDelegate and it works) -- the finding's claim applies to the Runner copy only. Triggering requires a buggy/misdirected local client (correct yath clients never send these shapes; the unix socket is per-user), so exposure is robustness against bad peers, not a normal-operation crash; P1 is justified for the persistent multi-user-run daemon case, P2 if the transient path were the only consumer.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Confirmed at P1 as filed. Real-world trigger doesn't require an attacker: a retried/duplicate `queue_task` submission (e.g., a client retry after a timed-out ack) or a `queue_run` frame missing its `run` payload (protocol/version mismatch between client and runner) is plausible under normal operation of a persistent `yath start` daemon serving multiple terminals/CI jobs, and instantly aborts every other in-flight run on that daemon with an internal stack trace instead of a clean error reply. Cheap mitigation matches the proposal exactly: wrap the `handle_request` call in Role::Service::_handle_events (Service.pm ~382) in the mandated `my $ok = eval { ...; 1 }; my $err = $@;` pattern and send back an error response instead of letting the die propagate to Runner::process's outer eval; additionally validate `payload->{run}`/`payload->{task}` shape in the two request_handler_* entry points before touching State. No existing TODO_TASKS.md ticket covers this specific gap, so it should be filed/fixed on its own rather than assumed to ride along with #1685 (dead-code/forwarder cleanup) which touches the same State.pm lines for an unrelated reason.

confirmedFindings.title: DB logger: a die inside _run skips _finalize_run_row, leaving the runs row status='running' forever
confirmedFindings.evidence: run() does `my $ok = eval { $self->_run; 1 }; ... unless ($ok) { $self->_terminal_error(...) }` and returns — _finalize_run_row is only called at the END of _run (line 221). The workdir-vanished terminal path (inside the loop) reaches _finalize_run_row and correctly marks the run 'broken', but any die out of _sync/_import (a transient DB error, a QuickORM constraint failure, a decode error in the snapshot fold) bypasses it entirely: the row seeded with status => 'running' is never updated.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: During a `yath test -LDB...` run, one insert fails (e.g. the DB connection drops mid-run, or a constraint violation from an unexpected payload). _sync dies, run() records the terminal error only to stderr/its exit code, and the runs row in the database is left permanently status='running' with zero counters — the web UI / queries show a run that never finishes, indistinguishable from a live run, with no 'broken' marker even though the logger knew it aborted.
confirmedFindings.proposal: In run()'s failure branch, after _terminal_error, call `eval { $self->_finalize_run_row; 1 }` so the row is stamped status='broken' whenever the run row was seeded.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Impact is slightly understated: DB/Sync.pm line 177 only syncs runs whose status is 'complete'/'broken'/'canceled', so the stuck 'running' run is also permanently excluded from `db sync` propagation to other targets, not just misrendered in the UI. The proposal is correct as written; note _finalize_run_row's `return unless RUN_ROW_SEEDED` guard already makes it safe for dies that occur before the run row is seeded (e.g., connection-build failure), and the eval wrap is needed because the finalize write itself may fail for the same reason the run died (dead DB connection).
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Upgrading from the audit's original P3 to P2: this is not latent/theoretical dead code (I traced it live in Logger.pm on 2.0d and the -LDB logger mode is a supported feature), but it does need an unusual triggering condition (a genuine DB/decode error mid-sync), not just normal test-run traffic, which keeps it out of P1. No existing TODO_TASKS.md ticket covers this gap. Cheap fix matching the proposal: wrap the failure branch in run() with `eval { $self->_finalize_run_row } if $self->{+RUN_ROW_SEEDED}` (guard already exists inside _finalize_run_row itself, so simply calling it unconditionally from run()'s `unless ($ok)` branch after _terminal_error is sufficient and low-risk).

confirmedFindings.title: Verbose mode tags every first job launch 'RETRY' instead of 'LAUNCH': 1-based try ordinal used directly as the boolean retry flag
confirmedFindings.evidence: Driver::_render_launch emits `harness_job_launch => {stamp => $stamp, retry => $try}` (line 336) where $try comes from the collector's try ordinal, which is 1-BASED since R10/#49 (Runner/Job.pm line 429: `is_try //= task->{is_try} // 1`; State.pm comment "the first attempt is is_try == 1"). Renderer::Formatter line 116: `tag => $f->{harness_job_launch}->{retry} ? 'RETRY' : 'LAUNCH'` — 1 is truthy. VERIFIED LIVE: `yath test -v` on a fresh single passing test prints `(  RETRY )  job  1  .../pass.t` as its first line.
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: Any `yath test -v` (or --show-job-launch) run labels every job's FIRST attempt with the RETRY tag; the LAUNCH tag is never shown. Users conclude every test is being retried / something failed earlier. Real retries are indistinguishable from first runs.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Emit a 0/1 retry flag: in Driver's launch events use `retry => ($try // 1) > 1 ? 1 : 0` (both _render_launch and _render_aborted), keeping the raw ordinal in a separate field if needed.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Cited line Driver.pm:382 (_render_aborted) does not show the RETRY-on-first-launch symptom: that path hard-codes $try = 0 (line 356), so it always tags LAUNCH — its defect is the inverse (an aborted job that was a retry is never tagged RETRY, and its harness_job/harness_job_launch report is_try/retry 0 even for retries). The proposal is still right to fix both sites, but the aborted path also needs the real try ordinal (e.g. from $job or the task) rather than a normalized constant.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Impact is purely cosmetic/UX: it mislabels output but does not change exit codes, pass/fail results, job counts, or leave orphans — a P1 upgrade isn't warranted since the rubric ties P1 to wrong exit code/results/orphans, none of which occur here. However, because it is 100%-reproducible on the common `-v` path (not gated behind unusual conditions), it sits at the top of P2 rather than drifting to P3: users watching verbose/CI logs will see every single test tagged RETRY and reasonably conclude flakiness/instability is present when it isn't, which can mask real retries (since RETRY is shown for both first attempts and actual retries, real retries become indistinguishable — this compounds the confusion beyond a single mislabel). Cheap fix as proposed: normalize to a boolean before emitting (`retry => ($try // 1) > 1 ? 1 : 0`) in both _render_launch and _render_aborted (Driver.pm:336 and 382), keeping raw ordinal separately if still needed downstream. No existing TODO_TASKS.md entry found for this specific bug; recommend filing since it's a trivial, low-risk one-line-per-site fix.

confirmedFindings.title: speedtag does not recognize the supported HARNESS-DUR-* alias, so it prepends a duplicate directive that the parser then IGNORES (stale tag wins)
confirmedFindings.evidence: Line 147 regex: `HARNESS-(CAT(EGORY)?|DUR(ATION))-(LONG|MEDIUM|SHORT)` — `DUR(ATION)` only matches the full word DURATION (missing the `?`), yet the harness's directive parser explicitly accepts the short alias (`Util/Directives/Legacy.pm:227: elsif ($dir eq 'duration' || $dir eq 'dur')`). When no line matches, speedtag prepends a new `# HARNESS-DURATION-X` header (the `unless ($injected)` branch), and Legacy::_set is last-wins, so the pre-existing later `# HARNESS-DUR-Y` line silently overrides the new tag. Bonus: line 101's validation message for MAX_MEDIUM reads "max short duration must be an integer" (copy-paste of line 100).
confirmedFindings.failure_scenario: A project tags tests with `# HARNESS-DUR-LONG`. Running `yath speedtag log.jsonl` prints 'Tagged short: ...' for a now-fast test and rewrites the file — but the new HARNESS-DURATION-SHORT line is prepended above the untouched HARNESS-DUR-LONG line, which wins at parse time: the scheduler still treats the test as long. Repeated speedtag runs keep stacking duplicate directive lines. Separately, `yath speedtag log 15 abc` dies with 'max SHORT duration must be an integer, got abc' although the medium value is at fault.
confirmedFindings.proposal: Make the regex `DUR(ATION)?`, and fix the second die message to say 'max medium duration'.
confirmedFindings.accuracy_note: Two corrections to the scenario: (1) There is no stacking on repeated runs — after the first run the file contains a HARNESS-DURATION-* line that DOES match the regex, so later runs update it in place and `next if $injected++` even removes extra matching lines; exactly one stale/new pair persists. (2) The new line is inserted after the leading header block (lines matching `^(#|use\s|package\s)`), not at the very top; if the stale HARNESS-DUR line is contiguous with the top-of-file header (unindented, no blank line before it) it is swept into @header ahead of the new line and the NEW tag wins (last-wins), so the failure only manifests when the DUR line follows a blank line or is indented. Proposal (`DUR(ATION)?` plus fixing the line-101 message to say 'max medium duration') is correct as written.
confirmedFindings.severity_note: Cheap fix confirmed sufficient: change regex to `DUR(ATION)?` (adding the `?`) so speedtag's line-matching stays in sync with what Legacy.pm's parser already accepts, plus fix the MAX_MEDIUM die message to say "medium" instead of copy-pasted "short" — both are one-line changes with no architectural risk. No existing TODO_TASKS.md entry targets this specific alias mismatch; TODO_TASKS.md:1984 only tracks a refactor to extract speedtag's read/inject/write logic into named subs with test coverage, which would be a natural place to add a regression test for the DUR alias while touching that code.
